papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary objective is to create compact models that retain high performance, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. The process involves training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, often by learning from its output distributions or internal feature representations. While initially conceived for creating smaller and faster models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. The framework is now used to enhance student model performance, improve interpretability, and address considerations like data privacy and algorithmic fairness, establishing it as a multifaceted tool in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Paradigm for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Originally conceived as a method for a smaller "student" model to learn from a larger "teacher" model, the paradigm has evolved significantly. Research now shows that the benefits of distillation extend beyond simple mimicry, with the regularization effects of soft labels playing a crucial role. This technique has proven effective in a wide array of complex domains, including natural language processing for text generation and translation, the compression of generative adversarial networks, and the optimization of graph neural networks. Advanced methods such as self-distillation, adversarial training, and extensions for domain adaptation further highlight its versatility. Ultimately, knowledge distillation is a critical tool for creating efficient, yet powerful, AI systems suitable for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Shields
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The primary objective is to create compact models that can be deployed on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones, without a substantial loss in performance. This is achieved by training the student model to mimic the outputs or internal feature representations of the teacher. This versatile framework has been widely applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, not only for creating smaller and faster models but also for enhancing model robustness and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Transferring Inductive Biases through Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Having the right inductive biases can be crucial in many tasks or scenarios where data or computing resources are a limiting factor, or where training data is not perfectly representative of the conditions at test time. However, defining, designing and efficiently adapting inductive biases is not necessarily straightforward. In this paper, we explore the power of knowledge distillation for transferring the effect of inductive biases from one model to another. We consider families of models with different inductive biases, LSTMs vs. Transformers and CNNs vs. MLPs, in the context of tasks and scenarios where having the right inductive biases is critical. We study the effect of inductive biases on the solutions the models converge to and investigate how and to what extent the effect of inductive biases is transferred through knowledge distillation, in terms of not only performance but also different aspects of converged solutions.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, the 'student'. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by significantly reducing their size and computational footprint while retaining high performance. The core idea involves training the student model to replicate the teacher's output probabilities, which contain richer information than simple class labels. Advanced methods also involve distilling knowledge from the teacher's intermediate feature representations, using multiple teachers, or even operating without access to the original training data. Knowledge distillation has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing, speech recognition, computer vision, and for improving model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Compressing Deep Learning Models for Enhanced Efficiency
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning and natural language processing. It facilitates the creation of compact, efficient 'student' models by transferring knowledge from larger, more complex 'teacher' models. This process allows for the deployment of powerful neural networks on devices with limited computational and storage resources, such as mobile phones. Various distillation strategies have been developed, including methods that function without access to the original training data, thereby addressing privacy and data availability concerns. By mimicking the outputs or intermediate representations of a teacher model, the student network can achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller footprint, making it a versatile tool for optimizing deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of compact, efficient models suitable for real-world deployment. The process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to create models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a substantial loss in performance. By transferring the rich, nuanced information captured by the teacher, the student model can achieve high accuracy. The utility of knowledge distillation extends beyond simple compression, serving as a powerful framework for enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and transferring complex capabilities across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Molina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance but their large size often prevents deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique to address this issue. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller computational footprint. Beyond compression, this versatile framework can also enhance model performance and generalization. Its applications are widespread across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it a crucial tool for creating practical and deployable artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective and Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression in deep learning. This process addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments by training a smaller 'student' model to mimic a larger 'teacher' model. This transfer of knowledge allows the compact student model to achieve high performance with a fraction of the computational and memory requirements. The versatility of this framework has led to its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it a foundational tool for developing efficient and practical artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models have achieved unprecedented performance but their immense size and computational cost often hinder practical deployment. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression framework to address this challenge. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer resources. This makes it possible to deploy state-of-the-art models on devices with limited computational power, such as mobile phones. The technique's versatility is demonstrated by its broad application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its adaptation into advanced methods like self-distillation and data-free distillation, further expanding its utility in developing efficient and robust AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Hamilton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a critical technique for model compression in deep learning, addressing the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models on resource-constrained devices. This method operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student can achieve comparable accuracy with a significantly smaller footprint and faster inference times. The versatility of this approach is demonstrated by its successful application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and through the development of advanced methods like data-free and self-distillation, making it an essential tool for creating practical and efficient AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Owens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Paradigm for Efficient and Adaptable Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This process, where a compact "student" model learns from a larger "teacher" model, is crucial for deploying state-of-the-art neural networks on resource-constrained devices. Beyond simple compression, distillation has evolved into a versatile framework for transferring knowledge in a variety of challenging contexts. It enables training without access to original data, facilitates collaborative learning across heterogeneous devices in federated settings, and improves model generalization and adaptation to new domains. This demonstrates that knowledge distillation is not merely a compression tool but a fundamental paradigm for making advanced artificial intelligence more practical, private, and widely applicable.

papers_seen.author: Snyder
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of compact, efficient models from larger, more complex ones. Operating on a teacher-student paradigm, this method transfers learned knowledge, allowing smaller student models to achieve high performance while being suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. The utility of knowledge distillation extends beyond simple size reduction, with applications in enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling privacy-preserving learning. Its versatility across domains like natural language processing and computer vision has established it as a foundational tool for developing practical and accessible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Murray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models from larger, computationally expensive ones. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and knowledge of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to enable the deployment of powerful neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile or edge devices, without a significant loss in performance. By transferring the rich information embedded in the teacher's predictions or internal representations, the student model can achieve high accuracy. The applications of this versatile framework extend beyond simple compression to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling advanced learning paradigms.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm designed to create smaller, more efficient deep learning models without a significant loss in performance. The technique involves training a compact "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich, generalized knowledge learned by the teacher, typically through its output probabilities or internal feature representations, the student model can be deployed on resource-constrained devices. This framework has seen wide application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and has been extended to more advanced use cases such as performance enhancement and data-private learning scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Show, Attend and Distill:Knowledge Distillation via Attention-based Feature Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation extracts general knowledge from a pre-trained teacher network and provides guidance to a target student network. Most studies manually tie intermediate features of the teacher and student, and transfer knowledge through pre-defined links. However, manual selection often constructs ineffective links that limit the improvement from the distillation. There has been an attempt to address the problem, but it is still challenging to identify effective links under practical scenarios. In this paper, we introduce an effective and efficient feature distillation method utilizing all the feature levels of the teacher without manually selecting the links. Specifically, our method utilizes an attention-based meta-network that learns relative similarities between features, and applies identified similarities to control distillation intensities of all possible pairs. As a result, our method determines competent links more efficiently than the previous approach and provides better performance on model compression and transfer learning tasks. Further qualitative analyses and ablative studies describe how our method contributes to better distillation. The implementation code is available at github.com/clovaai/attention-feature-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of compact, efficient models from larger, more complex ones. Operating on a teacher-student paradigm, this process involves training a smaller student model to replicate the behavior of a pre-trained teacher network. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art models, enabling their deployment on resource-constrained devices like mobile phones. The transfer of knowledge is achieved by mimicking the teacher's outputs or its internal feature representations. This versatile framework has demonstrated success across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and has evolved to address challenges such as data privacy and performance enhancement.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful paradigm in deep learning, primarily known as a model compression technique. It facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient 'student' models by transferring knowledge from larger, pre-trained 'teacher' models. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. However, the applications of this framework extend far beyond simple compression. Knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile tool for enhancing model performance, ensuring data privacy, and mitigating algorithmic and gender biases. Its adaptability across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, highlights its critical role in developing practical, robust, and responsible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models. The process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact "student" model is trained to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This enables the deployment of complex neural networks on devices with limited computational resources. Knowledge is typically transferred by training the student on the teacher's output probabilities or its internal feature representations. While its primary use is model compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness against adversarial attacks, and transferring knowledge in data-scarce or privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Tran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale deep learning models present significant deployment challenges due to their computational and memory demands. Knowledge distillation offers a solution by transferring knowledge from a large "teacher" model to a smaller "student" model. This process trains the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, creating a compact and efficient model that retains high performance. This versatile framework enables the practical application of advanced models in resource-constrained environments across various domains like natural language processing and computer vision, and its utility extends beyond compression to areas like domain adaptation and performance enhancement.

This process enables the deployment of high-performing models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices or systems with limited computational power. While primarily aimed at reducing model size and inference latency, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used to enhance model performance across various tasks, improve interpretability, and facilitate knowledge transfer between different model architectures and data modalities. The versatility of this framework has made it a cornerstone in developing practical, efficient, and robust artificial intelligence systems.

This approach has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to compress massive models like BERT, improve performance on tasks such as machine translation and object detection, and enable the creation of highly accurate yet lightweight neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Anderson

This approach involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, including its predictions on unlabeled data, the student model can achieve comparable performance to its larger counterpart while being significantly smaller and faster. This technique has proven effective across a wide range of applications, from compressing large language models to enabling efficient object detection and transferring knowledge across different data modalities, making it a critical tool for creating practical, real-world artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Bernard

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, called the 'student'. This process enables the creation of compact neural networks that are suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. The core idea is to train the student model to mimic the output distribution of the teacher model, leveraging the rich, learned information contained in the teacher's predictions. Variations of this technique include using multiple teachers, distilling knowledge from intermediate feature layers, and even training teacher models to be more 'student-friendly'. Knowledge distillation has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, as well as in specialized paradigms like federated learning to preserve privacy and improve communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

The primary goal is to transfer the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, including nuanced relationships between classes, to the student, enabling it to achieve comparable or even superior performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing and computer vision, facilitating the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices and in specialized environments like federated learning. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation also serves as a potent regularization technique and a method for enhancing model performance and enabling novel cross-modal knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a highly effective and versatile framework for model compression in deep learning. This technique addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller footprint and faster inference speed. The applications of this method extend beyond simple compression, serving to enhance model performance, improve generalization, and enable new learning paradigms across domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, called the 'student'. This process enables the creation of compact neural networks that are suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. The core idea is to train the student model to mimic the output distribution of the teacher model, leveraging the rich, learned information contained in the teacher's predictions. Variations of this technique include using multiple teachers, distilling knowledge from intermediate feature layers, and even training teacher models to be more 'student-friendly'. Knowledge distillation has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, as well as in specialized paradigms like federated learning to preserve privacy and improve communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Kelley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments. The process involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich, learned knowledge from the teacher, the student model can achieve high performance while maintaining a significantly smaller footprint. This makes it possible to utilize state-of-the-art architectures in practical applications, such as on mobile devices. The technique has proven to be highly adaptable, with wide-ranging applications across natural language processing, computer vision, and beyond, extending its utility from simple compression to enhancing overall model performance and robustness.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile and Effective Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models often have immense computational requirements, limiting their use in practical applications. Knowledge distillation offers a powerful solution for model compression. This technique involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process enables the creation of smaller, faster models that retain high performance, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. The versatility of this framework has led to its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, bridging the gap between state-of-the-art performance and real-world deployability.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique in deep learning, primarily for model compression. This process involves training a smaller, efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, including nuanced probability distributions and internal feature representations, the student can achieve comparable or even superior performance with significantly fewer computational resources. While its primary application is creating compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, the utility of knowledge distillation extends further. It has been successfully applied to enhance model robustness, improve algorithmic fairness, facilitate domain adaptation, and increase model interpretability, making it a highly versatile and powerful tool for developing practical and efficient deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile and Effective Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models from larger, complex ones. This process operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model learns to mimic the behavior of a pre-trained teacher model, thereby inheriting its rich, generalized knowledge. The primary goal is to enable the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures, such as large language models, on resource-constrained devices where computational power and memory are limited. While initially conceived for creating lightweight networks, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly, demonstrating its utility for enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and transferring knowledge in privacy-sensitive scenarios across domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions suitable for real-world deployment. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. While the primary goal is to reduce computational and memory requirements for resource-constrained environments, the applications of knowledge distillation extend far beyond simple model compression. The technique has proven to be a versatile framework for enhancing student model performance, improving generalization, adapting models to new domains, and enabling knowledge transfer in complex scenarios such as lifelong learning. This makes it a fundamental tool for creating more practical, robust, and efficient artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and powerful technique for model compression within the field of deep learning. This paradigm addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from a large 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The student is trained to mimic the behavior of the teacher, often by learning from its softened probability outputs or intermediate feature representations. This process allows the compact student model to achieve high performance, often comparable to its much larger teacher, without the associated computational and memory overhead. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it an essential tool for developing practical and deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to deploy high-performing models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their size and computational cost. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, extending from compressing large language models and generative adversarial networks to improving performance in tasks like neural machine translation, graph-based learning, and recommender systems. Variations of the technique leverage multiple teachers, adversarial samples, and feature-based mimicry to enhance the student model's capabilities, sometimes even allowing the student to surpass the performance of its teacher.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient neural networks without a significant loss in performance. This is achieved through a teacher-student framework, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the outputs and internal representations of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of complex models, enabling their deployment on resource-constrained devices such as mobile phones. This versatile method has been successfully applied across a wide array of domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its applications have expanded beyond simple compression to include performance enhancement and knowledge transfer in privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models suitable for resource-constrained environments. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, the student can achieve high performance that might otherwise be unattainable. While its primary application is in reducing model size and computational cost for deployment on devices like mobile phones, the framework has proven to be highly versatile. Its applications now extend beyond simple compression to include performance enhancement, knowledge transfer across different tasks and data modalities, and addressing fairness concerns in artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique for compressing large deep learning models. This method involves training a smaller, computationally efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to create compact models that retain high performance while being significantly faster and requiring fewer computational resources, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. However, the applications of this framework extend far beyond simple compression. It can be used to enhance model performance, transfer specific capabilities like adversarial robustness, and even operate in scenarios where the original training data is unavailable, making it a critical tool for the practical application of modern artificial intelligence.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: The Versatility of Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of state-of-the-art deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, have emerged as a powerful solution. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. Knowledge distillation has proven to be a highly versatile and effective method, extending far beyond simple model size reduction for classification tasks. Its applications span diverse domains such as natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning. The framework is adaptable, enabling knowledge transfer between models of different architectures, across different data modalities, and even in scenarios with limited or no access to the original training data. This demonstrates its crucial role in making advanced AI models more practical and accessible for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Rubio
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models from larger, complex ones. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact "student" model is trained to replicate the performance and behavior of a pre-trained "teacher" model. The primary objective is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art neural networks, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. This is typically achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs or internal feature representations. The applications of this versatile framework are broad, spanning domains like natural language processing and computer vision, and its utility extends beyond simple compression to performance enhancement and improved model generalization.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework Beyond Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning, widely recognized for its ability to compress large, complex models into smaller, more efficient "student" networks. However, its applications extend far beyond simple model compression. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is a versatile framework capable of not only creating efficient models but also enhancing their performance, enabling new functionalities, and addressing critical challenges such as fairness, privacy, and domain adaptation. By transferring knowledge from one or more "teacher" models, student models can achieve state-of-the-art results in diverse areas including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning. The evolution of distillation techniques, from mimicking output logits to advanced feature-mimicking and meta-learning approaches, further underscores its flexibility and growing importance in the development of robust and adaptable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a prominent technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. The process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This approach addresses the significant computational and memory challenges associated with deploying state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, student models can achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller footprint. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains and its adaptation to address challenges like data privacy and architectural mismatches, making advanced AI more accessible for real-world use.

papers_seen.author: Walters
