papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of compact, efficient models from larger, more complex ones. Operating on a teacher-student paradigm, this process involves training a smaller student model to replicate the behavior of a pre-trained teacher network. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art models, enabling their deployment on resource-constrained devices like mobile phones. The transfer of knowledge is achieved by mimicking the teacher's outputs or its internal feature representations. This versatile framework has demonstrated success across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and has evolved to address challenges such as data privacy and performance enhancement.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments. The method operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient "student" model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process transfers the rich knowledge from the teacher, enabling the creation of compact, fast models that retain high performance. While its primary use is to reduce model size, the framework's versatility extends to enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and transferring knowledge across different domains and architectures. Its successful application in fields like natural language processing and computer vision makes it a crucial tool for developing practical, real-world AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for model compression, enabling the creation of smaller, more efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger, cumbersome teacher models. This process allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has emerged as a versatile framework that can also enhance a model's generalization capabilities, improve its robustness against adversarial attacks, and increase its interpretability. By leveraging the rich information contained in a teacher's predictions, this technique offers a multifaceted approach to optimizing neural networks for a wide range of practical applications in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique in deep learning for model compression. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, enabling the creation of smaller, more efficient 'student' models by transferring knowledge from larger, more complex 'teacher' models. This process facilitates the deployment of powerful neural networks on devices with limited computational resources, such as mobile phones. While its primary goal is to reduce model size and latency, the applications of knowledge distillation extend further, serving as a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling advanced learning strategies in areas like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous domains, but their large size and computational expense often hinder deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and effective model compression technique to address this challenge. The process involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher's predictions or internal representations, the student can achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters. The utility of this framework has expanded beyond simple compression, proving effective for enhancing model performance, transferring specific capabilities like adversarial robustness, and even mitigating societal biases within language models. Advanced methods such as self-distillation, online distillation, and data-free approaches further increase its versatility, making it a critical tool for developing efficient and practical AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient and Practical Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks but their significant computational and memory requirements pose major challenges for real-world deployment. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, offer a powerful solution to this problem. Knowledge distillation is a training paradigm where a smaller "student" model learns to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process allows the student to inherit the teacher's learned knowledge, resulting in a compact, efficient model that retains high performance. This approach has proven highly effective and adaptable, enabling the creation of practical models for diverse applications in natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and distributed learning systems, thereby bridging the gap between cutting-edge research and deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Compressing Deep Learning Models for Enhanced Efficiency
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning and natural language processing. It facilitates the creation of compact, efficient 'student' models by transferring knowledge from larger, more complex 'teacher' models. This process allows for the deployment of powerful neural networks on devices with limited computational and storage resources, such as mobile phones. Various distillation strategies have been developed, including methods that function without access to the original training data, thereby addressing privacy and data availability concerns. By mimicking the outputs or intermediate representations of a teacher model, the student network can achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller footprint, making it a versatile tool for optimizing deep learning applications.

While initially developed for model compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly, now encompassing performance enhancement, improved model robustness, and knowledge transfer across different tasks and domains, making it a multifaceted tool for developing practical and powerful artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning, enabling the creation of smaller, more efficient models suitable for resource-constrained environments. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and internal representations of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. While its primary application is to reduce computational and memory requirements without significant performance degradation, the utility of knowledge distillation has expanded considerably. It is now used to enhance model performance, transfer knowledge across different data modalities, improve model interpretability, and adapt large-scale models for specific downstream tasks in domains like natural language processing and computer vision. This versatility makes knowledge distillation a foundational strategy for developing practical and effective artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression technique where a compact 'student' model learns to replicate the behavior of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has been shown to improve model performance, enhance interpretability, and facilitate knowledge transfer across different data modalities. However, the process is not without challenges, as student models can struggle with optimization and may inherit undesirable biases from their teachers. Ongoing research focuses on developing more effective distillation strategies, such as using multiple teachers, applying data augmentation, and mitigating fairness issues to create smaller, faster, and more robust models for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression paradigm in deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the performance of a larger, more complex teacher model. This process enables the deployment of powerful models on resource-constrained devices, which is critical for many real-world applications. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, spanning natural language processing tasks like language model compression and computer vision tasks such as compressing generative models. Researchers have developed numerous variations of the core technique, including methods that leverage multiple teachers, distill knowledge from intermediate network layers, and perform distillation without access to the original training data. Beyond creating smaller and faster models, knowledge distillation is also used to achieve other objectives, such as enhancing model privacy, improving interpretability, and mitigating biases.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial and flexible model compression technique in deep learning. This method addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models on resource-constrained devices by training a smaller 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger 'teacher' model. This knowledge transfer process enables the creation of compact, efficient models that retain high performance. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains and its evolution beyond simple compression to enhance model generalization, transfer knowledge across modalities, and enable new training paradigms.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework Beyond Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful paradigm in deep learning, primarily known as a model compression technique. It facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient 'student' models by transferring knowledge from larger, pre-trained 'teacher' models. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. However, the applications of this framework extend far beyond simple compression. Knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile tool for enhancing model performance, ensuring data privacy, and mitigating algorithmic and gender biases. Its adaptability across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, highlights its critical role in developing practical, robust, and responsible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Torres
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique in deep learning that enables the deployment of large, complex models in resource-constrained environments. The method involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer computational resources. By reducing model size and inference time, knowledge distillation facilitates the practical application of state-of-the-art architectures across diverse domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making advanced artificial intelligence more accessible and efficient.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models, have achieved state-of-the-art performance but their immense size and computational requirements hinder their deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, extending beyond simple compression to enable complex distributed learning paradigms like federated learning on heterogeneous devices. Advanced methods leverage multiple teachers to improve knowledge transfer, and innovative approaches even permit distillation without access to the original training data. Furthermore, the technique can be adapted to various model architectures, including generative networks, and can be used to improve the interpretability of complex deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Stein
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that utilizes a teacher-student framework to create smaller, more efficient models. In this process, a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model, effectively transferring its learned knowledge. The primary objective is to enable the deployment of powerful models on resource-constrained devices without significant performance degradation. This versatile paradigm has broad applications in domains such as natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simply reducing model size, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance model performance, improve generalization, and transfer complex capabilities between different architectures.

papers_seen.author: Farmer
papers_seen.title: Towards Efficient 3D Object Detection with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite substantial progress in 3D object detection, advanced 3D detectors often suffer from heavy computation overheads. To this end, we explore the potential of knowledge distillation (KD) for developing efficient 3D object detectors, focusing on popular pillar- and voxel-based detectors.In the absence of well-developed teacher-student pairs, we first study how to obtain student models with good trade offs between accuracy and efficiency from the perspectives of model compression and input resolution reduction. Then, we build a benchmark to assess existing KD methods developed in the 2D domain for 3D object detection upon six well-constructed teacher-student pairs. Further, we propose an improved KD pipeline incorporating an enhanced logit KD method that performs KD on only a few pivotal positions determined by teacher classification response, and a teacher-guided student model initialization to facilitate transferring teacher model's feature extraction ability to students through weight inheritance. Finally, we conduct extensive experiments on the Waymo dataset. Our best performing model achieves $65.75\%$ LEVEL 2 mAPH, surpassing its teacher model and requiring only $44\%$ of teacher flops. Our most efficient model runs 51 FPS on an NVIDIA A100, which is $2.2\times$ faster than PointPillar with even higher accuracy. Code is available at \url{https://github.com/CVMI-Lab/SparseKD}.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression technique designed to create smaller, more efficient deep learning models without significant performance loss. The process involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This allows for the deployment of complex neural networks on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones. The transfer of knowledge can occur by replicating the teacher's output predictions, its internal representations, or by using more advanced methods like adversarial learning. This technique has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing for compressing large language models, computer vision for efficient image recognition and synthesis, and even in specialized fields like medical imaging and federated learning.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Efficient and Versatile Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to reduce computational and storage costs, making large models deployable on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. This technique has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing for compressing large language models, computer vision for optimizing generative networks, and reinforcement learning for policy transfer. Advanced methods have expanded upon the traditional framework, introducing data-free distillation, meta-learning approaches where the teacher adapts its teaching strategy, and multi-teacher setups. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has also been leveraged to enhance model interpretability and improve generalization across different data distributions, demonstrating its versatility as a powerful tool in the development of practical deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Wells
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient neural networks. It utilizes a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to reduce the computational and memory requirements of state-of-the-art models, facilitating their deployment on resource-constrained devices like mobile phones. This process involves transferring the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, such as its output probability distributions and internal feature representations, to the student. The applications of this versatile framework extend beyond simple compression to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling knowledge transfer in privacy-preserving scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: The Versatility of Knowledge Distillation for Efficient and Robust Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique where a smaller "student" model learns from a larger "teacher" model. This process enables the deployment of complex neural networks on resource-constrained devices. Beyond simple size reduction, distillation can transfer inductive biases, improve performance on downstream tasks, and enhance model efficiency across various domains like natural language processing, computer vision, and graph learning. The framework is highly adaptable, extending to scenarios involving ensemble models, self-improvement, and addressing broader concerns such as data privacy and algorithmic fairness, making it a cornerstone of modern machine learning engineering.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful paradigm in deep learning for compressing large, computationally expensive models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. This process involves a "student" model learning to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By training on the soft probability distributions or intermediate feature representations produced by the teacher, the student model can learn richer information and achieve better generalization than if it were trained solely on hard labels. This technique extends beyond simple model compression, enabling the transfer of inductive biases, performance improvements through self-distillation, and the unification of knowledge from multiple models. Its applications are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and privacy-preserving federated learning, making it a crucial tool for deploying state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. It addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in real-world applications by training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. While primarily used to create lightweight yet powerful models that are significantly faster at inference, the applications of knowledge distillation extend further. The technique can be used to transfer beneficial inductive biases between different model architectures, improve algorithmic fairness by mitigating biases against protected groups, and facilitate domain adaptation by transferring knowledge from source domains to a new target domain. By enabling the creation of efficient, robust, and versatile models, knowledge distillation serves as a crucial tool in the practical application of deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that enables the creation of compact, efficient models from larger, more complex ones. Operating on a teacher-student paradigm, this process involves training a smaller student model to replicate the behavior and performance of a pre-trained teacher network. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art models, enabling their deployment on resource-constrained devices like mobile phones. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple compression, the technique has also proven effective for enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and transferring complex capabilities between models.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: The Versatility of Knowledge Distillation in Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. It enables the creation of smaller, more efficient 'student' models by transferring knowledge from larger, more complex 'teacher' models. This process is critical for deploying state-of-the-art networks in resource-constrained environments. However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple compression. Its applications now encompass a wide range of objectives, including enhancing model interpretability, promoting algorithmic fairness, preserving data privacy in distributed learning settings, and unifying knowledge from multiple disparate models. While the process is not without its challenges, such as the potential for propagating teacher model errors, its flexibility across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision makes it a foundational and versatile tool for developing efficient, effective, and responsible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Vance
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Operating on a teacher-student framework, a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher to the student, enabling the smaller model to achieve high performance with significantly lower computational and memory requirements. While its primary application is model compression, the utility of knowledge distillation has expanded to include performance enhancement, improved model interpretability, and enabling novel applications in privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful machine learning technique where a compact 'student' model learns from a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process enables the creation of smaller, faster, and more computationally efficient neural networks that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts. Initially conceived for model compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now widely used across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to adapt large models for specific tasks, improve model robustness against adversarial attacks, and facilitate learning across different data modalities. By transferring learned representations rather than just final predictions, this framework provides a flexible and effective method for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Gates
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile model compression technique in deep learning. It utilizes a teacher-student framework where a small, efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of complex models, enabling their deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. Beyond compression, this paradigm has expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and facilitating knowledge transfer across different domains and architectures.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and computational cost of modern deep learning models pose significant challenges for their deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent and effective model compression technique to address this issue. The method operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve high performance with a fraction of the computational resources. Beyond its primary use in creating smaller and faster models, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework with applications in improving model generalization, enabling knowledge transfer in data-private scenarios, and adapting models to new domains.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale deep learning models often have computational and storage requirements that hinder their deployment in practical, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a key model compression technique to overcome this challenge. It operates under a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and inherit the knowledge of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process enables the creation of compact, high-performance models suitable for real-world applications. The versatility of this framework extends beyond mere compression, with applications in performance enhancement, domain adaptation, and knowledge transfer in privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This process involves a teacher-student framework, where a compact 'student' model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The student learns from the rich, nuanced information provided by the teacher, such as its output probabilities or internal feature representations. This allows for the development of lightweight yet powerful models across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, without a significant loss in performance.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Crosby
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful and versatile model compression technique in deep learning. It employs a teacher-student framework where a smaller, computationally efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and predictions of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the nuanced knowledge from the teacher, the student can achieve comparable or even enhanced performance while having a significantly smaller footprint. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices, bridging the gap between high accuracy and practical applicability in fields like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has produced increasingly large and complex models that achieve state-of-the-art performance but are often impractical for deployment due to their computational and memory requirements. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, address this challenge by transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the creation of compact models that retain a significant portion of the teacher's performance, making them suitable for resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. The flexibility of knowledge distillation is evident in its successful application across various domains, including natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph-based learning, as well as its adaptability to scenarios where the original training data is unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression technique that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient neural networks. This is achieved through a teacher-student framework, where a smaller "student" model is trained to replicate the outputs or internal representations of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. The primary goal is often to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art models, making them suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has also been shown to improve the performance of student models, sometimes enabling them to outperform models of a similar size trained from scratch. The technique has been successfully applied across a wide array of domains, including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph-based learning, with various methodological innovations continually expanding its utility.

papers_seen.author: Nunez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large, complex deep learning models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. This process involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a pre-trained, high-capacity 'teacher' model. The core idea is to transfer the generalized 'dark knowledge' from the teacher's softened probability distributions or intermediate feature representations to the student. This allows the smaller model to learn more effectively than it would from hard labels alone. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition. It enables the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures on resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, and has been adapted to address challenges like data privacy, domain adaptation, and few-shot learning.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for model compression, enabling the creation of smaller, more efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger, cumbersome teacher models. This process allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has emerged as a versatile framework that can also enhance a model's generalization capabilities, improve its robustness against adversarial attacks, and increase its interpretability. By leveraging the rich information contained in a teacher's predictions, this technique offers a multifaceted approach to optimizing neural networks for a wide range of practical applications in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression technique where a compact 'student' model learns to replicate the behavior of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has been shown to improve model performance, enhance interpretability, and facilitate knowledge transfer across different data modalities. However, the process is not without challenges, as student models can struggle with optimization and may inherit undesirable biases from their teachers. Ongoing research focuses on developing more effective distillation strategies, such as using multiple teachers, applying data augmentation, and mitigating fairness issues to create smaller, faster, and more robust models for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Model Compression Technique in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have demonstrated state-of-the-art performance across many fields, but their large size and high computational requirements often hinder their deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques aim to address this challenge by creating smaller, faster, and more efficient models. Knowledge distillation is a prominent compression paradigm that involves transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained 'teacher' model to a more compact 'student' model. This process allows the student model to achieve performance comparable to the teacher while having a significantly smaller footprint. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Advanced methods have been developed to handle various scenarios, including using multiple teachers, transferring knowledge across different data modalities, and applying distillation in distributed learning frameworks. These techniques are crucial for enabling the practical use of powerful deep learning models in production systems.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and computational demands of modern deep learning models present significant obstacles to their deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible model compression technique to address this challenge. It employs a teacher-student framework where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and inherit the knowledge of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process enables the creation of compact, high-performance models suitable for devices with limited computational power or strict latency requirements. The applications of this technique are broad, spanning natural language processing and computer vision, bridging the gap between state-of-the-art research and practical application.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, especially large pre-trained language models, have achieved state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and computationally expensive for real-world applications. Model compression seeks to address this by creating smaller, more efficient models. Knowledge distillation is a popular compression technique where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the teacher's learned knowledge, enabling the student to achieve high accuracy with significantly fewer resources. Advanced distillation strategies include leveraging multiple teachers, transferring knowledge from intermediate model layers, and even operating in data-free scenarios where the original training set is unavailable. The versatility of knowledge distillation has led to its application in diverse areas beyond simple compression, including domain adaptation and mitigating model bias.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.
