papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, cumbersome teacher model to a smaller, more efficient student model. This process enables the deployment of complex deep learning architectures on resource-constrained devices by reducing model size and inference latency without a significant loss in performance. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing tasks like question answering and machine translation, as well as computer vision domains such as object detection and action recognition. Various methods have been developed, including multi-teacher frameworks, data-free distillation, and fine-grained feature imitation, to improve the knowledge transfer process. These techniques not only facilitate model compression but can also enhance the student model's generalization capabilities and, in some cases, lead to performance that is comparable or even superior to the original teacher model.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework Beyond Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning, widely recognized for its ability to compress large, complex models into smaller, more efficient "student" networks. However, its applications extend far beyond simple model compression. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is a versatile framework capable of not only creating efficient models but also enhancing their performance, enabling new functionalities, and addressing critical challenges such as fairness, privacy, and domain adaptation. By transferring knowledge from one or more "teacher" models, student models can achieve state-of-the-art results in diverse areas including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning. The evolution of distillation techniques, from mimicking output logits to advanced feature-mimicking and meta-learning approaches, further underscores its flexibility and growing importance in the development of robust and adaptable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This process involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a pre-trained, cumbersome 'teacher' model, enabling the deployment of advanced neural networks on resource-constrained devices. The primary goal is to retain the high performance of the teacher model while significantly reducing computational and storage costs. Beyond simple model compression, the applications of knowledge distillation are broad and varied. The framework is used to enhance model robustness against adversarial attacks, facilitate privacy-preserving learning, and even boost the performance of student models beyond their teachers in specific tasks. Its versatility has led to successful applications across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, establishing it as a foundational tool for the practical deployment of state-of-the-art artificial intelligence.

papers_seen.author: Kennedy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression technique where a compact 'student' model learns to replicate the behavior of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has been shown to improve model performance, enhance interpretability, and facilitate knowledge transfer across different data modalities. However, the process is not without challenges, as student models can struggle with optimization and may inherit undesirable biases from their teachers. Ongoing research focuses on developing more effective distillation strategies, such as using multiple teachers, applying data augmentation, and mitigating fairness issues to create smaller, faster, and more robust models for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique for model compression in deep learning. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones, without a significant loss in accuracy. While originally conceived for reducing model size and inference time, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used not only for creating smaller and faster models but also for enhancing model performance, improving interpretability, and addressing practical challenges like data privacy. This demonstrates its evolution from a simple compression tool into a multifaceted framework for developing more efficient, robust, and practical artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Peters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models, have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks. However, their significant computational and memory requirements hinder deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve comparable performance with a fraction of the parameters and faster inference speeds. This approach has proven effective across various domains, including Natural Language Processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, enabling the practical application of complex neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for model compression, where a compact "student" model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, more complex "teacher" model. This process facilitates the deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, by significantly reducing their size and computational requirements. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework capable of enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and enabling novel applications across various domains. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, student models can achieve higher accuracy and robustness than they could by training on ground-truth labels alone.

papers_seen.author: Freeman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance in many fields, but their large size and computational demands often prevent their use in resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques address this issue, with knowledge distillation emerging as a prominent and versatile paradigm. This method involves a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The process transfers the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher to the student, enabling the creation of compact models that are faster and require less memory. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation can also enhance the performance and generalization of the student model, making it a powerful tool for optimizing neural networks for practical deployment.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique in deep learning, primarily for model compression. This process involves training a smaller, efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, including nuanced probability distributions and internal feature representations, the student can achieve comparable or even superior performance with significantly fewer computational resources. While its primary application is creating compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, the utility of knowledge distillation extends further. It has been successfully applied to enhance model robustness, improve algorithmic fairness, facilitate domain adaptation, and increase model interpretability, making it a highly versatile and powerful tool for developing practical and efficient deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning designed to compress large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions. The process involves training a compact 'student' model to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. While the primary objective is to create lightweight models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant drop in accuracy, the applications of knowledge distillation extend much further. It serves as a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, transferring knowledge across different architectures, and addressing challenges such as data privacy and model interpretability. This makes it a foundational strategy for developing practical, robust, and accessible artificial intelligence systems across various domains.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient neural networks without a significant loss in performance. This is achieved through a teacher-student framework, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the outputs and internal representations of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of complex models, enabling their deployment on resource-constrained devices such as mobile phones. This versatile method has been successfully applied across a wide array of domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its applications have expanded beyond simple compression to include performance enhancement and knowledge transfer in privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenges of deploying large, computationally expensive models. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to transfer the generalized knowledge from the teacher to the student, creating a compact model suitable for resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. While initially developed for creating lightweight models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded, proving its versatility for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and transferring knowledge across different architectures.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective and Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression in deep learning. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory requirements of state-of-the-art models, facilitating their deployment on resource-constrained devices such as mobile phones. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve high performance while being significantly more compact. The applications of this versatile framework extend beyond simple compression, proving useful for enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and enabling complex learning scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient neural networks. This is achieved through a teacher-student framework, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the outputs and internal representations of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of complex models, enabling their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation also serves as a versatile tool for enhancing the performance and interpretability of student models. The technique has been successfully applied across a wide array of domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, with ongoing research refining the methods for knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: From Model Compression to a Versatile Deep Learning Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning, initially developed for model compression. It enables the creation of small, efficient "student" models by transferring knowledge from large, complex "teacher" models, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. While its primary use is to reduce computational and memory footprints, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It has evolved into a versatile framework used not only for creating compact models but also for enhancing model performance, improving interpretability, and enabling novel forms of knowledge transfer across different domains, modalities, and architectures. This demonstrates its crucial role in developing more practical, robust, and capable artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: May
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique for compressing large deep learning models. This method involves training a smaller, computationally efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to create compact models that retain high performance while being significantly faster and requiring fewer computational resources, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. However, the applications of this framework extend far beyond simple compression. It can be used to enhance model performance, transfer specific capabilities like adversarial robustness, and even operate in scenarios where the original training data is unavailable, making it a critical tool for the practical application of modern artificial intelligence.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful machine learning technique where a compact 'student' model learns from a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process enables the creation of smaller, faster, and more computationally efficient neural networks that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts. Initially conceived for model compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now widely used across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to adapt large models for specific tasks, improve model robustness against adversarial attacks, and facilitate learning across different data modalities. By transferring learned representations rather than just final predictions, this framework provides a flexible and effective method for deploying state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective and Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression in deep learning. This process addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments by training a smaller 'student' model to mimic a larger 'teacher' model. This transfer of knowledge allows the compact student model to achieve high performance with a fraction of the computational and memory requirements. The versatility of this framework has led to its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it a foundational tool for developing efficient and practical artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and powerful technique for model compression within the field of deep learning. This paradigm addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from a large 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The student is trained to mimic the behavior of the teacher, often by learning from its softened probability outputs or intermediate feature representations. This process allows the compact student model to achieve high performance, often comparable to its much larger teacher, without the associated computational and memory overhead. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it an essential tool for developing practical and deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Fernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique in deep learning that addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments. This paradigm involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge from the teacher, such as its output probabilities or internal feature representations, the student model can achieve high performance with a significantly smaller computational and memory footprint. Initially developed for creating compact models, the applications of this versatile framework have expanded to include enhancing model robustness, improving performance, and facilitating knowledge transfer across different domains and tasks, making it a crucial tool for developing practical and deployable artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Bryant
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and computational demands of modern deep learning models present significant obstacles to their deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible model compression technique to address this challenge. It employs a teacher-student framework where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and inherit the knowledge of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process enables the creation of compact, high-performance models suitable for devices with limited computational power or strict latency requirements. The applications of this technique are broad, spanning natural language processing and computer vision, bridging the gap between state-of-the-art research and practical application.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that operates on a teacher-student paradigm. This process involves training a smaller, computationally efficient student model to mimic the behavior and internal representations of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to reduce computational and memory requirements, enabling the deployment of complex models on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. Beyond compression, the utility of this framework has expanded considerably. It is now widely used to enhance model performance, transfer knowledge across different domains, improve model robustness, and adapt large-scale models for specialized tasks in natural language processing and computer vision, making it a foundational tool for developing practical and efficient AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile model compression technique in deep learning that transfers knowledge from a large 'teacher' model to a smaller 'student' model. The primary goal is to create lightweight, efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. This is achieved by training the student to mimic the rich output distributions or internal representations of the teacher. Beyond model compression, this paradigm has been adapted for a wide range of applications, including enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling knowledge transfer in privacy-sensitive or data-scarce scenarios. Its flexibility has made it a foundational tool in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful machine learning technique for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. This process involves training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The core idea is to transfer the generalized knowledge learned by the teacher, which is often encoded in its output probabilities, to the student. This allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices or applications with strict latency requirements. The applications of knowledge distillation are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and graph-based learning. Beyond simple model compression, distillation has been shown to improve the accuracy of student models, facilitate domain adaptation, and enable training even when the original data is unavailable.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique designed to reduce the size and computational cost of large deep learning models. The process involves a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This knowledge transfer allows the student to achieve high performance while being suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile and edge devices. Originally developed for compression, the applications of this versatile paradigm have expanded to include performance enhancement, robustness improvement, and knowledge transfer in various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Scott
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the deployment of powerful models in resource-constrained environments. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable or even superior performance with significantly lower computational and memory costs. While initially conceived for compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used across diverse domains like natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning not only to create smaller models but also to enhance performance, improve robustness against adversarial attacks, and transfer specialized knowledge, demonstrating its versatility as a fundamental tool in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient ones. The process involves transferring knowledge from a pre-trained "teacher" model to a compact "student" model. The student is trained to mimic the teacher's outputs, such as class probabilities or internal feature representations, in addition to learning from the ground-truth data. This method leverages the rich, nuanced information captured by the teacher to improve the student's performance and generalization capabilities. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to create lightweight models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining high accuracy and sometimes even gaining additional benefits like improved robustness or fairness.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: BERT Learns to Teach: Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We present Knowledge Distillation with Meta Learning (MetaDistil), a simple yet effective alternative to traditional knowledge distillation (KD) methods where the teacher model is fixed during training. We show the teacher network can learn to better transfer knowledge to the student network (i.e., learning to teach) with the feedback from the performance of the distilled student network in a meta learning framework. Moreover, we introduce a pilot update mechanism to improve the alignment between the inner-learner and meta-learner in meta learning algorithms that focus on an improved inner-learner. Experiments on various benchmarks show that MetaDistil can yield significant improvements compared with traditional KD algorithms and is less sensitive to the choice of different student capacity and hyperparameters, facilitating the use of KD on different tasks and models.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm where a compact "student" model is trained to reproduce the performance of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This technique addresses the challenge of deploying computationally intensive deep learning networks on resource-constrained devices. The process involves transferring knowledge from the teacher to the student, often by using the teacher's output probabilities as soft labels or by mimicking its internal feature representations. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing for tasks like machine translation and language model compression, and in computer vision for object detection and image generation. Advanced applications of this framework include enhancing model robustness, preserving privacy in federated learning, and enabling data-free model training.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that enables the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex teacher model to a smaller, more efficient student model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a significant loss in performance. This is typically achieved by training the student to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher. Over time, techniques have evolved beyond simple output matching to include methods based on intermediate features, attention mechanisms, and adversarial learning. These advanced approaches have demonstrated success across a wide range of tasks and domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and generative modeling, making knowledge distillation a critical tool for operationalizing state-of-the-art deep learning models.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary objective is to reduce computational and memory requirements, enabling the deployment of powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining high performance. This is typically achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, often using its output probabilities as supervisory signals. The technique has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework used to enhance model performance, facilitate privacy-preserving distributed learning, and adapt models to new domains.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, pre-trained 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The primary goal is to create lightweight yet powerful models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. The student model learns to mimic the rich output distributions or internal representations of the teacher, thereby inheriting its learned capabilities. Beyond its primary use in compression, knowledge distillation has been adapted for a wide range of applications, including enhancing model performance, improving interpretability, enabling domain generalization, and facilitating privacy-preserving federated learning. Its versatility has made it a foundational tool across various domains, such as natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models, particularly in natural language processing, pose significant challenges for their deployment in resource-constrained or latency-sensitive environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique to address these issues. This method involves transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. Various advanced strategies have been developed to enhance this process, including using multiple teachers, employing adversarial learning, and enabling the teacher to learn how to teach via meta-learning. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, extending from compressing large language models and enabling efficient graph-based inference to facilitating federated learning across heterogeneous devices. These techniques allow for the creation of smaller, faster models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making state-of-the-art deep learning more accessible for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: As deep learning models grow in size and complexity, their deployment in resource-constrained environments becomes a significant challenge. Model compression techniques are essential for creating smaller, faster, and more efficient models without substantial performance degradation. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for this purpose. It involves transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome 'teacher' model to a smaller 'student' model. The student learns to mimic the rich output distributions of the teacher, thereby inheriting its performance capabilities while maintaining a much smaller footprint. This approach has proven effective across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the use of state-of-the-art architectures in practical, real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Long
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical model compression technique in deep learning and natural language processing. The method operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process facilitates the creation of compact, fast, and resource-efficient models that retain high accuracy, enabling the deployment of complex neural networks on devices with limited computational capabilities. While initially developed for model compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly, now encompassing performance enhancement, improved model robustness, and knowledge transfer across different tasks and domains, making it a multifaceted tool for developing practical and powerful artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Compressing Deep Learning Models for Enhanced Efficiency
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning and natural language processing. It facilitates the creation of compact, efficient 'student' models by transferring knowledge from larger, more complex 'teacher' models. This process allows for the deployment of powerful neural networks on devices with limited computational and storage resources, such as mobile phones. Various distillation strategies have been developed, including methods that function without access to the original training data, thereby addressing privacy and data availability concerns. By mimicking the outputs or intermediate representations of a teacher model, the student network can achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller footprint, making it a versatile tool for optimizing deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

papers_seen.author: Aguirre
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, cumbersome teacher model to a smaller, more efficient student model. This process enables the deployment of complex deep learning architectures on resource-constrained devices by reducing model size and inference latency without a significant loss in performance. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing tasks like question answering and machine translation, as well as computer vision domains such as object detection and action recognition. Various methods have been developed, including multi-teacher frameworks, data-free distillation, and fine-grained feature imitation, to improve the knowledge transfer process. These techniques not only facilitate model compression but can also enhance the student model's generalization capabilities and, in some cases, lead to performance that is comparable or even superior to the original teacher model.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing complexity of deep learning models has created significant challenges for their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible model compression technique to address this issue. This method involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model, effectively transferring its learned knowledge. This process enables the creation of smaller, faster models that retain high performance, making them suitable for practical applications. The versatility of knowledge distillation is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, as well as in specialized contexts like data-free learning and enhancing model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Novak
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient ones. This process involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a pre-trained, cumbersome 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to retain the high performance of the teacher model while significantly reducing computational and storage costs, making advanced models deployable on resource-constrained devices. The applications of knowledge distillation are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and healthcare. Beyond simple output matching, advanced methods focus on transferring knowledge from intermediate feature representations and using adversarial techniques to improve the student's learning process. This versatility makes knowledge distillation a crucial tool for optimizing and deploying state-of-the-art neural networks in real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that employs a teacher-student framework. In this process, a compact student model learns to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to create smaller, more computationally efficient networks that can be deployed in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. Knowledge is typically transferred by training the student on the teacher's output probabilities or internal feature representations. This versatile technique is widely applied across domains like natural language processing and computer vision. Its utility extends beyond simple compression, as it can also be used to enhance model performance, improve generalization, and address challenges such as data scarcity and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning where a small, efficient 'student' model is trained to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to transfer the knowledge from a cumbersome, high-performance network to a compact one, making it suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices like mobile phones. This process typically involves training the student on the richer information provided by the teacher's outputs or internal representations. Beyond simply reducing model size, this versatile framework is also used to enhance model performance, improve robustness, and address challenges in areas like data privacy and fairness, making it a crucial tool for creating practical and accessible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a key technique in deep learning for model compression. This method involves training a compact 'student' model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The goal is to create smaller, more computationally efficient models that can be deployed on resource-constrained devices without a substantial loss in performance. By transferring the nuanced knowledge captured by the teacher, the student model can often achieve accuracy comparable to its larger counterpart. The applications of this framework have expanded beyond simple size reduction, proving to be a versatile tool for enhancing model robustness, enabling privacy-preserving learning in decentralized settings, and adapting large models for specific tasks.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Estes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique designed to create smaller, more efficient deep learning models. The process involves training a compact 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the knowledge from the complex teacher to the lightweight student, this method reduces computational and memory requirements, enabling the deployment of powerful models in resource-constrained environments. This approach has proven effective across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and has evolved to include advanced methods that enhance performance and operate under data constraints.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Compressing Large Neural Networks for Practical Applications
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, offer a promising solution by transferring knowledge from a large, powerful 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the creation of compact networks that retain much of the performance of their larger counterparts. Innovations in this field have led to advanced methods, including adversarial training frameworks that adaptively measure the discrepancy between models, and data-free approaches that preserve privacy by eliminating the need for the original training dataset. These developments extend the applicability of state-of-the-art models to a wider range of practical scenarios, from mobile devices to embedded systems, across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary objective is to reduce computational and memory requirements for inference, enabling the deployment of powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments, while preserving high performance. This is achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, often using its output probabilities as supervisory signals. The technique has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, leading to numerous advancements and specialized methods to improve the knowledge transfer process.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The primary objective is to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. This is achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, often by replicating its output probabilities or internal feature representations. The applications of this versatile framework are broad, spanning domains such as natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition, where it is used not only for compression but also to enhance model performance, improve interpretability, and facilitate privacy-preserving learning.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the deployment challenges of large, computationally expensive models. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational costs. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple size reduction, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include performance enhancement and the development of more efficient artificial intelligence systems for real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.
