Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique in deep learning, primarily for model compression. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. While initially conceived to create lightweight networks suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used to improve model robustness against adversarial attacks, transfer knowledge between different model architectures, and facilitate complex learning paradigms such as federated and continual learning. This technique has proven effective across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, demonstrating its flexibility and broad utility beyond simple compression.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Paradigm for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique in deep learning for model compression and performance enhancement. Operating on a teacher-student framework, it enables the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex model to a smaller, more efficient one. The primary objective is to create compact yet powerful models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without significant performance degradation. This versatile approach has found wide-ranging applications in natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition. Its utility extends beyond mere compression, serving to improve model generalization, enable privacy-preserving distributed learning, and even allow student models to surpass their teachers in performance.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly in natural language processing and computer vision, have grown increasingly large and computationally expensive. This trend presents significant challenges for deploying these models in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible model compression technique to address this issue. It involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student to achieve performance far exceeding what it could attain by training on the data alone. The applications of this paradigm are diverse, extending beyond simple compression to areas like continual learning, data-free learning, and unifying knowledge from multiple sources.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Task Enhancement in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning. This method involves training a compact "student" model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. Its primary application is to create lightweight, efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. The utility of knowledge distillation extends across various domains, including natural language processing for compressing large language models and computer vision for tasks like object detection and generative modeling. Advanced strategies have also been developed, such as task-adaptive compression, data-free distillation, and online learning frameworks, showcasing the versatility and ongoing evolution of this technique.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments. The process involves a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This knowledge transfer allows the student to achieve high performance while maintaining a significantly smaller footprint, making it suitable for practical applications. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile paradigm used for improving model generalization, enabling training without access to original data, and facilitating learning in complex settings like federated learning.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression technique that facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, the 'student'. This process aims to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. The fundamental idea is to train the student model to mimic the teacher's behavior, often by using the teacher's output probabilities as soft labels. This method has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, not only for compression but also to improve the performance and generalization of the student model.

papers_seen.author: Stein
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that utilizes a teacher-student framework to create smaller, more efficient models. In this process, a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model, effectively transferring its learned knowledge. The primary objective is to enable the deployment of powerful models on resource-constrained devices without significant performance degradation. This versatile paradigm has broad applications in domains such as natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simply reducing model size, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance model performance, improve generalization, and transfer complex capabilities between different architectures.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models, while powerful, often possess immense computational and memory requirements that hinder their deployment in practical, resource-constrained applications. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a versatile and effective model compression technique to overcome this challenge. The method operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher to the student, enabling the creation of compact models that retain high performance while being significantly smaller and faster. This framework has proven successful across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it a critical tool for bridging the gap between state-of-the-art research and real-world deployability.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful machine learning technique for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. This process involves training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The core idea is to transfer the generalized knowledge learned by the teacher, which is often encoded in its output probabilities, to the student. This allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices or applications with strict latency requirements. The applications of knowledge distillation are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and graph-based learning. Beyond simple model compression, distillation has been shown to improve the accuracy of student models, facilitate domain adaptation, and enable training even when the original data is unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: The Expanding Role of Knowledge Distillation in Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning where knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model is transferred to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. Originally conceived as a method for model compression, its applications have expanded significantly. This technique not only enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments but also serves as a mechanism to enhance the performance of student models beyond what they could achieve through standard training. The versatility of knowledge distillation is demonstrated by its application across diverse domains, from natural language processing to computer vision. Recent advancements have introduced more dynamic and effective distillation frameworks, such as online and self-distillation, and have even leveraged the technique to improve model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Ellis
papers_seen.title: On Representation Knowledge Distillation for Graph Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a learning paradigm for boosting resource-efficient graph neural networks (GNNs) using more expressive yet cumbersome teacher models. Past work on distillation for GNNs proposed the Local Structure Preserving loss (LSP), which matches local structural relationships defined over edges across the student and teacher's node embeddings. This paper studies whether preserving the global topology of how the teacher embeds graph data can be a more effective distillation objective for GNNs, as real-world graphs often contain latent interactions and noisy edges. We propose Graph Contrastive Representation Distillation (G-CRD), which uses contrastive learning to implicitly preserve global topology by aligning the student node embeddings to those of the teacher in a shared representation space. Additionally, we introduce an expanded set of benchmarks on large-scale real-world datasets where the performance gap between teacher and student GNNs is non-negligible. Experiments across 4 datasets and 14 heterogeneous GNN architectures show that G-CRD consistently boosts the performance and robustness of lightweight GNNs, outperforming LSP (and a global structure preserving variant of LSP) as well as baselines from 2D computer vision. An analysis of the representational similarity among teacher and student embedding spaces reveals that G-CRD balances preserving local and global relationships, while structure preserving approaches are best at preserving one or the other. Our code is available at https://github.com/chaitjo/efficient-gnns

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to transfer the rich knowledge from the teacher to the student, enabling the creation of compact, high-performance models suitable for resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. While initially focused on reducing model size and latency, the applications of this technique have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and transferring complex knowledge across various domains such as natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Leonard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient ones without a significant loss in performance. This process involves a large, pre-trained 'teacher' model transferring its knowledge to a smaller 'student' model. The student learns to mimic the teacher's output, thereby inheriting its capabilities. This not only enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices but can also improve the student model's accuracy and generalization ability. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition, making it a crucial tool for creating practical and efficient artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: House
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models, have achieved state-of-the-art performance but their immense size and computational requirements hinder their deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, extending beyond simple compression to enable complex distributed learning paradigms like federated learning on heterogeneous devices. Advanced methods leverage multiple teachers to improve knowledge transfer, and innovative approaches even permit distillation without access to the original training data. Furthermore, the technique can be adapted to various model architectures, including generative networks, and can be used to improve the interpretability of complex deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Ross
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and computational cost of modern deep learning models pose significant challenges for their deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent and effective model compression technique to address this issue. The method operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve high performance with a fraction of the computational resources. Beyond its primary use in creating smaller and faster models, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework with applications in improving model generalization, enabling knowledge transfer in data-private scenarios, and adapting models to new domains.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of compact, efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger, more complex teacher models. This teacher-student learning paradigm enables the deployment of powerful neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as on mobile devices, without a significant loss in performance. The process typically involves training the student to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher. Beyond its primary application in creating lightweight models, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework used to enhance model generalization, transfer knowledge across different architectures, and enable advanced learning strategies.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models without substantial performance degradation. The process involves transferring knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a compact 'student' model. This allows for the deployment of powerful neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. The student learns to mimic the rich output distributions and internal representations of the teacher, thereby inheriting its capabilities while maintaining a smaller footprint. This versatile framework has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its applications extend beyond compression to areas like performance enhancement, robustness, and privacy.

papers_seen.author: Heath
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique used to create smaller, more efficient deep learning models without significant performance loss. The process involves transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained "teacher" model to a more compact "student" model. This paradigm has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning. By leveraging the rich representations learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve high accuracy while being suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices or in latency-sensitive applications. This method proves versatile, addressing challenges such as domain adaptation, few-shot learning, and privacy-preserving federated learning.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Compressing Large Neural Networks for Practical Applications
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, offer a promising solution by transferring knowledge from a large, powerful 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the creation of compact networks that retain much of the performance of their larger counterparts. Innovations in this field have led to advanced methods, including adversarial training frameworks that adaptively measure the discrepancy between models, and data-free approaches that preserve privacy by eliminating the need for the original training dataset. These developments extend the applicability of state-of-the-art models to a wider range of practical scenarios, from mobile devices to embedded systems, across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Yu
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression paradigm where a compact 'student' model learns from a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This technique aims to create smaller, more efficient networks that retain the high performance of their cumbersome counterparts, making them suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Initially focused on mimicking output probabilities, the field has evolved to encompass a wide range of applications beyond simple classification, including complex tasks in natural language processing and computer vision. The effectiveness of distillation is now understood to hinge on more sophisticated methods, such as transferring knowledge from internal feature representations and adapting the process to transfer specific qualities like adversarial robustness. Modern approaches integrate distillation with other compression techniques and advanced training strategies, demonstrating its versatility and importance in developing state-of-the-art, deployable deep learning models.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique to address the challenges posed by the increasing size and complexity of deep learning models. This method involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, more cumbersome 'teacher' model. The goal is to transfer the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the creation of compact, fast models that retain high performance. This makes state-of-the-art deep learning more accessible for deployment in resource-constrained or latency-sensitive environments, such as mobile devices. The technique has proven successful and versatile across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly in fields like natural language processing, have grown significantly in size and computational cost, posing challenges for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Model compression aims to create smaller, more efficient models while retaining high performance. Knowledge distillation is a prominent compression paradigm where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger 'teacher' model. This approach transfers the learned knowledge of the teacher, enabling the smaller student to achieve better performance than if trained alone. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, with research exploring advanced techniques such as transferring knowledge from intermediate layers, using multiple teachers, and performing distillation without access to the original training data.

papers_seen.author: Gilbert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenges of deploying large, computationally expensive models. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to transfer the generalized knowledge from the teacher to the student, creating a compact model suitable for resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. While initially developed for creating lightweight models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded, proving its versatility for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and transferring knowledge across different architectures.

papers_seen.author: Tucker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique that facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This is achieved by training the student to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Advanced methods have been developed to address specific challenges, such as transferring adversarial robustness, performing distillation without access to original training data, mitigating biases, and improving the interaction between teacher and student models.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex model to a smaller, more efficient one. This process operates on a teacher-student framework, where the compact student model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of the larger teacher. The primary objective is to enable the deployment of powerful, state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, where computational power and memory are limited. While initially conceived for creating smaller and faster models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used to enhance model performance, improve interpretability, and address challenges in areas like data privacy and federated learning across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model to a smaller, more efficient one. This teacher-student learning paradigm enables the deployment of powerful models in resource-constrained environments by significantly reducing their computational and memory requirements. The process involves training the compact student model to mimic the behavior of the pre-trained teacher, often by using the teacher's output probabilities or internal feature representations as a supervisory signal. This allows the student to learn richer, more nuanced information than it would from ground-truth labels alone. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing and computer vision, and its utility extends beyond compression to include performance enhancement, regularization, and cross-modal knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments. The process involves a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This knowledge transfer allows the student to achieve high performance while maintaining a significantly smaller footprint, making it suitable for practical applications. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile paradigm used for improving model generalization, enabling training without access to original data, and facilitating learning in complex settings like federated learning.

papers_seen.author: Lambert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The primary objective is to enable the deployment of powerful, state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their size and computational requirements without a substantial loss in performance. The process typically involves training the student to mimic the rich output distributions of the teacher, which contain more information than simple ground-truth labels. The applications of this paradigm are extensive, spanning natural language processing and computer vision. Advanced methods have evolved to include transferring knowledge from intermediate layers, using multiple teachers, and extending the technique's utility beyond compression to areas such as improving model robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Cooke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary objective is to create lightweight models that maintain high performance while reducing computational and memory requirements, which is crucial for deployment in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. The process typically involves training the student model to mimic the behavior of the teacher, often by learning from its rich output probability distributions or intermediate feature representations. This versatile framework has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and has been extended to address challenges in areas such as data privacy and domain adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial and flexible model compression technique in deep learning. This method addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models on resource-constrained devices by training a smaller 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger 'teacher' model. This knowledge transfer process enables the creation of compact, efficient models that retain high performance. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains and its evolution beyond simple compression to enhance model generalization, transfer knowledge across modalities, and enable new training paradigms.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the deployment of large, complex models in resource-constrained environments. It employs a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a more powerful, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the teacher's generalized knowledge, allowing the smaller student to achieve comparable performance with significantly lower computational and memory costs. Beyond its primary role in creating lightweight models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling knowledge transfer across different domains and learning paradigms.

papers_seen.author: Mccarthy

This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the performance of a pre-trained teacher model, enabling the deployment of powerful neural networks on devices with limited computational resources. The student learns by mimicking the rich output distributions or internal feature representations of the teacher. While its primary use is model compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include performance enhancement, knowledge transfer across different data modalities, and enabling learning in privacy-sensitive scenarios. This technique has proven effective across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the deployment of large, complex models in resource-constrained environments. The core idea involves transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained 'teacher' model to a smaller 'student' model, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. Beyond simple compression, this paradigm has been adapted to address a wide range of challenges. Researchers have successfully employed knowledge distillation to enhance model fairness by mitigating algorithmic and gender biases, to improve data privacy by creating models with differential privacy guarantees, and even to develop student models that outperform their teachers. This adaptability across various domains, including natural language processing and graph-based learning, highlights knowledge distillation as a powerful and flexible tool in the development of efficient and responsible AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Evans

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and powerful technique for model compression within the field of deep learning. This paradigm addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from a large 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The student is trained to mimic the behavior of the teacher, often by learning from its softened probability outputs or intermediate feature representations. This process allows the compact student model to achieve high performance, often comparable to its much larger teacher, without the associated computational and memory overhead. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it an essential tool for developing practical and deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary objective is to create compact models that retain high performance, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. The process involves training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, often by learning from its output distributions or internal feature representations. While initially conceived for creating smaller and faster models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. The framework is now used to enhance student model performance, improve interpretability, and address considerations like data privacy and algorithmic fairness, establishing it as a multifaceted tool in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Brown

This paradigm has been successfully applied across diverse fields, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning. By learning from the teacher's output distributions, the student model can achieve significant performance gains compared to training from scratch, effectively enabling the practical use of state-of-the-art but cumbersome deep learning architectures.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Enhancement in Deep Learning

Its widespread applications across domains like natural language processing and computer vision make it a critical tool for developing practical and efficient artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments. The method operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student to achieve high performance with significantly reduced size and computational cost. Its applications are widespread, particularly in natural language processing and computer vision, and advanced methods have expanded its utility beyond simple compression to include performance enhancement and knowledge transfer in complex learning scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Learning Student-Friendly Teacher Networks for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel knowledge distillation approach to facilitate the transfer of dark knowledge from a teacher to a student. Contrary to most of the existing methods that rely on effective training of student models given pretrained teachers, we aim to learn the teacher models that are friendly to students and, consequently, more appropriate for knowledge transfer. In other words, at the time of optimizing a teacher model, the proposed algorithm learns the student branches jointly to obtain student-friendly representations. Since the main goal of our approach lies in training teacher models and the subsequent knowledge distillation procedure is straightforward, most of the existing knowledge distillation methods can adopt this technique to improve the performance of diverse student models in terms of accuracy and convergence speed. The proposed algorithm demonstrates outstanding accuracy in several well-known knowledge distillation techniques with various combinations of teacher and student models even in the case that their architectures are heterogeneous and there is no prior knowledge about student models at the time of training teacher networks.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning designed to compress large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions. The process involves training a compact "student" model to mimic the behavior and outputs of a pre-trained, high-performance "teacher" model. This knowledge transfer enables the deployment of powerful artificial intelligence systems in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a substantial loss in accuracy. While originally conceived for model compression, the applications of distillation have expanded significantly, now serving as a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling advanced learning paradigms like domain adaptation and federated learning.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large, complex deep learning models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This process involves a "teacher-student" paradigm, where a smaller student network learns to mimic the outputs or internal representations of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve comparable performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. This makes it possible to deploy state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as on mobile devices or for latency-sensitive applications. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing, where it is used to create compact language models, and computer vision, for tasks like object detection and image classification. Research continues to explore novel distillation methods, including data-free approaches and cross-architecture knowledge transfer, further enhancing its flexibility and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique for compressing large deep learning models. This method involves training a smaller, computationally efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the nuanced 'dark knowledge' from the teacher's predictions, rather than just learning from ground-truth labels, the student model can achieve performance comparable to its larger counterpart while being significantly smaller and faster. This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices without a substantial sacrifice in accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: FedZKT: Zero-Shot Knowledge Transfer towards Resource-Constrained Federated Learning with Heterogeneous On-Device Models
papers_seen.abstract: Federated learning enables multiple distributed devices to collaboratively learn a shared prediction model without centralizing their on-device data. Most of the current algorithms require comparable individual efforts for local training with the same structure and size of on-device models, which, however, impedes participation from resource-constrained devices. Given the widespread yet heterogeneous devices nowadays, in this paper, we propose an innovative federated learning framework with heterogeneous on-device models through Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer, named by FedZKT. Specifically, FedZKT allows devices to independently determine the on-device models upon their local resources. To achieve knowledge transfer across these heterogeneous on-device models, a zero-shot distillation approach is designed without any prerequisites for private on-device data, which is contrary to certain prior research based on a public dataset or a pre-trained data generator. Moreover, this compute-intensive distillation task is assigned to the server to allow the participation of resource-constrained devices, where a generator is adversarially learned with the ensemble of collected on-device models. The distilled central knowledge is then sent back in the form of the corresponding on-device model parameters, which can be easily absorbed on the device side. Extensive experimental studies demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of FedZKT towards on-device knowledge agnostic, on-device model heterogeneity, and other challenging federated learning scenarios, such as heterogeneous on-device data and straggler effects.

By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, student models can achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller footprint. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains and its adaptation to address challenges like data privacy and architectural mismatches, making advanced AI more accessible for real-world use.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile technique for compressing large, complex deep learning models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. The process typically involves a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model that transfers its learned knowledge to a smaller 'student' model. By training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, often through its output probabilities or intermediate feature representations, the smaller model can achieve high performance that would be unattainable by training on data alone. This approach is critical for deploying state-of-the-art models, particularly in natural language processing, on resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. The applications of knowledge distillation are broad, extending beyond simple compression to areas like domain adaptation, privacy preservation, and overall performance enhancement.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Task Enhancement in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning. This method involves training a compact "student" model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. Its primary application is to create lightweight, efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. The utility of knowledge distillation extends across various domains, including natural language processing for compressing large language models and computer vision for tasks like object detection and generative modeling. Advanced strategies have also been developed, such as task-adaptive compression, data-free distillation, and online learning frameworks, showcasing the versatility and ongoing evolution of this technique.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance on many tasks but their size and computational requirements pose significant challenges for deployment. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, offer a solution by transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. This process enables the creation of compact models that retain a high degree of the teacher's performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing, to develop smaller, domain-specific language models, improve machine translation systems, and compress complex ensemble models. Research has also explored its use in mitigating societal biases in language models. The versatility of this technique is further demonstrated by different approaches, such as self-distillation and data-free distillation, which expand its applicability. The success of knowledge distillation is often attributed to the rich, supervisory information contained in the teacher's soft probability outputs and its ability to act as a form of learned regularization.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective Strategy for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques have emerged as a critical field of study to address these issues. Knowledge distillation, a prominent compression method, involves training a smaller 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student model to achieve performance far exceeding what it could attain by training on ground-truth labels alone. This approach has proven versatile, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, leading to models that are not only smaller and faster but also maintain high levels of accuracy, facilitating the practical application of state-of-the-art deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.
