papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile framework for compressing large, complex deep learning models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This teacher-student learning paradigm enables the transfer of knowledge from a high-capacity teacher model to a compact student model, allowing for the deployment of state-of-the-art performance on resource-constrained devices. The process involves training the student to mimic the rich outputs or internal representations of the teacher, effectively creating models that are not only smaller and faster but can also exhibit enhanced performance and robustness. The applications of this technique are extensive, spanning domains like natural language processing and computer vision, and its adaptability has led to advanced methods involving multiple teachers, adversarial learning, and data-free scenarios, solidifying its role as a crucial tool for creating practical and deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Contreras
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique in deep learning, primarily for model compression. Operating on a teacher-student framework, it facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex model to a smaller, more efficient one. This process enables the deployment of powerful models on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones, without a significant loss in performance. However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond creating smaller models. It has evolved into a versatile paradigm for enhancing model performance, improving robustness and fairness, and adapting models for specialized contexts. This demonstrates its crucial role in developing practical, efficient, and responsible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile model compression technique in deep learning that operates on a teacher-student paradigm. It involves training a smaller, more efficient student model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to create compact models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This is achieved by transferring the rich knowledge from the teacher's soft probability outputs or intermediate feature representations to the student. The technique has widespread applications in fields such as natural language processing and computer vision. The framework has evolved to include advanced methods like multi-teacher, online, and self-distillation, as well as data-free approaches for scenarios with privacy constraints. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation is also leveraged to enhance model performance and improve learning robustness.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. The core idea involves training the student network to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher. Innovations in this field have expanded the technique's applicability, leading to methods like zero-shot distillation, which functions without access to the original training data, and self-distillation, where a model learns from its own representations. These approaches have been successfully applied to compress a wide range of models, from large-scale language models in Natural Language Processing (NLP) to complex architectures used in computer vision and multimodal tasks, demonstrating the flexibility and practical utility of knowledge distillation in creating lightweight, yet powerful, AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

Beyond compression, knowledge distillation can also be used to improve a model's performance, enhance its generalization capabilities across different data distributions, and transfer beneficial properties, such as inductive biases, from one model to another. The technique is versatile, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, and has given rise to numerous variations, including self-distillation, data-free distillation, and methods involving multiple or adaptive teachers.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for model compression in deep learning. This approach facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more computationally efficient model, the 'student'. The primary goal is to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. This teacher-student learning framework is not limited to simple label matching; it often involves transferring knowledge from intermediate layers and output distributions. The technique has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing for compressing large language models like BERT, and in computer vision for tasks such as object detection and image segmentation. Research has also explored advanced strategies like data-free distillation to address privacy concerns and methods to train more effective 'student-friendly' teachers.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework Beyond Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning, widely recognized for its ability to compress large, complex models into smaller, more efficient "student" networks. However, its applications extend far beyond simple model compression. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is a versatile framework capable of not only creating efficient models but also enhancing their performance, enabling new functionalities, and addressing critical challenges such as fairness, privacy, and domain adaptation. By transferring knowledge from one or more "teacher" models, student models can achieve state-of-the-art results in diverse areas including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning. The evolution of distillation techniques, from mimicking output logits to advanced feature-mimicking and meta-learning approaches, further underscores its flexibility and growing importance in the development of robust and adaptable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks, but their large size and computational expense often hinder their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model, effectively transferring the teacher's learned knowledge. This process allows for the creation of compact models that are significantly faster and smaller, yet retain a high level of performance. Knowledge distillation has proven to be a flexible and effective strategy across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, enabling the development of powerful and practical AI applications.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to transfer the rich knowledge from the teacher to the student, enabling the creation of compact, high-performance models suitable for resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. While initially focused on reducing model size and latency, the applications of this technique have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and transferring complex knowledge across various domains such as natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Deep neural networks have become increasingly large and complex, which hinders their deployment on devices with limited computational resources. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" network to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" network or an ensemble of models. The student learns to reproduce the teacher's outputs or its internal representations, effectively transferring the rich knowledge learned by the larger model. This process enables the creation of compact models that maintain high performance across a variety of domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, without requiring architectural changes or additional data.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective and Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial and highly effective technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. The process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This transfer of knowledge allows for the creation of compact models that retain high performance while being suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. The applications of this paradigm have expanded significantly beyond simple size reduction, now encompassing tasks like performance enhancement, improving model robustness, and enabling learning in privacy-sensitive settings. This versatility establishes knowledge distillation as a foundational framework for developing practical, deployable, and powerful artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique in deep learning for model compression. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, enabling the creation of smaller, more efficient 'student' models by transferring knowledge from larger, more complex 'teacher' models. This process facilitates the deployment of powerful neural networks on devices with limited computational resources, such as mobile phones. While its primary goal is to reduce model size and latency, the applications of knowledge distillation extend further, serving as a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling advanced learning strategies in areas like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Montoya
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: As deep learning models increase in size and complexity, their deployment in resource-constrained environments poses a significant challenge. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and widely adopted technique for model compression. This method involves a teacher-student learning paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student can achieve comparable or even enhanced performance with a significantly smaller computational footprint. This approach enables the practical application of state-of-the-art models on devices with limited memory and processing power, proving effective across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Douglas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning designed to compress large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions. The process involves training a compact 'student' model to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. While the primary objective is to create lightweight models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant drop in accuracy, the applications of knowledge distillation extend much further. It serves as a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, transferring knowledge across different architectures, and addressing challenges such as data privacy and model interpretability. This makes it a foundational strategy for developing practical, robust, and accessible artificial intelligence systems across various domains.

papers_seen.author: Mueller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Optimization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm wherein a compact "student" model is trained to reproduce the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. The primary objective is to transfer the generalized knowledge from the cumbersome teacher to the lightweight student, thereby creating a smaller, faster model suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This technique has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. By learning from the richer, soft probability distributions output by the teacher, rather than just the hard labels from the training data, the student model can often achieve performance superior to what it could attain if trained on the data alone.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing complexity of deep learning models poses significant challenges for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial model compression technique to address this issue. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, enabling the creation of compact models that retain high performance while reducing computational and memory requirements. Beyond simple compression, this versatile framework has found applications in enhancing model generalization, improving robustness, and enabling knowledge transfer in novel scenarios, making advanced artificial intelligence more accessible and practical for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Wells
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient neural networks. It utilizes a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to reduce the computational and memory requirements of state-of-the-art models, facilitating their deployment on resource-constrained devices like mobile phones. This process involves transferring the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, such as its output probability distributions and internal feature representations, to the student. The applications of this versatile framework extend beyond simple compression to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling knowledge transfer in privacy-preserving scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique for compressing large deep learning models. This method involves training a smaller, computationally efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the nuanced 'dark knowledge' from the teacher's predictions, rather than just learning from ground-truth labels, the student model can achieve performance comparable to its larger counterpart while being significantly smaller and faster. This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices without a substantial sacrifice in accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Rivera
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: More Than Just Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile technique in deep learning designed to compress large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions. This process involves a compact 'student' model being trained to mimic the behavior of a pre-trained, cumbersome 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to retain the high performance of the teacher while reducing computational and memory requirements, enabling the deployment of advanced models on resource-constrained devices. However, the applications and implications of knowledge distillation extend far beyond simple compression. It serves as a powerful framework for knowledge transfer, performance enhancement, and addressing ethical considerations like fairness, making it a fundamental tool for creating more practical and robust artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Understanding and Improving Lexical Choice in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is essential for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models by reducing the complexity of the raw data with an autoregressive teacher model. In this study, we empirically show that as a side effect of this training, the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words are propagated to the NAT model from the teacher model. To alleviate this problem, we propose to expose the raw data to NAT models to restore the useful information of low-frequency words, which are missed in the distilled data. To this end, we introduce an extra Kullback-Leibler divergence term derived by comparing the lexical choice of NAT model and that embedded in the raw data. Experimental results across language pairs and model architectures demonstrate the effectiveness and universality of the proposed approach. Extensive analyses confirm our claim that our approach improves performance by reducing the lexical choice errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach pushes the SOTA NAT performance on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets up to 27.8 and 33.8 BLEU points, respectively. The source code will be released.

papers_seen.author: Martin

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a highly effective and versatile framework for model compression in deep learning. This technique addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller footprint and faster inference speed. The applications of this method extend beyond simple compression, serving to enhance model performance, improve generalization, and enable new learning paradigms across domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Highlight Every Step: Knowledge Distillation via Collaborative Teaching
papers_seen.abstract: High storage and computational costs obstruct deep neural networks to be deployed on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation aims to train a compact student network by transferring knowledge from a larger pre-trained teacher model. However, most existing methods on knowledge distillation ignore the valuable information among training process associated with training results. In this paper, we provide a new Collaborative Teaching Knowledge Distillation (CTKD) strategy which employs two special teachers. Specifically, one teacher trained from scratch (i.e., scratch teacher) assists the student step by step using its temporary outputs. It forces the student to approach the optimal path towards the final logits with high accuracy. The other pre-trained teacher (i.e., expert teacher) guides the student to focus on a critical region which is more useful for the task. The combination of the knowledge from two special teachers can significantly improve the performance of the student network in knowledge distillation. The results of experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, SVHN and Tiny ImageNet datasets verify that the proposed knowledge distillation method is efficient and achieves state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions suitable for real-world deployment. This process involves a smaller "student" model learning from a larger "teacher" model, transferring knowledge beyond simple labels. Originally conceived for model compression, its applications have expanded significantly across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Research shows that distillation not only reduces model size and inference time but can also enhance the student model's performance, sometimes even surpassing models trained from scratch. Advanced methods like self-distillation and data-free distillation further broaden its utility, making it a crucial tool for developing practical and effective deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale deep learning models, particularly in natural language processing, have demonstrated state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and computationally expensive for real-world applications. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model, thereby transferring its learned knowledge. This process allows for the creation of smaller, faster models that maintain high performance, making them suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Advanced approaches have extended this framework to scenarios without original training data, settings with multiple teachers, and decentralized paradigms like federated learning, showcasing its versatility and importance in creating efficient AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Payne
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient neural networks. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to transfer the teacher's learned knowledge, enabling the student to achieve high performance with significantly fewer computational resources. This makes it possible to deploy state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. The applications of this versatile framework are broad, extending beyond simple compression to include performance enhancement and knowledge transfer across various domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has produced increasingly large and complex models that achieve state-of-the-art performance but are often impractical for deployment due to their computational and memory requirements. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, address this challenge by transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the creation of compact models that retain a significant portion of the teacher's performance, making them suitable for resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. The flexibility of knowledge distillation is evident in its successful application across various domains, including natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph-based learning, as well as its adaptability to scenarios where the original training data is unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Mathis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Paradigm for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. Operating on a teacher-student paradigm, it facilitates the creation of compact, efficient models by transferring knowledge from a larger, more complex model to a smaller one. This process is crucial for deploying state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. The utility of knowledge distillation extends beyond simple size reduction, offering a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, enabling privacy-preserving learning, and adapting models to new domains, making it a cornerstone of practical artificial intelligence development.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the deployment of large, complex models in resource-constrained environments. It employs a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a more powerful, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the teacher's generalized knowledge, allowing the smaller student to achieve comparable performance with significantly lower computational and memory costs. Beyond its primary role in creating lightweight models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling knowledge transfer across different domains and learning paradigms.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Hawkins
papers_seen.title: A Fast Knowledge Distillation Framework for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: While Knowledge Distillation (KD) has been recognized as a useful tool in many visual tasks, such as supervised classification and self-supervised representation learning, the main drawback of a vanilla KD framework is its mechanism, which consumes the majority of the computational overhead on forwarding through the giant teacher networks, making the entire learning procedure inefficient and costly. ReLabel, a recently proposed solution, suggests creating a label map for the entire image. During training, it receives the cropped region-level label by RoI aligning on a pre-generated entire label map, allowing for efficient supervision generation without having to pass through the teachers many times. However, as the KD teachers are from conventional multi-crop training, there are various mismatches between the global label-map and region-level label in this technique, resulting in performance deterioration. In this study, we present a Fast Knowledge Distillation (FKD) framework that replicates the distillation training phase and generates soft labels using the multi-crop KD approach, while training faster than ReLabel since no post-processes such as RoI align and softmax operations are used. When conducting multi-crop in the same image for data loading, our FKD is even more efficient than the traditional image classification framework. On ImageNet-1K, we obtain 79.8% with ResNet-50, outperforming ReLabel by ~1.0% while being faster. On the self-supervised learning task, we also show that FKD has an efficiency advantage. Our project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/FKD/index.html, source code and models are available at: https://github.com/szq0214/FKD.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous domains, but their large size and computational expense often hinder deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and effective model compression technique to address this challenge. The process involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher's predictions or internal representations, the student can achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters. The utility of this framework has expanded beyond simple compression, proving effective for enhancing model performance, transferring specific capabilities like adversarial robustness, and even mitigating societal biases within language models. Advanced methods such as self-distillation, online distillation, and data-free approaches further increase its versatility, making it a critical tool for developing efficient and practical AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique in deep learning, primarily for model compression. This process involves training a smaller, efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, including nuanced probability distributions and internal feature representations, the student can achieve comparable or even superior performance with significantly fewer computational resources. While its primary application is creating compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, the utility of knowledge distillation extends further. It has been successfully applied to enhance model robustness, improve algorithmic fairness, facilitate domain adaptation, and increase model interpretability, making it a highly versatile and powerful tool for developing practical and efficient deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Rivas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Enhancement in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that creates smaller, more efficient models from larger ones. This process uses a teacher-student framework, where a compact "student" model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. The primary goal is to enable the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a significant loss in performance. Knowledge is typically transferred by mimicking the teacher's output probabilities or internal feature representations. While widely used for compressing models in fields like natural language processing and computer vision, its applications extend beyond size reduction to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling advanced learning paradigms like self-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, the 'student'. This process enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. The fundamental approach involves training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs, but numerous variations have been developed to enhance this process. These include distilling knowledge from intermediate feature representations, using multiple teachers for domain adaptation or multi-task learning, and applying distillation in specialized areas like object detection and graph neural networks. Advanced methods address challenges such as the absence of training data, the propagation of model biases, and applications in privacy-preserving federated learning. By leveraging knowledge from more capable models, distillation significantly improves the performance of compact networks across a wide range of tasks in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression in deep learning, addressing the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models in resource-constrained environments. This method involves a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich knowledge from the teacher, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer resources. Beyond simple compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model robustness, facilitating training without original data, and improving overall performance. Its adaptability across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, highlights its role as a foundational tool for creating practical and efficient AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Flores
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large, computationally expensive deep learning models into smaller, more efficient versions suitable for practical deployment. This method employs a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student can achieve comparable or even superior performance with a significantly smaller footprint. The framework's versatility is demonstrated by its successful application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, bridging the gap between high-performance research models and deployable artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Chapman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient ones. The process involves transferring knowledge from a pre-trained "teacher" model to a compact "student" model. The student is trained to mimic the teacher's outputs, such as class probabilities or internal feature representations, in addition to learning from the ground-truth data. This method leverages the rich, nuanced information captured by the teacher to improve the student's performance and generalization capabilities. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to create lightweight models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices while maintaining high accuracy and sometimes even gaining additional benefits like improved robustness or fairness.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning where a small, efficient 'student' model is trained to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to transfer the knowledge from a cumbersome, high-performance network to a compact one, making it suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices like mobile phones. This process typically involves training the student on the richer information provided by the teacher's outputs or internal representations. Beyond simply reducing model size, this versatile framework is also used to enhance model performance, improve robustness, and address challenges in areas like data privacy and fairness, making it a crucial tool for creating practical and accessible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and computational cost of modern deep learning models pose significant challenges for their deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent and effective model compression technique to address this issue. The method operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve high performance with a fraction of the computational resources. Beyond its primary use in creating smaller and faster models, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework with applications in improving model generalization, enabling knowledge transfer in data-private scenarios, and adapting models to new domains.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm in deep learning where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of complex neural networks, enabling their deployment on resource-constrained devices without a substantial loss in performance. This is achieved by transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, such as output probabilities or internal feature representations, to the student. While initially developed for model compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly, proving its versatility across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision for enhancing model robustness, preserving privacy, and transferring knowledge across different model architectures.

papers_seen.author: Beck
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile and Effective Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models often have immense computational requirements, limiting their use in practical applications. Knowledge distillation offers a powerful solution for model compression. This technique involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process enables the creation of smaller, faster models that retain high performance, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. The versatility of this framework has led to its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, bridging the gap between state-of-the-art performance and real-world deployability.

By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, student models can achieve higher accuracy and robustness than they could by training on ground-truth labels alone.

While the primary goal is to reduce computational and memory requirements for resource-constrained environments, the applications of knowledge distillation extend far beyond simple model compression. This makes it a fundamental tool for creating more practical, robust, and efficient artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale deep learning models often have computational and storage requirements that hinder their deployment in practical, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a key model compression technique to overcome this challenge. It operates under a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and inherit the knowledge of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process enables the creation of compact, high-performance models suitable for real-world applications. The versatility of this framework extends beyond mere compression, with applications in performance enhancement, domain adaptation, and knowledge transfer in privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression paradigm designed to create efficient, lightweight "student" deep learning models by transferring knowledge from larger, more powerful "teacher" models. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art networks in resource-constrained environments. The methods for knowledge transfer have evolved from matching output probabilities to more sophisticated techniques that focus on mimicking intermediate feature representations. Innovations in the field include adversarial training frameworks, the application of automated machine learning for architecture search, and even teacher-free approaches that leverage self-distillation as a form of regularization. Knowledge distillation has demonstrated significant success across a wide range of applications, including the compression of large language models in natural language processing, the simplification of complex graph neural networks, and the optimization of models in federated learning and speech recognition systems.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez

By transferring the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, the student model can achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller footprint. The utility of this framework extends beyond simple size reduction, proving effective for enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and even mitigating societal biases. Knowledge distillation is a critical and versatile tool for developing efficient, practical, and accessible AI systems.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile technique for compressing large, complex deep learning models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. By training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, often through its output probabilities or intermediate feature representations, the smaller model can achieve high performance that would be unattainable by training on data alone. This approach is critical for deploying state-of-the-art models, particularly in natural language processing, on resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. The applications of knowledge distillation are broad, extending beyond simple compression to areas like domain adaptation, privacy preservation, and overall performance enhancement.

papers_seen.author: Allison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly in natural language processing and computer vision, have grown increasingly large and computationally expensive. This trend presents significant challenges for deploying these models in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible model compression technique to address this issue. It involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student to achieve performance far exceeding what it could attain by training on the data alone. The applications of this paradigm are diverse, extending beyond simple compression to areas like continual learning, data-free learning, and unifying knowledge from multiple sources.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful machine learning technique focused on transferring knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the teacher, to a smaller, more efficient model, called the student. Originally conceived for model compression, this process allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by creating smaller, faster versions that retain much of the original's performance. The applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly beyond simple compression. It is now used to improve the absolute performance of student models, sometimes even allowing them to outperform their teachers. Furthermore, the technique has been adapted to address challenges in diverse areas such as federated learning, data privacy, and multimodal learning. By leveraging the learned representations of a teacher, knowledge distillation provides a flexible framework for creating more practical, robust, and capable models across various domains, particularly in Natural Language Processing (NLP).

papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models, have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks. Model compression techniques, especially knowledge distillation, have emerged as a powerful solution to this problem. papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Taylor

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique for model compression within deep learning.
