papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Mcdonald
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models. Operating under a teacher-student paradigm, a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process enables the deployment of complex, state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, by significantly reducing computational and memory requirements without a substantial loss in performance. While its primary application is compression, the utility of knowledge distillation has expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and transferring specific capabilities across various domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and powerful technique in deep learning, primarily aimed at model compression. This method operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The core objective is to create compact, computationally inexpensive models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. By transferring the nuanced knowledge from a teacher's internal representations or output probabilities, the student can achieve superior performance than by learning from data alone. The applications of this versatile framework extend beyond simple compression, proving effective in enhancing model robustness, transferring knowledge in data-scarce scenarios, and improving performance across a wide range of domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Maddox
papers_seen.title: BERT-EMD: Many-to-Many Layer Mapping for BERT Compression with Earth Mover's Distance
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained language models (e.g., BERT) have achieved significant success in various natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, high storage and computational costs obstruct pre-trained language models to be effectively deployed on resource-constrained devices. In this paper, we propose a novel BERT distillation method based on many-to-many layer mapping, which allows each intermediate student layer to learn from any intermediate teacher layers. In this way, our model can learn from different teacher layers adaptively for various NLP tasks. %motivated by the intuition that different NLP tasks require different levels of linguistic knowledge contained in the intermediate layers of BERT. In addition, we leverage Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to compute the minimum cumulative cost that must be paid to transform knowledge from teacher network to student network. EMD enables the effective matching for many-to-many layer mapping. %EMD can be applied to network layers with different sizes and effectively measures semantic distance between the teacher network and student network. Furthermore, we propose a cost attention mechanism to learn the layer weights used in EMD automatically, which is supposed to further improve the model's performance and accelerate convergence time. Extensive experiments on GLUE benchmark demonstrate that our model achieves competitive performance compared to strong competitors in terms of both accuracy and model compression.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Valdez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Paradigm for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a versatile and powerful technique for model compression within deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process facilitates the deployment of complex, state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their size and computational requirements. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation also serves as a method to enhance student model performance, improve generalization, and enable novel applications in areas like privacy-preserving learning and cross-modal knowledge transfer. Its flexibility has led to widespread adoption and research across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in which a compact 'student' model is trained to emulate the performance of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of deep learning models, enabling their deployment on resource-constrained devices without a substantial loss in accuracy. This is achieved by transferring the 'knowledge' from the teacher to the student, often by using the teacher's output probabilities as soft targets for training the student. While initially focused on compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and facilitating training in privacy-sensitive or data-scarce environments. The versatility of this framework has made it a crucial tool across various domains, including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm designed to create smaller, more efficient deep learning models without a significant loss in performance. The technique involves training a compact "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich, generalized knowledge learned by the teacher, typically through its output probabilities or internal feature representations, the student model can be deployed on resource-constrained devices. This framework has seen wide application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and has been extended to more advanced use cases such as performance enhancement and data-private learning scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression paradigm where a compact "student" network learns from a larger "teacher" network. This technique facilitates the deployment of complex deep learning models in settings with limited computational resources. The process involves transferring knowledge through various mechanisms, including mimicking the teacher's final outputs, aligning intermediate feature representations, or preserving relational knowledge. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse fields such as natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition. Beyond simple compression, this framework can be used for more advanced purposes, including transferring specific properties like adversarial robustness or inductive biases between different model architectures. It also enables novel applications like cross-modal learning and improving models in federated learning environments.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Model Compression Technique in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective model compression and training paradigm in which a compact 'student' model learns to mimic a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to transfer the knowledge from the high-performing teacher to the student, enabling the creation of smaller, faster, and more efficient models that are suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. This knowledge transfer can occur in various forms, from mimicking the teacher's final output probabilities (soft labels) to replicating its intermediate feature representations. The technique has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing for compressing large language models like BERT, and in computer vision for tasks such as object detection and image classification. Advanced distillation frameworks include using ensembles of teachers, adversarial training schemes, and self-distillation, where a model learns from its own past predictions. Furthermore, knowledge distillation is a key enabler for collaborative learning paradigms like federated learning, allowing knowledge transfer between heterogeneous devices.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique designed to create smaller, more efficient deep learning models. This process involves training a compact "student" model to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, this paradigm facilitates the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. The technique has proven to be highly versatile, finding successful applications across a wide range of domains including natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the creation of lightweight yet powerful neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a prominent and versatile paradigm for model compression in deep learning. This technique operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to create compact, fast models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a substantial loss in performance. By transferring the rich, generalized knowledge learned by the teacher, the student can achieve high accuracy. The applications of knowledge distillation have expanded beyond simple compression to include performance enhancement, knowledge transfer across different domains, and improving model robustness and interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique to address the challenges posed by the increasing size and complexity of deep learning models. This method involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, more cumbersome 'teacher' model. The goal is to transfer the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the creation of compact, fast models that retain high performance. This makes state-of-the-art deep learning more accessible for deployment in resource-constrained or latency-sensitive environments, such as mobile devices. The technique has proven successful and versatile across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of compact, efficient models suitable for real-world deployment. Operating on a teacher-student paradigm, it involves transferring knowledge from a large, complex model to a smaller one. This process reduces the computational and memory footprint of the student model, allowing powerful architectures to run on resource-constrained devices. While initially conceived for compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, not only to create smaller models but also to enhance performance, improve generalization, and enable novel capabilities like cross-modal learning.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Perry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique used to create smaller, more efficient deep learning models from larger, complex ones. This process utilizes a teacher-student framework where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge acquired by the teacher, this method facilitates the deployment of powerful artificial intelligence systems on resource-constrained devices that have limited computational power and memory. The applications of this versatile framework extend beyond simple model size reduction, often contributing to performance enhancement and making state-of-the-art AI more practical and accessible for real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Model Compression Technique
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in real-world applications, particularly in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile model compression technique to address this issue. This method employs a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, this process enables the creation of compact, high-performance models that are suitable for devices with limited computational power or strict latency requirements. The applications of this technique are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and beyond, making it a critical tool for operationalizing state-of-the-art artificial intelligence.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Preserving Privacy in Federated Learning with Ensemble Cross-Domain Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Federated Learning (FL) is a machine learning paradigm where local nodes collaboratively train a central model while the training data remains decentralized. Existing FL methods typically share model parameters or employ co-distillation to address the issue of unbalanced data distribution. However, they suffer from communication bottlenecks. More importantly, they risk privacy leakage. In this work, we develop a privacy preserving and communication efficient method in a FL framework with one-shot offline knowledge distillation using unlabeled, cross-domain public data. We propose a quantized and noisy ensemble of local predictions from completely trained local models for stronger privacy guarantees without sacrificing accuracy. Based on extensive experiments on image classification and text classification tasks, we show that our privacy-preserving method outperforms baseline FL algorithms with superior performance in both accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a pivotal technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions. This process involves a teacher-student framework where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger teacher model. The primary benefit is enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, where computational power and memory are limited. The applications of this technique are widespread, spanning natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple model size reduction, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance a model's performance, transfer beneficial properties between architectures, and improve generalization.

papers_seen.author: Wells
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient neural networks. It utilizes a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to reduce the computational and memory requirements of state-of-the-art models, facilitating their deployment on resource-constrained devices like mobile phones. This process involves transferring the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, such as its output probability distributions and internal feature representations, to the student. The applications of this versatile framework extend beyond simple compression to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling knowledge transfer in privacy-preserving scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning, enabling the creation of smaller, more efficient models suitable for resource-constrained environments. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and internal representations of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. While its primary application is to reduce computational and memory requirements without significant performance degradation, the utility of knowledge distillation has expanded considerably. It is now used to enhance model performance, transfer knowledge across different data modalities, improve model interpretability, and adapt large-scale models for specific downstream tasks in domains like natural language processing and computer vision. This versatility makes knowledge distillation a foundational strategy for developing practical and effective artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Ramos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: More Than Just Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. It involves transferring knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, the 'student'. While the initial goal was to reduce the computational and memory footprint of models for deployment on resource-constrained devices, the application and understanding of knowledge distillation have significantly evolved. Modern approaches now leverage distillation not only for compression but also to enhance student model performance, enable training in data-scarce or private environments, and improve the robustness of learning. Advanced methods distill information from intermediate layers, attention mechanisms, and even from the student model itself in a process called self-distillation. This demonstrates that knowledge distillation is a versatile and fundamental framework for optimizing and improving deep learning models across a wide range of tasks and constraints.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, the 'student'. This process enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. The fundamental approach involves training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs, but numerous variations have been developed to enhance this process. These include distilling knowledge from intermediate feature representations, using multiple teachers for domain adaptation or multi-task learning, and applying distillation in specialized areas like object detection and graph neural networks. Advanced methods address challenges such as the absence of training data, the propagation of model biases, and applications in privacy-preserving federated learning. By leveraging knowledge from more capable models, distillation significantly improves the performance of compact networks across a wide range of tasks in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Cooke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary objective is to create lightweight models that maintain high performance while reducing computational and memory requirements, which is crucial for deployment in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. The process typically involves training the student model to mimic the behavior of the teacher, often by learning from its rich output probability distributions or intermediate feature representations. This versatile framework has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and has been extended to address challenges in areas such as data privacy and domain adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression paradigm where a compact "student" network learns from a larger "teacher" network. This technique facilitates the deployment of complex deep learning models in settings with limited computational resources. The process involves transferring knowledge through various mechanisms, including mimicking the teacher's final outputs, aligning intermediate feature representations, or preserving relational knowledge. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse fields such as natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition. Beyond simple compression, this framework can be used for more advanced purposes, including transferring specific properties like adversarial robustness or inductive biases between different model architectures. It also enables novel applications like cross-modal learning and improving models in federated learning environments.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Gaines
papers_seen.title: AdaBERT: Task-Adaptive BERT Compression with Differentiable Neural Architecture Search
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained language models such as BERT have shown their effectiveness in various natural language processing tasks. However, the huge parameter size makes them difficult to be deployed in real-time applications that require quick inference with limited resources. Existing methods compress BERT into small models while such compression is task-independent, i.e., the same compressed BERT for all different downstream tasks. Motivated by the necessity and benefits of task-oriented BERT compression, we propose a novel compression method, AdaBERT, that leverages differentiable Neural Architecture Search to automatically compress BERT into task-adaptive small models for specific tasks. We incorporate a task-oriented knowledge distillation loss to provide search hints and an efficiency-aware loss as search constraints, which enables a good trade-off between efficiency and effectiveness for task-adaptive BERT compression. We evaluate AdaBERT on several NLP tasks, and the results demonstrate that those task-adaptive compressed models are 12.7x to 29.3x faster than BERT in inference time and 11.5x to 17.0x smaller in terms of parameter size, while comparable performance is maintained.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression paradigm designed to create efficient, lightweight "student" deep learning models by transferring knowledge from larger, more powerful "teacher" models. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art networks in resource-constrained environments. The methods for knowledge transfer have evolved from matching output probabilities to more sophisticated techniques that focus on mimicking intermediate feature representations. Innovations in the field include adversarial training frameworks, the application of automated machine learning for architecture search, and even teacher-free approaches that leverage self-distillation as a form of regularization. Knowledge distillation has demonstrated significant success across a wide range of applications, including the compression of large language models in natural language processing, the simplification of complex graph neural networks, and the optimization of models in federated learning and speech recognition systems.

papers_seen.author: Boyd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: More Than a Model Compression Technique
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical framework in deep learning, initially designed for model compression. This process involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model, enabling the deployment of powerful artificial intelligence on resource-constrained devices. However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond creating smaller and faster models. It has evolved into a versatile tool for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and addressing complex challenges such as data privacy and federated learning. Its adaptability has led to widespread adoption and the development of advanced methods, establishing it as a foundational technique for creating more efficient, practical, and robust AI systems across various domains.

The applications of knowledge distillation are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and healthcare. Beyond simple output matching, advanced methods focus on transferring knowledge from intermediate feature representations and using adversarial techniques to improve the student's learning process. This versatility makes knowledge distillation a crucial tool for optimizing and deploying state-of-the-art neural networks in real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile model compression technique in deep learning. It addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from a large 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process allows the student to achieve high performance with a significantly reduced footprint, making advanced AI practical for applications on devices like mobile phones. papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Apprentice: Using Knowledge Distillation Techniques To Improve Low-Precision Network Accuracy
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a significant loss in performance. The core idea involves training the student not only on the ground-truth data but also using the outputs or intermediate representations of the trained teacher as a richer, soft target. This method has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and recommender systems, leading to a wide range of lightweight models that retain the capabilities of their larger counterparts.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers with Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we study the problem of unifying knowledge from a set of classifiers with different architectures and target classes into a single classifier, given only a generic set of unlabelled data. We call this problem Unifying Heterogeneous Classifiers (UHC). This problem is motivated by scenarios where data is collected from multiple sources, but the sources cannot share their data, e.g., due to privacy concerns, and only privately trained models can be shared. In addition, each source may not be able to gather data to train all classes due to data availability at each source, and may not be able to train the same classification model due to different computational resources. To tackle this problem, we propose a generalisation of knowledge distillation to merge HCs. We derive a probabilistic relation between the outputs of HCs and the probability over all classes. Based on this relation, we propose two classes of methods based on cross-entropy minimisation and matrix factorisation, which allow us to estimate soft labels over all classes from unlabelled samples and use them in lieu of ground truth labels to train a unified classifier. Our extensive experiments on ImageNet, LSUN, and Places365 datasets show that our approaches significantly outperform a naive extension of distillation and can achieve almost the same accuracy as classifiers that are trained in a centralised, supervised manner.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous domains, but their large size and computational expense often hinder deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and effective model compression technique to address this challenge. The process involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher's predictions or internal representations, the student can achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters. The utility of this framework has expanded beyond simple compression, proving effective for enhancing model performance, transferring specific capabilities like adversarial robustness, and even mitigating societal biases within language models. Advanced methods such as self-distillation, online distillation, and data-free approaches further increase its versatility, making it a critical tool for developing efficient and practical AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm designed to create efficient, lightweight deep learning models. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller "student" model is trained to mimic the behavior and knowledge of a larger, more powerful "teacher" model. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art networks, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. Methodologies for knowledge transfer have evolved from matching output probabilities to more advanced techniques that focus on intermediate feature representations. This versatile technique has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including computer vision, natural language processing, and graph-based learning, demonstrating its effectiveness beyond simple compression to enhance overall model performance.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Compressing Large Neural Networks for Practical Applications
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, offer a promising solution by transferring knowledge from a large, powerful 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the creation of compact networks that retain much of the performance of their larger counterparts. Innovations in this field have led to advanced methods, including adversarial training frameworks that adaptively measure the discrepancy between models, and data-free approaches that preserve privacy by eliminating the need for the original training dataset. These developments extend the applicability of state-of-the-art models to a wider range of practical scenarios, from mobile devices to embedded systems, across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenges posed by large, computationally expensive models. This method operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and replicate the knowledge of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to create lightweight models that retain high performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. The applications of this versatile framework are extensive, spanning domains like natural language processing and computer vision, and advanced methods have extended its utility to enhance model robustness, facilitate privacy-preserving learning, and improve generalization.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary objective is to reduce computational and memory requirements, enabling the deployment of powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining high performance. This is typically achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, often using its output probabilities as supervisory signals. The technique has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework used to enhance model performance, facilitate privacy-preserving distributed learning, and adapt models to new domains.

papers_seen.author: Murphy
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that operates on a teacher-student paradigm. This process involves training a smaller, computationally efficient student model to mimic the behavior and internal representations of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to reduce computational and memory requirements, enabling the deployment of complex models on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. Beyond compression, the utility of this framework has expanded considerably. It is now widely used to enhance model performance, transfer knowledge across different domains, improve model robustness, and adapt large-scale models for specialized tasks in natural language processing and computer vision, making it a foundational tool for developing practical and efficient AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models in Natural Language Processing (NLP), have achieved state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and slow for practical deployment. Model compression techniques are essential for creating smaller, more efficient models. Knowledge distillation is a popular compression paradigm where a compact "student" model learns from a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process involves transferring the teacher's knowledge, often through its output probabilities or internal representations, to guide the student's training. Advanced methods have emerged, including multi-teacher distillation, self-distillation, and data-free approaches that work without the original training data. Knowledge distillation can also be combined with other compression methods like pruning and quantization to further enhance model efficiency, making powerful deep learning models accessible for resource-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Powers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful machine learning technique for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. This process involves training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The core idea is to transfer the generalized knowledge learned by the teacher, which is often encoded in its output probabilities, to the student. This allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices or applications with strict latency requirements. The applications of knowledge distillation are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and graph-based learning. Beyond simple model compression, distillation has been shown to improve the accuracy of student models, facilitate domain adaptation, and enable training even when the original data is unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient neural networks. This method operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to reduce computational and memory requirements, enabling the deployment of large models in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. This versatile approach has proven effective across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its applications extend beyond simple compression to performance enhancement and knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for creating compact, efficient models by transferring knowledge from a large 'teacher' model to a smaller 'student' model. Originally developed for model compression to enable the deployment of complex neural networks on resource-constrained devices, its applications have expanded significantly. The process not only creates smaller and faster models that retain the teacher's performance but can also enhance the student model's generalization and robustness. This versatile framework is now used to address a wide range of challenges, including federated learning, data privacy, and improving performance on specific downstream tasks in domains like Natural Language Processing and computer vision, solidifying its role as a foundational tool for developing practical and powerful AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm where a compact "student" model is trained to reproduce the performance of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This technique addresses the challenge of deploying computationally intensive deep learning networks on resource-constrained devices. The process involves transferring knowledge from the teacher to the student, often by using the teacher's output probabilities as soft labels or by mimicking its internal feature representations. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing for tasks like machine translation and language model compression, and in computer vision for object detection and image generation. Advanced applications of this framework include enhancing model robustness, preserving privacy in federated learning, and enabling data-free model training.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Private Model Compression via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The soaring demand for intelligent mobile applications calls for deploying powerful deep neural networks (DNNs) on mobile devices. However, the outstanding performance of DNNs notoriously relies on increasingly complex models, which in turn is associated with an increase in computational expense far surpassing mobile devices' capacity. What is worse, app service providers need to collect and utilize a large volume of users' data, which contain sensitive information, to build the sophisticated DNN models. Directly deploying these models on public mobile devices presents prohibitive privacy risk. To benefit from the on-device deep learning without the capacity and privacy concerns, we design a private model compression framework RONA. Following the knowledge distillation paradigm, we jointly use hint learning, distillation learning, and self learning to train a compact and fast neural network. The knowledge distilled from the cumbersome model is adaptively bounded and carefully perturbed to enforce differential privacy. We further propose an elegant query sample selection method to reduce the number of queries and control the privacy loss. A series of empirical evaluations as well as the implementation on an Android mobile device show that RONA can not only compress cumbersome models efficiently but also provide a strong privacy guarantee. For example, on SVHN, when a meaningful $(9.83,10^{-6})$-differential privacy is guaranteed, the compact model trained by RONA can obtain 20$\times$ compression ratio and 19$\times$ speed-up with merely 0.97% accuracy loss.

papers_seen.author: Wolfe
papers_seen.title: Robust and Resource-Efficient Data-Free Knowledge Distillation by Generative Pseudo Replay
papers_seen.abstract: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (KD) allows knowledge transfer from a trained neural network (teacher) to a more compact one (student) in the absence of original training data. Existing works use a validation set to monitor the accuracy of the student over real data and report the highest performance throughout the entire process. However, validation data may not be available at distillation time either, making it infeasible to record the student snapshot that achieved the peak accuracy. Therefore, a practical data-free KD method should be robust and ideally provide monotonically increasing student accuracy during distillation. This is challenging because the student experiences knowledge degradation due to the distribution shift of the synthetic data. A straightforward approach to overcome this issue is to store and rehearse the generated samples periodically, which increases the memory footprint and creates privacy concerns. We propose to model the distribution of the previously observed synthetic samples with a generative network. In particular, we design a Variational Autoencoder (VAE) with a training objective that is customized to learn the synthetic data representations optimally. The student is rehearsed by the generative pseudo replay technique, with samples produced by the VAE. Hence knowledge degradation can be prevented without storing any samples. Experiments on image classification benchmarks show that our method optimizes the expected value of the distilled model accuracy while eliminating the large memory overhead incurred by the sample-storing methods.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for model compression, where a compact "student" model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, more complex "teacher" model. This process facilitates the deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, by significantly reducing their size and computational requirements. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework capable of enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and enabling novel applications across various domains. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, student models can achieve higher accuracy and robustness than they could by training on ground-truth labels alone.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Model Compression and Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large, complex deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. This process typically involves a teacher-student framework, where a smaller student model learns to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This paradigm addresses the significant computational and storage costs associated with state-of-the-art models in fields like Natural Language Processing and computer vision. Various methods have been developed to tackle challenges such as data privacy, architectural mismatches between teacher and student, and information transfer efficiency. Applications are diverse, ranging from compressing large language models and generative adversarial networks to enhancing model robustness against adversarial attacks and enabling efficient federated learning. Extensions to the basic framework include using multiple teachers, adversarial learning, and data-free distillation techniques, continually expanding the utility of this compression strategy.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful training paradigm where a smaller "student" model learns from a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. Initially conceived for model compression, this technique enables the development of lightweight, efficient neural networks that retain the high performance of their cumbersome counterparts. Beyond creating faster and smaller models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now a crucial tool for a range of tasks including domain adaptation, where models must adjust to new data distributions, and federated learning, which facilitates collaborative training across distributed devices with heterogeneous models without sharing private data. The success of distillation often depends on sophisticated strategies that go beyond simple output matching, such as aligning intermediate feature representations and leveraging statistically sound data augmentation. Despite its power, challenges in optimization remain, but knowledge distillation continues to be a versatile and impactful framework in modern deep learning.

papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: The Versatility of Knowledge Distillation in Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. It enables the creation of smaller, more efficient 'student' models by transferring knowledge from larger, more complex 'teacher' models. This process is critical for deploying state-of-the-art networks in resource-constrained environments. However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple compression. Its applications now encompass a wide range of objectives, including enhancing model interpretability, promoting algorithmic fairness, preserving data privacy in distributed learning settings, and unifying knowledge from multiple disparate models. While the process is not without its challenges, such as the potential for propagating teacher model errors, its flexibility across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision makes it a foundational and versatile tool for developing efficient, effective, and responsible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Green
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile model compression technique to address this issue. This method employs a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, this process enables the creation of compact, faster models that maintain high accuracy. The utility of knowledge distillation extends beyond simple compression, with applications in enhancing model performance, preserving data privacy in federated learning, and enabling knowledge transfer even without access to the original training data.
