papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for model compression in deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, enabling the creation of compact models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices, without a substantial loss in performance. This approach has proven effective and versatile, with broad applications across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, for both compressing models and enhancing their overall performance.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: Improved Feature Distillation via Projector Ensemble
papers_seen.abstract: In knowledge distillation, previous feature distillation methods mainly focus on the design of loss functions and the selection of the distilled layers, while the effect of the feature projector between the student and the teacher remains under-explored. In this paper, we first discuss a plausible mechanism of the projector with empirical evidence and then propose a new feature distillation method based on a projector ensemble for further performance improvement. We observe that the student network benefits from a projector even if the feature dimensions of the student and the teacher are the same. Training a student backbone without a projector can be considered as a multi-task learning process, namely achieving discriminative feature extraction for classification and feature matching between the student and the teacher for distillation at the same time. We hypothesize and empirically verify that without a projector, the student network tends to overfit the teacher's feature distributions despite having different architecture and weights initialization. This leads to degradation on the quality of the student's deep features that are eventually used in classification. Adding a projector, on the other hand, disentangles the two learning tasks and helps the student network to focus better on the main feature extraction task while still being able to utilize teacher features as a guidance through the projector. Motivated by the positive effect of the projector in feature distillation, we propose an ensemble of projectors to further improve the quality of student features. Experimental results on different datasets with a series of teacher-student pairs illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

papers_seen.author: Ryan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. The core idea involves training the student network to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher. Innovations in this field have expanded the technique's applicability, leading to methods like zero-shot distillation, which functions without access to the original training data, and self-distillation, where a model learns from its own representations. These approaches have been successfully applied to compress a wide range of models, from large-scale language models in Natural Language Processing (NLP) to complex architectures used in computer vision and multimodal tasks, demonstrating the flexibility and practical utility of knowledge distillation in creating lightweight, yet powerful, AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Releasing Graph Neural Networks with Differential Privacy Guarantees
papers_seen.abstract: With the increasing popularity of graph neural networks (GNNs) in several sensitive applications like healthcare and medicine, concerns have been raised over the privacy aspects of trained GNNs. More notably, GNNs are vulnerable to privacy attacks, such as membership inference attacks, even if only black-box access to the trained model is granted. We propose PrivGNN, a privacy-preserving framework for releasing GNN models in a centralized setting. Assuming an access to a public unlabeled graph, PrivGNN provides a framework to release GNN models trained explicitly on public data along with knowledge obtained from the private data in a privacy preserving manner. PrivGNN combines the knowledge-distillation framework with the two noise mechanisms, random subsampling, and noisy labeling, to ensure rigorous privacy guarantees. We theoretically analyze our approach in the Renyi differential privacy framework. Besides, we show the solid experimental performance of our method compared to several baselines adapted for graph-structured data. Our code is available at https://github.com/iyempissy/privGnn.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression paradigm designed to create efficient, lightweight "student" deep learning models by transferring knowledge from larger, more powerful "teacher" models. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art networks in resource-constrained environments. The methods for knowledge transfer have evolved from matching output probabilities to more sophisticated techniques that focus on mimicking intermediate feature representations. Innovations in the field include adversarial training frameworks, the application of automated machine learning for architecture search, and even teacher-free approaches that leverage self-distillation as a form of regularization. Knowledge distillation has demonstrated significant success across a wide range of applications, including the compression of large language models in natural language processing, the simplification of complex graph neural networks, and the optimization of models in federated learning and speech recognition systems.

papers_seen.author: Chambers

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models suitable for resource-constrained environments. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, the student can achieve high performance that might otherwise be unattainable. While its primary application is in reducing model size and computational cost for deployment on devices like mobile phones, the framework has proven to be highly versatile. Its applications now extend beyond simple compression to include performance enhancement, knowledge transfer across different tasks and data modalities, and addressing fairness concerns in artificial intelligence systems.

The applications of this framework extend beyond simple compression, including enhancing model performance, enabling domain adaptation, and facilitating learning in privacy-sensitive settings.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical model compression technique in deep learning and natural language processing. The method operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process facilitates the creation of compact, fast, and resource-efficient models that retain high accuracy, enabling the deployment of complex neural networks on devices with limited computational capabilities. While initially developed for model compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly, now encompassing performance enhancement, improved model robustness, and knowledge transfer across different tasks and domains, making it a multifaceted tool for developing practical and powerful artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning: A Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models suitable for resource-constrained environments. The process involves a compact "student" model learning to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich knowledge from the teacher, the student can achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer computational resources. The applications of this paradigm extend beyond simple compression, encompassing performance enhancement, improved model robustness, and enabling learning in privacy-sensitive settings. This versatility has established knowledge distillation as a fundamental tool in natural language processing, computer vision, and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Stein
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that utilizes a teacher-student framework to create smaller, more efficient models. In this process, a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model, effectively transferring its learned knowledge. The primary objective is to enable the deployment of powerful models on resource-constrained devices without significant performance degradation. This versatile paradigm has broad applications in domains such as natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simply reducing model size, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance model performance, improve generalization, and transfer complex capabilities between different architectures.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. The core concept involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process allows for the deployment of complex neural networks on resource-constrained devices by creating lightweight versions without a significant drop in accuracy. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance model performance, transfer capabilities across different model architectures or data modalities, and address challenges such as privacy in federated learning and adversarial robustness. Its applications are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and graph-based learning.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for creating compact, efficient models by transferring knowledge from a large 'teacher' model to a smaller 'student' model. Originally developed for model compression to enable the deployment of complex neural networks on resource-constrained devices, its applications have expanded significantly. The process not only creates smaller and faster models that retain the teacher's performance but can also enhance the student model's generalization and robustness. This versatile framework is now used to address a wide range of challenges, including federated learning, data privacy, and improving performance on specific downstream tasks in domains like Natural Language Processing and computer vision, solidifying its role as a foundational tool for developing practical and powerful AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Model Compression Technique in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective model compression and training paradigm in which a compact 'student' model learns to mimic a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to transfer the knowledge from the high-performing teacher to the student, enabling the creation of smaller, faster, and more efficient models that are suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. This knowledge transfer can occur in various forms, from mimicking the teacher's final output probabilities (soft labels) to replicating its intermediate feature representations. The technique has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing for compressing large language models like BERT, and in computer vision for tasks such as object detection and image classification. Advanced distillation frameworks include using ensembles of teachers, adversarial training schemes, and self-distillation, where a model learns from its own past predictions. Furthermore, knowledge distillation is a key enabler for collaborative learning paradigms like federated learning, allowing knowledge transfer between heterogeneous devices.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Compressing Deep Learning Models for Enhanced Efficiency
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning and natural language processing. It facilitates the creation of compact, efficient 'student' models by transferring knowledge from larger, more complex 'teacher' models. This process allows for the deployment of powerful neural networks on devices with limited computational and storage resources, such as mobile phones. Various distillation strategies have been developed, including methods that function without access to the original training data, thereby addressing privacy and data availability concerns. By mimicking the outputs or intermediate representations of a teacher model, the student network can achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller footprint, making it a versatile tool for optimizing deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to transfer the rich knowledge from the teacher, thereby creating a compact model that retains high performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. This enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated through its application across diverse tasks and the continuous development of advanced methods that go beyond simple output matching, solidifying its role in making advanced artificial intelligence more practical and accessible.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: As deep learning models grow in size and complexity, their deployment in resource-constrained environments becomes a significant challenge. Model compression techniques are essential for creating smaller, faster, and more efficient models without substantial performance degradation. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for this purpose. It involves transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome 'teacher' model to a smaller 'student' model. The student learns to mimic the rich output distributions of the teacher, thereby inheriting its performance capabilities while maintaining a much smaller footprint. This approach has proven effective across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the use of state-of-the-art architectures in practical, real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: The Versatility of Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of state-of-the-art deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, have emerged as a powerful solution. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. Knowledge distillation has proven to be a highly versatile and effective method, extending far beyond simple model size reduction for classification tasks. Its applications span diverse domains such as natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning. The framework is adaptable, enabling knowledge transfer between models of different architectures, across different data modalities, and even in scenarios with limited or no access to the original training data. This demonstrates its crucial role in making advanced AI models more practical and accessible for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful machine learning technique focused on transferring knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the teacher, to a smaller, more efficient model, called the student. Originally conceived for model compression, this process allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by creating smaller, faster versions that retain much of the original's performance. The applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly beyond simple compression. It is now used to improve the absolute performance of student models, sometimes even allowing them to outperform their teachers. Furthermore, the technique has been adapted to address challenges in diverse areas such as federated learning, data privacy, and multimodal learning. By leveraging the learned representations of a teacher, knowledge distillation provides a flexible framework for creating more practical, robust, and capable models across various domains, particularly in Natural Language Processing (NLP).

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions suitable for real-world deployment. This process involves a smaller "student" model learning from a larger "teacher" model, transferring knowledge beyond simple labels. Originally conceived for model compression, its applications have expanded significantly across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Research shows that distillation not only reduces model size and inference time but can also enhance the student model's performance, sometimes even surpassing models trained from scratch. Advanced methods like self-distillation and data-free distillation further broaden its utility, making it a crucial tool for developing practical and effective deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Ashley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. This teacher-student paradigm enables the deployment of powerful neural networks on resource-constrained devices by significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. The process involves training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs, which provides richer supervisory signals than traditional training labels alone. The versatility of this framework extends beyond simple compression, with applications in enhancing model performance, improving fairness, and enabling novel learning paradigms like privacy-preserving machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm where a compact "student" model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process facilitates the deployment of powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their size and computational requirements. The technique has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, for tasks ranging from text generation to image classification. The core principle involves transferring the knowledge embedded in the teacher's outputs or internal representations to the student. Advanced variations of this technique have emerged, such as data-free distillation for scenarios with private data, self-distillation where a model learns from itself, and ensemble distillation using multiple teachers. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation can also be used to improve a model's performance, transfer specific capabilities like adversarial robustness, and create more efficient and generalizable models.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large, complex deep learning models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This process involves a "teacher-student" paradigm, where a smaller student network learns to mimic the outputs or internal representations of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve comparable performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. This makes it possible to deploy state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as on mobile devices or for latency-sensitive applications. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing, where it is used to create compact language models, and computer vision, for tasks like object detection and image classification. Research continues to explore novel distillation methods, including data-free approaches and cross-architecture knowledge transfer, further enhancing its flexibility and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Model Compression and Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a key technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large, complex deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. This process involves transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained "teacher" model to a smaller "student" model, aiming to replicate the teacher's performance with significantly fewer computational resources. This approach is applied across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, to create models that are smaller, faster, and more efficient. Research has explored numerous variations, such as self-distillation, multi-teacher distillation, and data-free methods that address challenges like data privacy and availability. Knowledge distillation is often combined with other compression techniques like pruning and quantization to further optimize model efficiency, striking a balance between performance and practicality.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a critical technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. This process involves training a smaller, efficient "student" model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. The primary goal is to transfer the teacher's knowledge, enabling the creation of compact models that maintain high performance while reducing computational and memory demands. This facilitates the deployment of advanced AI on resource-constrained devices. The applications of this versatile framework extend beyond simple compression to include performance enhancement, improved generalization, and enabling complex learning scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Brennan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly large language and vision models, have achieved state-of-the-art performance but are often computationally expensive and memory-intensive, hindering their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Model compression techniques address this challenge by creating smaller, more efficient models without significant performance degradation. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible method for this purpose. This process involves training a compact "student" network to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" network. By transferring the rich "dark knowledge" from the teacher, such as class relationship information or intermediate feature representations, the student model can achieve performance comparable to its larger counterpart. This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, demonstrating its versatility in making advanced AI more accessible and practical.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student can achieve comparable performance with significantly reduced computational and memory footprints, making it suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. The applications of this technique extend beyond simple compression, encompassing performance enhancement, domain generalization, and knowledge transfer across different tasks and modalities, establishing it as a multifaceted tool in modern machine learning.

This method employs a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to create compact, fast models suitable for resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a significant loss in performance. The applications of this framework are widespread, spanning natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple size reduction, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance model performance, improve robustness, and facilitate knowledge transfer across different tasks and modalities.

papers_seen.author: Robinson
papers_seen.title: Towards Understanding Ensemble, Knowledge Distillation and Self-Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: We formally study how ensemble of deep learning models can improve test accuracy, and how the superior performance of ensemble can be distilled into a single model using knowledge distillation. We consider the challenging case where the ensemble is simply an average of the outputs of a few independently trained neural networks with the SAME architecture, trained using the SAME algorithm on the SAME data set, and they only differ by the random seeds used in the initialization.   We show that ensemble/knowledge distillation in Deep Learning works very differently from traditional learning theory (such as boosting or NTKs, neural tangent kernels). To properly understand them, we develop a theory showing that when data has a structure we refer to as ``multi-view'', then ensemble of independently trained neural networks can provably improve test accuracy, and such superior test accuracy can also be provably distilled into a single model by training a single model to match the output of the ensemble instead of the true label. Our result sheds light on how ensemble works in deep learning in a way that is completely different from traditional theorems, and how the ``dark knowledge'' is hidden in the outputs of the ensemble and can be used in distillation. In the end, we prove that self-distillation can also be viewed as implicitly combining ensemble and knowledge distillation to improve test accuracy.

The primary goal is to retain the high performance of the teacher while significantly reducing its computational and memory footprint, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures on resource-constrained devices. The applications for this versatile technique are widespread, spanning natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple size reduction, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance model performance, improve generalization, and transfer knowledge in privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, the 'student'. This process enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. The fundamental approach involves training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs, but numerous variations have been developed to enhance this process. These include distilling knowledge from intermediate feature representations, using multiple teachers for domain adaptation or multi-task learning, and applying distillation in specialized areas like object detection and graph neural networks. Advanced methods address challenges such as the absence of training data, the propagation of model biases, and applications in privacy-preserving federated learning. By leveraging knowledge from more capable models, distillation significantly improves the performance of compact networks across a wide range of tasks in natural language processing and computer vision.

The primary objective is to enable the deployment of powerful models on resource-constrained devices without significant performance degradation. This versatile paradigm has broad applications in domains such as natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simply reducing model size, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance model performance, improve generalization, and transfer complex capabilities between different architectures.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning networks have achieved state-of-the-art accuracies on computer vision workloads like image classification and object detection. The performant systems, however, typically involve big models with numerous parameters. Once trained, a challenging aspect for such top performing models is deployment on resource constrained inference systems - the models (often deep networks or wide networks or both) are compute and memory intensive. Low-precision numerics and model compression using knowledge distillation are popular techniques to lower both the compute requirements and memory footprint of these deployed models. In this paper, we study the combination of these two techniques and show that the performance of low-precision networks can be significantly improved by using knowledge distillation techniques. Our approach, Apprentice, achieves state-of-the-art accuracies using ternary precision and 4-bit precision for variants of ResNet architecture on ImageNet dataset. We present three schemes using which one can apply knowledge distillation techniques to various stages of the train-and-deploy pipeline.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that enables the creation of compact, efficient models from larger, more complex ones. Operating on a teacher-student paradigm, this process involves training a smaller student model to replicate the behavior and performance of a pre-trained teacher network. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art models, enabling their deployment on resource-constrained devices like mobile phones. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple compression, the technique has also proven effective for enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and transferring complex capabilities between models.

papers_seen.author: Whitehead
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique in deep learning, initially designed for model compression. This process involves training a compact "student" model to replicate the behavior of a larger, more powerful "teacher" model, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art networks in resource-constrained environments. Beyond creating smaller and faster models, the paradigm has evolved significantly. It now serves as a versatile framework for a wide range of tasks, including improving model interpretability, enabling training without access to original data, enhancing generalization, and facilitating collaborative learning in federated settings. This demonstrates that knowledge distillation is not just a compression tool but a foundational method for making advanced artificial intelligence more practical, adaptable, and widely applicable.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Shaw
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. The core concept involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process allows for the deployment of complex neural networks on resource-constrained devices by creating lightweight versions without a significant drop in accuracy. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance model performance, transfer capabilities across different model architectures or data modalities, and address challenges such as privacy in federated learning and adversarial robustness. Its applications are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and graph-based learning.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a key technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large, complex deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. This process involves transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained "teacher" model to a smaller "student" model, aiming to replicate the teacher's performance with significantly fewer computational resources. This approach is applied across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, to create models that are smaller, faster, and more efficient. Research has explored numerous variations, such as self-distillation, multi-teacher distillation, and data-free methods that address challenges like data privacy and availability. Knowledge distillation is often combined with other compression techniques like pruning and quantization to further optimize model efficiency, striking a balance between performance and practicality.

The primary goal is to create lightweight, efficient models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. This is achieved by training the student to mimic the rich output distributions or internal representations of the teacher. Beyond model compression, this paradigm has been adapted for a wide range of applications, including enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling knowledge transfer in privacy-sensitive or data-scarce scenarios. Its flexibility has made it a foundational tool in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Nelson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to transfer the rich knowledge from the teacher to the student, enabling the creation of compact, high-performance models suitable for resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. While initially focused on reducing model size and latency, the applications of this technique have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and transferring complex knowledge across various domains such as natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models have achieved unprecedented performance but their immense size and computational cost often hinder practical deployment. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression framework to address this challenge. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer resources. This makes it possible to deploy state-of-the-art models on devices with limited computational power, such as mobile phones. The technique's versatility is demonstrated by its broad application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its adaptation into advanced methods like self-distillation and data-free distillation, further expanding its utility in developing efficient and robust AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Molina
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance but their large size often prevents deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique to address this issue. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller computational footprint. Beyond compression, this versatile framework can also enhance model performance and generalization. Its applications are widespread across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it a crucial tool for creating practical and deployable artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique that addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive deep learning models in real-world applications. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, this process facilitates the creation of compact yet powerful models suitable for resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. The utility of this framework extends beyond mere compression, encompassing applications in performance enhancement, knowledge transfer in data-private scenarios, and improving model robustness, making it a crucial tool in modern AI.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.

papers_seen.author: Spears
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a pivotal technique in deep learning for creating compact and efficient models. It involves transferring knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. While initially developed for model compression to enable deployment on resource-constrained devices, its applications have expanded significantly. The technique is now used to enhance the performance and generalization of student models, sometimes surpassing their original training capabilities. Its versatility is demonstrated through its successful application in diverse and complex scenarios, including federated learning across heterogeneous devices, non-autoregressive machine translation, and domain adaptation. Advanced distillation methods have evolved to transfer richer forms of knowledge and address challenges in the learning process, solidifying its role as a foundational tool for developing practical and powerful artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective model compression technique that facilitates the deployment of large, complex deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, including its understanding of data structure and inter-class relationships, the student model can achieve performance far superior to what it could by training on the data alone. This approach has proven successful across various domains, including natural language processing, speech recognition, and computer vision, enabling the creation of compact models that are faster and require less memory without a significant drop in accuracy. The flexibility of knowledge distillation allows it to be combined with other techniques like data augmentation and federated learning, extending its applicability to diverse and challenging scenarios such as privacy-preservation and few-shot learning.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Collaborative Distillation for Ultra-Resolution Universal Style Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Universal style transfer methods typically leverage rich representations from deep Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) models (e.g., VGG-19) pre-trained on large collections of images. Despite the effectiveness, its application is heavily constrained by the large model size to handle ultra-resolution images given limited memory. In this work, we present a new knowledge distillation method (named Collaborative Distillation) for encoder-decoder based neural style transfer to reduce the convolutional filters. The main idea is underpinned by a finding that the encoder-decoder pairs construct an exclusive collaborative relationship, which is regarded as a new kind of knowledge for style transfer models. Moreover, to overcome the feature size mismatch when applying collaborative distillation, a linear embedding loss is introduced to drive the student network to learn a linear embedding of the teacher's features. Extensive experiments show the effectiveness of our method when applied to different universal style transfer approaches (WCT and AdaIN), even if the model size is reduced by 15.5 times. Especially, on WCT with the compressed models, we achieve ultra-resolution (over 40 megapixels) universal style transfer on a 12GB GPU for the first time. Further experiments on optimization-based stylization scheme show the generality of our algorithm on different stylization paradigms. Our code and trained models are available at https://github.com/mingsun-tse/collaborative-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective and Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression in deep learning. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory requirements of state-of-the-art models, facilitating their deployment on resource-constrained devices such as mobile phones. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve high performance while being significantly more compact. The applications of this versatile framework extend beyond simple compression, proving useful for enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and enabling complex learning scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments. The method operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient "student" model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process transfers the rich knowledge from the teacher, enabling the creation of compact, fast models that retain high performance. While its primary use is to reduce model size, the framework's versatility extends to enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and transferring knowledge across different domains and architectures. Its successful application in fields like natural language processing and computer vision makes it a crucial tool for developing practical, real-world AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Mckee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model to a smaller, more efficient one. This teacher-student learning paradigm enables the deployment of powerful models in resource-constrained environments by significantly reducing their computational and memory requirements. The process involves training the compact student model to mimic the behavior of the pre-trained teacher, often by using the teacher's output probabilities or internal feature representations as a supervisory signal. This allows the student to learn richer, more nuanced information than it would from ground-truth labels alone. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing and computer vision, and its utility extends beyond compression to include performance enhancement, regularization, and cross-modal knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful machine learning technique focused on transferring knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the teacher, to a smaller, more efficient model, called the student. Originally conceived for model compression, this process allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by creating smaller, faster versions that retain much of the original's performance. The applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly beyond simple compression. It is now used to improve the absolute performance of student models, sometimes even allowing them to outperform their teachers. Furthermore, the technique has been adapted to address challenges in diverse areas such as federated learning, data privacy, and multimodal learning. By leveraging the learned representations of a teacher, knowledge distillation provides a flexible framework for creating more practical, robust, and capable models across various domains, particularly in Natural Language Processing (NLP).

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The primary objective is to create compact models that retain the high performance of the teacher, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. This is typically achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs or internal feature representations. While initially conceived for compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. The framework is now used to enhance student model performance, sometimes even surpassing the teacher, and to address critical considerations like algorithmic fairness and data privacy. Its versatility has led to successful applications across diverse domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, establishing it as a multifaceted tool in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large, state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This process involves training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The core principle is to transfer the nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, often encapsulated in its soft predictions, to the more compact student network. This approach has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to compress models like large language transformers and generative adversarial networks. Advanced methods have been developed that utilize multiple teachers, distill knowledge from intermediate layers, and even operate in data-free settings to address privacy concerns. Furthermore, knowledge distillation plays a crucial role in communication-efficient frameworks like federated learning, demonstrating its versatility and importance in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly in fields like natural language processing, have grown significantly in size and computational cost, posing challenges for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Model compression aims to create smaller, more efficient models while retaining high performance. Knowledge distillation is a prominent compression paradigm where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger 'teacher' model. This approach transfers the learned knowledge of the teacher, enabling the smaller student to achieve better performance than if trained alone. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, with research exploring advanced techniques such as transferring knowledge from intermediate layers, using multiple teachers, and performing distillation without access to the original training data.

papers_seen.author: Lin

It enables the creation of small, efficient "student" models by transferring knowledge from large, complex "teacher" models, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. While its primary use is to reduce computational and memory footprints, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It has evolved into a versatile framework used not only for creating compact models but also for enhancing model performance, improving interpretability, and enabling novel forms of knowledge transfer across different domains, modalities, and architectures. This demonstrates its crucial role in developing more practical, robust, and capable artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Bryant

It employs a teacher-student framework where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and inherit the knowledge of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process enables the creation of compact, high-performance models suitable for devices with limited computational power or strict latency requirements. The applications of this technique are broad, spanning natural language processing and computer vision, bridging the gap between state-of-the-art research and practical application.
