papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Cooke
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary objective is to create lightweight models that maintain high performance while reducing computational and memory requirements, which is crucial for deployment in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. The process typically involves training the student model to mimic the behavior of the teacher, often by learning from its rich output probability distributions or intermediate feature representations. This versatile framework has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and has been extended to address challenges in areas such as data privacy and domain adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Zavala
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique in deep learning for model compression. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. By transferring the rich, nuanced information captured by the teacher, such as output probabilities and intermediate feature representations, the student model can achieve high accuracy. The utility of knowledge distillation extends beyond simple compression, serving as a powerful framework for enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and transferring complex capabilities across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Garrison
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental and powerful technique in deep learning, primarily aimed at model compression. This method operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The core objective is to create compact, computationally inexpensive models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. By transferring the nuanced knowledge from a teacher's internal representations or output probabilities, the student can achieve superior performance than by learning from data alone. The applications of this versatile framework extend beyond simple compression, proving effective in enhancing model robustness, transferring knowledge in data-scarce scenarios, and improving performance across a wide range of domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large, complex deep learning models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This process involves a "teacher-student" paradigm, where a smaller student network learns to mimic the outputs or internal representations of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve comparable performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. This makes it possible to deploy state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as on mobile devices or for latency-sensitive applications. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing, where it is used to create compact language models, and computer vision, for tasks like object detection and image classification. Research continues to explore novel distillation methods, including data-free approaches and cross-architecture knowledge transfer, further enhancing its flexibility and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

papers_seen.author: Frost
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile technique for compressing large, complex deep learning models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. The process typically involves a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model that transfers its learned knowledge to a smaller 'student' model. By training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, often through its output probabilities or intermediate feature representations, the smaller model can achieve high performance that would be unattainable by training on data alone. This approach is critical for deploying state-of-the-art models, particularly in natural language processing, on resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. The applications of knowledge distillation are broad, extending beyond simple compression to areas like domain adaptation, privacy preservation, and overall performance enhancement.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful training paradigm where a smaller "student" model learns from a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. Initially conceived for model compression, this technique enables the development of lightweight, efficient neural networks that retain the high performance of their cumbersome counterparts. Beyond creating faster and smaller models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now a crucial tool for a range of tasks including domain adaptation, where models must adjust to new data distributions, and federated learning, which facilitates collaborative training across distributed devices with heterogeneous models without sharing private data. The success of distillation often depends on sophisticated strategies that go beyond simple output matching, such as aligning intermediate feature representations and leveraging statistically sound data augmentation. Despite its power, challenges in optimization remain, but knowledge distillation continues to be a versatile and impactful framework in modern deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Henson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: As deep learning models increase in size and complexity, their deployment in real-world, resource-constrained applications has become a significant challenge. Model compression techniques aim to create smaller, faster, and more efficient models without substantial performance degradation. Among these techniques, knowledge distillation has emerged as a particularly powerful and flexible paradigm. It employs a teacher-student framework where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model, thereby inheriting its learned knowledge. While its primary application is to reduce model size for environments with limited computational resources, the utility of knowledge distillation extends further. This technique has been shown to improve model performance, enhance interpretability, and facilitate knowledge transfer across different domains and architectures, making it an indispensable tool in modern deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The primary goal is to retain the high performance of the teacher while reducing the computational and memory footprint of the student, making it suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This paradigm has been successfully applied across diverse fields, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning. By learning from the teacher's output distributions, the student model can achieve significant performance gains compared to training from scratch, effectively enabling the practical use of state-of-the-art but cumbersome deep learning architectures.

papers_seen.author: Blair
papers_seen.title: Distilling Policy Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The transfer of knowledge from one policy to another is an important tool in Deep Reinforcement Learning. This process, referred to as distillation, has been used to great success, for example, by enhancing the optimisation of agents, leading to stronger performance faster, on harder domains [26, 32, 5, 8]. Despite the widespread use and conceptual simplicity of distillation, many different formulations are used in practice, and the subtle variations between them can often drastically change the performance and the resulting objective that is being optimised. In this work, we rigorously explore the entire landscape of policy distillation, comparing the motivations and strengths of each variant through theoretical and empirical analysis. Our results point to three distillation techniques, that are preferred depending on specifics of the task. Specifically a newly proposed expected entropy regularised distillation allows for quicker learning in a wide range of situations, while still guaranteeing convergence.

papers_seen.author: Daniel
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Adversarial Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) has made remarkable progress in the last few years and become a popular paradigm for model compression and knowledge transfer. However, almost all existing KD algorithms are data-driven, i.e., relying on a large amount of original training data or alternative data, which is usually unavailable in real-world scenarios. In this paper, we devote ourselves to this challenging problem and propose a novel adversarial distillation mechanism to craft a compact student model without any real-world data. We introduce a model discrepancy to quantificationally measure the difference between student and teacher models and construct an optimizable upper bound. In our work, the student and the teacher jointly act the role of the discriminator to reduce this discrepancy, when a generator adversarially produces some "hard samples" to enlarge it. Extensive experiments demonstrate that the proposed data-free method yields comparable performance to existing data-driven methods. More strikingly, our approach can be directly extended to semantic segmentation, which is more complicated than classification, and our approach achieves state-of-the-art results. Code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/VainF/Data-Free-Adversarial-Distillation.

papers_seen.author: Robbins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and computationally expensive for practical deployment. Knowledge distillation addresses this challenge by enabling the creation of smaller, more efficient models. This process involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model learns to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge from the teacher, the student can achieve comparable or even superior performance with a significantly smaller footprint. This technique has proven highly adaptable, with successful applications in natural language processing and computer vision, bridging the gap between cutting-edge research and deployment in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Kidd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful paradigm in deep learning for compressing large, computationally expensive models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. This process involves a "student" model learning to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By training on the soft probability distributions or intermediate feature representations produced by the teacher, the student model can learn richer information and achieve better generalization than if it were trained solely on hard labels. This technique extends beyond simple model compression, enabling the transfer of inductive biases, performance improvements through self-distillation, and the unification of knowledge from multiple models. Its applications are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and privacy-preserving federated learning, making it a crucial tool for deploying state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. This process involves a teacher-student framework where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, cumbersome teacher model. The primary objective is to enable the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments by reducing computational and memory demands without a substantial loss in performance. However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple model compression. It has evolved into a versatile paradigm for addressing complex challenges such as domain adaptation, continual learning, and privacy preservation. By transferring knowledge in various forms, from output probabilities to intermediate feature representations, this framework enhances model efficiency, robustness, and adaptability across a wide range of applications in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Figueroa
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique in deep learning to address the deployment challenges of large, computationally expensive models. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. Beyond simple model size reduction, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include performance enhancement, privacy preservation, and the transfer of specific model capabilities, establishing it as a versatile and powerful tool for optimizing and deploying state-of-the-art neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of modern deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a highly effective model compression technique to address this issue. This method involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student can achieve high performance while being significantly smaller and faster. Initially developed for compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded, making it a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling advanced learning paradigms. This process successfully bridges the gap between state-of-the-art performance and practical deployability.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and computational complexity of state-of-the-art deep learning models present significant challenges for their deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile model compression technique to address this issue. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process enables the creation of compact, fast, and energy-efficient models that retain high performance. Beyond simple model size reduction, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include performance enhancement, knowledge transfer across different data modalities, and improving model robustness and interpretability, making it a foundational strategy for developing practical artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique designed to reduce the size and computational cost of large deep learning models. The process involves a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This knowledge transfer allows the student to achieve high performance while being suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile and edge devices. Originally developed for compression, the applications of this versatile paradigm have expanded to include performance enhancement, robustness improvement, and knowledge transfer in various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Carr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a key technique in deep learning for model compression. This method involves training a compact 'student' model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The goal is to create smaller, more computationally efficient models that can be deployed on resource-constrained devices without a substantial loss in performance. By transferring the nuanced knowledge captured by the teacher, the student model can often achieve accuracy comparable to its larger counterpart. The applications of this framework have expanded beyond simple size reduction, proving to be a versatile tool for enhancing model robustness, enabling privacy-preserving learning in decentralized settings, and adapting large models for specific tasks.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: The Evolution and Versatility of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a pivotal technique for creating compact and efficient deep learning models by transferring knowledge from a large teacher model to a smaller student. This process goes beyond simple model compression, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices and accelerating large-scale training. While the standard approach is effective, its limitations have spurred the development of advanced methods. These include dynamic teacher-student learning frameworks, the transfer of richer internal representations, and specialized adaptations for complex settings like federated learning and non-autoregressive machine translation. By addressing challenges such as optimization difficulties and error propagation, these evolved techniques demonstrate the adaptability and continued importance of knowledge distillation in modern NLP and deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Atkinson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that enables the creation of compact, efficient models from larger, more complex ones. Operating on a teacher-student paradigm, this process involves training a smaller student model to replicate the behavior and performance of a pre-trained teacher network. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art models, enabling their deployment on resource-constrained devices like mobile phones. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple compression, the technique has also proven effective for enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and transferring complex capabilities between models.

papers_seen.author: Waller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved remarkable success but their large size and computational demands often prevent deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and knowledge of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced information learned by the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer resources. The utility of this technique extends beyond simple compression, with applications in enhancing model robustness, improving fairness, and enabling knowledge transfer across different data modalities. Its flexibility has led to widespread adoption in fields like natural language processing and computer vision, making it a crucial tool for developing practical and accessible AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Huff
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Adaptation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks, but their large size and computational expense often hinder their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model, effectively transferring the teacher's learned knowledge. This process allows for the creation of compact models that are significantly faster and smaller, yet retain a high level of performance. Knowledge distillation has proven to be a flexible and effective strategy across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, enabling the development of powerful and practical AI applications.

papers_seen.author: Jackson
papers_seen.title: Online Knowledge Distillation via Mutual Contrastive Learning for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: The teacher-free online Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to train an ensemble of multiple student models collaboratively and distill knowledge from each other. Although existing online KD methods achieve desirable performance, they often focus on class probabilities as the core knowledge type, ignoring the valuable feature representational information. We present a Mutual Contrastive Learning (MCL) framework for online KD. The core idea of MCL is to perform mutual interaction and transfer of contrastive distributions among a cohort of networks in an online manner. Our MCL can aggregate cross-network embedding information and maximize the lower bound to the mutual information between two networks. This enables each network to learn extra contrastive knowledge from others, leading to better feature representations, thus improving the performance of visual recognition tasks. Beyond the final layer, we extend MCL to intermediate layers and perform an adaptive layer-matching mechanism trained by meta-optimization. Experiments on image classification and transfer learning to visual recognition tasks show that layer-wise MCL can lead to consistent performance gains against state-of-the-art online KD approaches. The superiority demonstrates that layer-wise MCL can guide the network to generate better feature representations. Our code is publicly avaliable at https://github.com/winycg/L-MCL.

papers_seen.author: Walker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Model Compression Technique in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique designed to create smaller, more efficient deep learning models. The process operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge from the teacher, typically through its output probabilities or internal representations, the student model can achieve comparable accuracy with significantly lower computational and memory requirements. This enables the deployment of complex, state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. The applications of this versatile technique are broad, extending beyond simple compression to performance enhancement and knowledge transfer across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the creation of compact neural networks suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. The student model is trained to mimic the behavior of the teacher, leveraging the rich, generalized information contained in its predictions or internal representations. While primarily used for reducing computational and memory footprints, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, enabling domain adaptation, and facilitating privacy-preserving learning.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for model compression and performance enhancement in deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student network is trained to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process facilitates the creation of compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. Methodologies have evolved beyond simply mimicking output predictions to include transferring knowledge from intermediate feature representations, employing multiple teachers, and selectively applying the teacher's knowledge. These advanced strategies have found broad applications across natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the compression of large language models, improving machine translation, and even enhancing algorithmic fairness.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/lgcnsai/PS-KD-Pytorch.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models suitable for resource-constrained environments. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, the student can achieve high performance that might otherwise be unattainable. While its primary application is in reducing model size and computational cost for deployment on devices like mobile phones, the framework has proven to be highly versatile. Its applications now extend beyond simple compression to include performance enhancement, knowledge transfer across different tasks and data modalities, and addressing fairness concerns in artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of compact, efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Operating on a teacher-student paradigm, it involves transferring knowledge from a large, complex model to a smaller one, reducing its computational footprint. Beyond simple compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used not only to create smaller models but also to enhance performance, improve generalization, and enable novel capabilities across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Different methodologies have been developed, such as self-distillation and multi-teacher distillation, showcasing the versatility of this framework.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.author: Mahoney
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Strategy for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile framework for compressing large, complex deep learning models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This teacher-student learning paradigm enables the transfer of knowledge from a high-capacity teacher model to a compact student model, allowing for the deployment of state-of-the-art performance on resource-constrained devices. The process involves training the student to mimic the rich outputs or internal representations of the teacher, effectively creating models that are not only smaller and faster but can also exhibit enhanced performance and robustness. The applications of this technique are extensive, spanning domains like natural language processing and computer vision, and its adaptability has led to advanced methods involving multiple teachers, adversarial learning, and data-free scenarios, solidifying its role as a crucial tool for creating practical and deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Velasquez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a deep learning technique primarily used for model compression, where a smaller 'student' model learns from a larger 'teacher' model. This process facilitates the deployment of powerful but cumbersome models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their computational and memory footprint. The student model is trained to mimic the teacher's outputs, effectively transferring its learned knowledge and generalization capabilities. While initially developed for creating efficient models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used to enhance model performance, improve fairness, and enable learning in specialized contexts like federated learning and domain adaptation. The evolution of methods, such as distilling information from intermediate layers or using self-distillation, highlights its transformation into a versatile and fundamental framework for optimizing deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Orr
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in which a smaller, more efficient "student" model is trained to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. The primary objective is to transfer the rich knowledge from the cumbersome teacher to the compact student, enabling the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This process creates smaller and faster models that maintain high accuracy. The versatility of knowledge distillation is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning. Advanced methods have been developed that extend beyond the basic teacher-student paradigm to further enhance knowledge transfer and address complex learning scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Gray
papers_seen.title: BERT-of-Theseus: Compressing BERT by Progressive Module Replacing
papers_seen.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel model compression approach to effectively compress BERT by progressive module replacing. Our approach first divides the original BERT into several modules and builds their compact substitutes. Then, we randomly replace the original modules with their substitutes to train the compact modules to mimic the behavior of the original modules. We progressively increase the probability of replacement through the training. In this way, our approach brings a deeper level of interaction between the original and compact models. Compared to the previous knowledge distillation approaches for BERT compression, our approach does not introduce any additional loss function. Our approach outperforms existing knowledge distillation approaches on GLUE benchmark, showing a new perspective of model compression.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Model Compression and Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a key technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large, complex deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. This process involves transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained "teacher" model to a smaller "student" model, aiming to replicate the teacher's performance with significantly fewer computational resources. This approach is applied across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, to create models that are smaller, faster, and more efficient. Research has explored numerous variations, such as self-distillation, multi-teacher distillation, and data-free methods that address challenges like data privacy and availability. Knowledge distillation is often combined with other compression techniques like pruning and quantization to further optimize model efficiency, striking a balance between performance and practicality.

papers_seen.author: Jacobs
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile and Effective Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique to address the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive deep learning models. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model, effectively transferring its learned knowledge. The primary benefit is the creation of compact, fast models suitable for resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its utility extends beyond simple compression to areas like performance enhancement and knowledge transfer across different tasks.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Juarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models in resource-constrained environments. The process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, the student can achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer computational resources. Initially developed for reducing model size and inference time, the applications of this versatile framework have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and transferring knowledge across different model architectures and data modalities in fields such as natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression in deep learning. This approach facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the teacher, to a smaller, more computationally efficient student model. The primary goal is to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. The process often involves transferring knowledge from the teacher's output distributions and intermediate features, not just the final predictions. This versatile framework has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Advanced strategies such as multi-teacher distillation, self-distillation, and teacher-free distillation have further expanded its utility, demonstrating its importance in developing practical and efficient AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large, state-of-the-art deep learning models into smaller, more efficient versions suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This process involves training a compact "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, including its predictions on unlabeled data, the student model can achieve performance far exceeding what it could by training on ground-truth labels alone. This approach has proven effective across a wide array of domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition, enabling the practical application of otherwise computationally prohibitive models. The methodology extends beyond simple output imitation, with advanced techniques focusing on transferring internal representations and adapting the teaching process itself to further enhance student performance and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of modern deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a highly effective model compression technique to address this issue. This method involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student can achieve high performance while being significantly smaller and faster. Initially developed for compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded, making it a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling advanced learning paradigms. This process successfully bridges the gap between state-of-the-art performance and practical deployability.

papers_seen.author: Baker
papers_seen.title: Rejuvenating Low-Frequency Words: Making the Most of Parallel Data in Non-Autoregressive Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is commonly used to construct synthetic data for training non-autoregressive translation (NAT) models. However, there exists a discrepancy on low-frequency words between the distilled and the original data, leading to more errors on predicting low-frequency words. To alleviate the problem, we directly expose the raw data into NAT by leveraging pretraining. By analyzing directed alignments, we found that KD makes low-frequency source words aligned with targets more deterministically but fails to align sufficient low-frequency words from target to source. Accordingly, we propose reverse KD to rejuvenate more alignments for low-frequency target words. To make the most of authentic and synthetic data, we combine these complementary approaches as a new training strategy for further boosting NAT performance. We conduct experiments on five translation benchmarks over two advanced architectures. Results demonstrate that the proposed approach can significantly and universally improve translation quality by reducing translation errors on low-frequency words. Encouragingly, our approach achieves 28.2 and 33.9 BLEU points on the WMT14 English-German and WMT16 Romanian-English datasets, respectively. Our code, data, and trained models are available at \url{https://github.com/alphadl/RLFW-NAT}.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models without a significant loss in performance. The process involves a teacher-student framework, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This transfer of knowledge allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures, such as large language models, in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. The methodology extends beyond simple output imitation to include transferring knowledge from intermediate feature layers and has led to advanced strategies like data-free distillation and meta-learning approaches. Ultimately, knowledge distillation serves as a versatile tool for developing practical, efficient, and robust artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Richards
papers_seen.title: TextKD-GAN: Text Generation using KnowledgeDistillation and Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Text generation is of particular interest in many NLP applications such as machine translation, language modeling, and text summarization. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) achieved a remarkable success in high quality image generation in computer vision,and recently, GANs have gained lots of interest from the NLP community as well. However, achieving similar success in NLP would be more challenging due to the discrete nature of text. In this work, we introduce a method using knowledge distillation to effectively exploit GAN setup for text generation. We demonstrate how autoencoders (AEs) can be used for providing a continuous representation of sentences, which is a smooth representation that assign non-zero probabilities to more than one word. We distill this representation to train the generator to synthesize similar smooth representations. We perform a number of experiments to validate our idea using different datasets and show that our proposed approach yields better performance in terms of the BLEU score and Jensen-Shannon distance (JSD) measure compared to traditional GAN-based text generation approaches without pre-training.

papers_seen.author: Adkins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing complexity of deep learning models poses significant challenges for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial model compression technique to address this issue. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, enabling the creation of compact models that retain high performance while reducing computational and memory requirements. Beyond simple compression, this versatile framework has found applications in enhancing model generalization, improving robustness, and enabling knowledge transfer in novel scenarios, making advanced artificial intelligence more accessible and practical for real-world applications.

This versatile technique has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the practical application of state-of-the-art models.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions suitable for real-world deployment. This process involves a smaller "student" model learning from a larger "teacher" model, transferring knowledge beyond simple labels. Originally conceived for model compression, its applications have expanded significantly across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Research shows that distillation not only reduces model size and inference time but can also enhance the student model's performance, sometimes even surpassing models trained from scratch. Advanced methods like self-distillation and data-free distillation further broaden its utility, making it a crucial tool for developing practical and effective deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Paradigm for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models, particularly in natural language processing, have created significant challenges for their deployment in real-world applications with limited resources. Model compression techniques have emerged as a critical field of study to address these challenges. Among these techniques, knowledge distillation has proven to be a particularly powerful and flexible approach. It involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process not only reduces model size and improves inference speed but can also enhance performance, improve interpretability, and enable new applications in areas like federated and lifelong learning. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by large models into more compact architectures, knowledge distillation offers a practical path toward making state-of-the-art AI more accessible and efficient.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm where a compact "student" model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. The technique has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, for tasks ranging from text generation to image classification. The core principle involves transferring the knowledge embedded in the teacher's outputs or internal representations to the student. Advanced variations of this technique have emerged, such as data-free distillation for scenarios with private data, self-distillation where a model learns from itself, and ensemble distillation using multiple teachers. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation can also be used to improve a model's performance, transfer specific capabilities like adversarial robustness, and create more efficient and generalizable models.

papers_seen.author: Montgomery
papers_seen.title: Object DGCNN: 3D Object Detection using Dynamic Graphs
papers_seen.abstract: 3D object detection often involves complicated training and testing pipelines, which require substantial domain knowledge about individual datasets. Inspired by recent non-maximum suppression-free 2D object detection models, we propose a 3D object detection architecture on point clouds. Our method models 3D object detection as message passing on a dynamic graph, generalizing the DGCNN framework to predict a set of objects. In our construction, we remove the necessity of post-processing via object confidence aggregation or non-maximum suppression. To facilitate object detection from sparse point clouds, we also propose a set-to-set distillation approach customized to 3D detection. This approach aligns the outputs of the teacher model and the student model in a permutation-invariant fashion, significantly simplifying knowledge distillation for the 3D detection task. Our method achieves state-of-the-art performance on autonomous driving benchmarks. We also provide abundant analysis of the detection model and distillation framework.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, the 'student'. This process aims to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts while being significantly faster and requiring fewer computational resources. The fundamental idea is to train the student not only on the ground-truth labels but also on the soft probability distributions produced by the teacher model. This technique has been adapted in numerous ways, including transferring knowledge from intermediate layers, operating in data-free scenarios to preserve privacy, and even applying it across different tasks or data modalities. The ultimate goal is to enable the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a substantial loss in accuracy.

Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher's predictions and internal representations, the student model can achieve performance comparable to its larger counterpart but with significantly lower computational and memory requirements. This approach has demonstrated success across a wide array of tasks, from question answering and object detection to generative modeling, making it a critical tool for creating practical, deployable deep learning applications.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

Knowledge distillation can also be combined with other compression methods like pruning and quantization to further enhance model efficiency, making powerful deep learning models accessible for resource-constrained applications.

papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.
