papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Zuniga
papers_seen.title: Large scale distributed neural network training through online distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Techniques such as ensembling and distillation promise model quality improvements when paired with almost any base model. However, due to increased test-time cost (for ensembles) and increased complexity of the training pipeline (for distillation), these techniques are challenging to use in industrial settings. In this paper we explore a variant of distillation which is relatively straightforward to use as it does not require a complicated multi-stage setup or many new hyperparameters. Our first claim is that online distillation enables us to use extra parallelism to fit very large datasets about twice as fast. Crucially, we can still speed up training even after we have already reached the point at which additional parallelism provides no benefit for synchronous or asynchronous stochastic gradient descent. Two neural networks trained on disjoint subsets of the data can share knowledge by encouraging each model to agree with the predictions the other model would have made. These predictions can come from a stale version of the other model so they can be safely computed using weights that only rarely get transmitted. Our second claim is that online distillation is a cost-effective way to make the exact predictions of a model dramatically more reproducible. We support our claims using experiments on the Criteo Display Ad Challenge dataset, ImageNet, and the largest to-date dataset used for neural language modeling, containing $6\times 10^{11}$ tokens and based on the Common Crawl repository of web data.

papers_seen.author: Stein
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that utilizes a teacher-student framework to create smaller, more efficient models. In this process, a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model, effectively transferring its learned knowledge. The primary objective is to enable the deployment of powerful models on resource-constrained devices without significant performance degradation. This versatile paradigm has broad applications in domains such as natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simply reducing model size, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance model performance, improve generalization, and transfer complex capabilities between different architectures.

papers_seen.author: Hensley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Model Compression Technique in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression and knowledge transfer paradigm where a compact 'student' model learns from a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. This technique addresses the challenge of deploying large deep learning models, such as those used in natural language processing (NLP), on resource-constrained devices. By transferring knowledge from the teacher, often in the form of soft label probabilities, the student model can achieve performance comparable to its larger counterpart while being significantly smaller and faster. Various strategies have been developed, including data-free distillation, self-distillation, and multi-teacher approaches, extending its application to diverse tasks like machine translation, object detection, and question answering.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance in numerous fields, but their significant computational and memory requirements hinder their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve comparable performance while being significantly smaller and faster. This approach has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, with specialized techniques developed for challenges such as domain adaptation, cross-modal learning, and scenarios where original training data is unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

Operating on a teacher-student paradigm, this process trains a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. While the primary goal is to enable the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It now serves as a versatile framework for not only reducing model size and latency but also for enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and enabling knowledge transfer in complex, privacy-sensitive scenarios. This evolution establishes knowledge distillation as a foundational tool for making advanced artificial intelligence more practical and widely applicable.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models from larger, more complex ones. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to transfer the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher to the student, enabling the deployment of powerful artificial intelligence architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile or edge devices. This process allows the lightweight student model to retain high performance, often exceeding what it could achieve by training on ground-truth data alone. The versatility of this paradigm extends beyond simple compression to areas like performance enhancement, domain adaptation, and knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Dodson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This process involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a pre-trained, cumbersome 'teacher' model, enabling the deployment of advanced neural networks on resource-constrained devices. The primary goal is to retain the high performance of the teacher model while significantly reducing computational and storage costs. Beyond simple model compression, the applications of knowledge distillation are broad and varied. The framework is used to enhance model robustness against adversarial attacks, facilitate privacy-preserving learning, and even boost the performance of student models beyond their teachers in specific tasks. Its versatility has led to successful applications across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, establishing it as a foundational tool for the practical deployment of state-of-the-art artificial intelligence.

papers_seen.author: Walton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful machine learning technique focused on transferring knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the teacher, to a smaller, more efficient model, called the student. Originally conceived for model compression, this process allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by creating smaller, faster versions that retain much of the original's performance. The applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly beyond simple compression. It is now used to improve the absolute performance of student models, sometimes even allowing them to outperform their teachers. Furthermore, the technique has been adapted to address challenges in diverse areas such as federated learning, data privacy, and multimodal learning. By leveraging the learned representations of a teacher, knowledge distillation provides a flexible framework for creating more practical, robust, and capable models across various domains, particularly in Natural Language Processing (NLP).

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of compact, efficient models suitable for real-world deployment. The process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to create models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a substantial loss in performance. By transferring the rich, nuanced information captured by the teacher, the student model can achieve high accuracy. The utility of knowledge distillation extends beyond simple compression, serving as a powerful framework for enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and transferring complex capabilities across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Sanchez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that employs a teacher-student framework. In this process, a compact student model learns to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to create smaller, more computationally efficient networks that can be deployed in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. Knowledge is typically transferred by training the student on the teacher's output probabilities or internal feature representations. This versatile technique is widely applied across domains like natural language processing and computer vision. Its utility extends beyond simple compression, as it can also be used to enhance model performance, improve generalization, and address challenges such as data scarcity and privacy.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Tool for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning, enabling the creation of smaller, more efficient models suitable for resource-constrained environments. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and internal representations of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. While its primary application is to reduce computational and memory requirements without significant performance degradation, the utility of knowledge distillation has expanded considerably. It is now used to enhance model performance, transfer knowledge across different data modalities, improve model interpretability, and adapt large-scale models for specific downstream tasks in domains like natural language processing and computer vision. This versatility makes knowledge distillation a foundational strategy for developing practical and effective artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: From Model Compression to a Versatile Deep Learning Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a key technique in deep learning, initially developed for model compression. It involves a teacher-student paradigm where a compact "student" model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, more powerful "teacher" model. This process allows for the creation of smaller, faster models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. While its primary application is compression, the utility of knowledge distillation has expanded considerably. It is now used to enhance model performance, facilitate learning in data-scarce environments, and enable advanced paradigms like federated and lifelong learning, establishing it as a versatile framework for building more efficient and robust AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Ensemble Knowledge Distillation for CTR Prediction
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, deep learning-based models have been widely studied for click-through rate (CTR) prediction and lead to improved prediction accuracy in many industrial applications. However, current research focuses primarily on building complex network architectures to better capture sophisticated feature interactions and dynamic user behaviors. The increased model complexity may slow down online inference and hinder its adoption in real-time applications. Instead, our work targets at a new model training strategy based on knowledge distillation (KD). KD is a teacher-student learning framework to transfer knowledge learned from a teacher model to a student model. The KD strategy not only allows us to simplify the student model as a vanilla DNN model but also achieves significant accuracy improvements over the state-of-the-art teacher models. The benefits thus motivate us to further explore the use of a powerful ensemble of teachers for more accurate student model training. We also propose some novel techniques to facilitate ensembled CTR prediction, including teacher gating and early stopping by distillation loss. We conduct comprehensive experiments against 12 existing models and across three industrial datasets. Both offline and online A/B testing results show the effectiveness of our KD-based training strategy.

papers_seen.author: Ferrell
papers_seen.title: AlphaNet: Improved Training of Supernets with Alpha-Divergence
papers_seen.abstract: Weight-sharing neural architecture search (NAS) is an effective technique for automating efficient neural architecture design. Weight-sharing NAS builds a supernet that assembles all the architectures as its sub-networks and jointly trains the supernet with the sub-networks. The success of weight-sharing NAS heavily relies on distilling the knowledge of the supernet to the sub-networks. However, we find that the widely used distillation divergence, i.e., KL divergence, may lead to student sub-networks that over-estimate or under-estimate the uncertainty of the teacher supernet, leading to inferior performance of the sub-networks. In this work, we propose to improve the supernet training with a more generalized alpha-divergence. By adaptively selecting the alpha-divergence, we simultaneously prevent the over-estimation or under-estimation of the uncertainty of the teacher model. We apply the proposed alpha-divergence based supernets training to both slimmable neural networks and weight-sharing NAS, and demonstrate significant improvements. Specifically, our discovered model family, AlphaNet, outperforms prior-art models on a wide range of FLOPs regimes, including BigNAS, Once-for-All networks, and AttentiveNAS. We achieve ImageNet top-1 accuracy of 80.0% with only 444M FLOPs. Our code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/AlphaNet.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning and natural language processing. It utilizes a teacher-student framework where a smaller, more compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to transfer the rich knowledge from the complex teacher to the student, thereby reducing computational and storage requirements for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. This knowledge transfer can occur through the teacher's final predictions, intermediate feature representations, or attention mechanisms. The versatility of this approach has led to its successful application across a wide range of domains and has spurred the development of advanced methods, including multi-teacher and data-free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Cruz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models. The process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact "student" model is trained to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This enables the deployment of complex neural networks on devices with limited computational resources. Knowledge is typically transferred by training the student on the teacher's output probabilities or its internal feature representations. While its primary use is model compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness against adversarial attacks, and transferring knowledge in data-scarce or privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Bright
papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.author: Cherry
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in which a compact 'student' model is trained to emulate the performance of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of deep learning models, enabling their deployment on resource-constrained devices without a substantial loss in accuracy. This is achieved by transferring the 'knowledge' from the teacher to the student, often by using the teacher's output probabilities as soft targets for training the student. While initially focused on compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and facilitating training in privacy-sensitive or data-scarce environments. The versatility of this framework has made it a crucial tool across various domains, including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, called the 'student'. This process enables the creation of compact neural networks that are suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. The core idea is to train the student model to mimic the output distribution of the teacher model, leveraging the rich, learned information contained in the teacher's predictions. Variations of this technique include using multiple teachers, distilling knowledge from intermediate feature layers, and even training teacher models to be more 'student-friendly'. Knowledge distillation has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, as well as in specialized paradigms like federated learning to preserve privacy and improve communication efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models without substantial performance degradation. The process involves transferring knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a compact 'student' model. This allows for the deployment of powerful neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. The student learns to mimic the rich output distributions and internal representations of the teacher, thereby inheriting its capabilities while maintaining a smaller footprint. This versatile framework has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its applications extend beyond compression to areas like performance enhancement, robustness, and privacy.

It utilizes a teacher-student framework where a small, efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. papers_seen.author: Warner
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments. The process involves a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This knowledge transfer allows the student to achieve high performance while maintaining a significantly smaller footprint, making it suitable for practical applications. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile paradigm used for improving model generalization, enabling training without access to original data, and facilitating learning in complex settings like federated learning.

papers_seen.author: Roberts
papers_seen.title: Improving the Interpretability of Deep Neural Networks with Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep Neural Networks have achieved huge success at a wide spectrum of applications from language modeling, computer vision to speech recognition. However, nowadays, good performance alone is not sufficient to satisfy the needs of practical deployment where interpretability is demanded for cases involving ethics and mission critical applications. The complex models of Deep Neural Networks make it hard to understand and reason the predictions, which hinders its further progress. To tackle this problem, we apply the Knowledge Distillation technique to distill Deep Neural Networks into decision trees in order to attain good performance and interpretability simultaneously. We formulate the problem at hand as a multi-output regression problem and the experiments demonstrate that the student model achieves significantly better accuracy performance (about 1\% to 5\%) than vanilla decision trees at the same level of tree depth. The experiments are implemented on the TensorFlow platform to make it scalable to big datasets. To the best of our knowledge, we are the first to distill Deep Neural Networks into vanilla decision trees on multi-class datasets.

papers_seen.author: Keith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Paradigm for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. It facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient 'student' models by transferring knowledge from larger, more complex 'teacher' models. This process enables the deployment of powerful neural networks on devices with limited computational and storage resources. The applications of this technique are widespread, moving beyond simple size reduction to include performance enhancement, improvements in model interpretability, and addressing algorithmic fairness. By leveraging the rich information captured by teacher models, distillation provides a flexible and powerful framework for optimizing deep learning systems for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models have achieved unprecedented performance but their large size and computational demands often hinder practical deployment. Model compression techniques are crucial for addressing this challenge, with knowledge distillation emerging as a particularly effective and versatile framework. This method involves transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. By training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, it is possible to create compact models that retain a high level of performance while being significantly faster and less resource-intensive. The utility of this approach extends beyond simple compression, as it can also be used to enhance model performance and robustness. Knowledge distillation has proven successful across diverse domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it an indispensable tool for bridging the gap between state-of-the-art research and real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Mitigating Gender Bias in Distilled Language Models via Counterfactual Role Reversal
papers_seen.abstract: Language models excel at generating coherent text, and model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation have enabled their use in resource-constrained settings. However, these models can be biased in multiple ways, including the unfounded association of male and female genders with gender-neutral professions. Therefore, knowledge distillation without any fairness constraints may preserve or exaggerate the teacher model's biases onto the distilled model. To this end, we present a novel approach to mitigate gender disparity in text generation by learning a fair model during knowledge distillation. We propose two modifications to the base knowledge distillation based on counterfactual role reversal$\unicode{x2014}$modifying teacher probabilities and augmenting the training set. We evaluate gender polarity across professions in open-ended text generated from the resulting distilled and finetuned GPT$\unicode{x2012}$2 models and demonstrate a substantial reduction in gender disparity with only a minor compromise in utility. Finally, we observe that language models that reduce gender polarity in language generation do not improve embedding fairness or downstream classification fairness.

papers_seen.author: Dominguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning designed to compress large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions. Operating on a teacher-student paradigm, this process trains a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. While the primary goal is to enable the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It now serves as a versatile framework for not only reducing model size and latency but also for enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and enabling knowledge transfer in complex, privacy-sensitive scenarios. This evolution establishes knowledge distillation as a foundational tool for making advanced artificial intelligence more practical and widely applicable.

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique where a compact 'student' model learns from a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process aims to transfer the teacher's learned knowledge, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. The transfer can occur through various means, including mimicking the teacher's output probabilities or its internal feature representations. Advanced methods have emerged, such as online distillation where models teach each other, and meta-learning approaches where the teacher adapts its training strategy to better instruct the student. This technique has found broad applications in both natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the deployment of sophisticated models in resource-constrained environments by creating efficient, task-specific networks for tasks ranging from language understanding to 3D object detection.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: May

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique for compressing large deep learning models. This method involves training a smaller, computationally efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to create compact models that retain high performance while being significantly faster and requiring fewer computational resources, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. However, the applications of this framework extend far beyond simple compression. It can be used to enhance model performance, transfer specific capabilities like adversarial robustness, and even operate in scenarios where the original training data is unavailable, making it a critical tool for the practical application of modern artificial intelligence.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large, complex deep learning models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This process involves a "teacher-student" paradigm, where a smaller student network learns to mimic the outputs or internal representations of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve comparable performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. This makes it possible to deploy state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as on mobile devices or for latency-sensitive applications. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing, where it is used to create compact language models, and computer vision, for tasks like object detection and image classification. Research continues to explore novel distillation methods, including data-free approaches and cross-architecture knowledge transfer, further enhancing its flexibility and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Rhodes
papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.author: Thompson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale deep learning models often have computational and storage requirements that hinder their deployment in practical, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a key model compression technique to overcome this challenge. It operates under a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and inherit the knowledge of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process enables the creation of compact, high-performance models suitable for real-world applications. The versatility of this framework extends beyond mere compression, with applications in performance enhancement, domain adaptation, and knowledge transfer in privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Aguilar
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions suitable for real-world deployment. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. While the primary goal is to reduce computational and memory requirements for resource-constrained environments, the applications of knowledge distillation extend far beyond simple model compression. The technique has proven to be a versatile framework for enhancing student model performance, improving generalization, adapting models to new domains, and enabling knowledge transfer in complex scenarios such as lifelong learning. This makes it a fundamental tool for creating more practical, robust, and efficient artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Mills
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression and knowledge transfer technique in deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to replicate the performance of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in accuracy. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation can also be used to improve a model's performance, enhance its generalization capabilities across different data distributions, and transfer beneficial properties, such as inductive biases, from one model to another. The technique is versatile, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, and has given rise to numerous variations, including self-distillation, data-free distillation, and methods involving multiple or adaptive teachers.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large, state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This process involves training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The core principle is to transfer the nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, often encapsulated in its soft predictions, to the more compact student network. This approach has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to compress models like large language transformers and generative adversarial networks. Advanced methods have been developed that utilize multiple teachers, distill knowledge from intermediate layers, and even operate in data-free settings to address privacy concerns. Furthermore, knowledge distillation plays a crucial role in communication-efficient frameworks like federated learning, demonstrating its versatility and importance in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.author: Murillo
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary goal is to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. The technique involves training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs, often using its softened probability distributions or intermediate feature representations. Its applications are wide-ranging, spanning domains like natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning.

papers_seen.author: Dean

This multifaceted capability establishes knowledge distillation not just as a compression tool, but as a fundamental paradigm for developing more practical, adaptable, and robust artificial intelligence systems.

However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond creating smaller and faster models. It has evolved into a versatile tool for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and addressing complex challenges such as data privacy and federated learning. Its adaptability has led to widespread adoption and the development of advanced methods, establishing it as a foundational technique for creating more efficient, practical, and robust AI systems across various domains.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Pierce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm where a compact "student" model is trained to reproduce the performance of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This technique addresses the challenge of deploying computationally intensive deep learning networks on resource-constrained devices. The process involves transferring knowledge from the teacher to the student, often by using the teacher's output probabilities as soft labels or by mimicking its internal feature representations. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing for tasks like machine translation and language model compression, and in computer vision for object detection and image generation. Advanced applications of this framework include enhancing model robustness, preserving privacy in federated learning, and enabling data-free model training.

papers_seen.author: Moore

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Towards Model Agnostic Federated Learning Using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Is it possible to design an universal API for federated learning using which an ad-hoc group of data-holders (agents) collaborate with each other and perform federated learning? Such an API would necessarily need to be model-agnostic i.e. make no assumption about the model architecture being used by the agents, and also cannot rely on having representative public data at hand. Knowledge distillation (KD) is the obvious tool of choice to design such protocols. However, surprisingly, we show that most natural KD-based federated learning protocols have poor performance.   To investigate this, we propose a new theoretical framework, Federated Kernel ridge regression, which can capture both model heterogeneity as well as data heterogeneity. Our analysis shows that the degradation is largely due to a fundamental limitation of knowledge distillation under data heterogeneity. We further validate our framework by analyzing and designing new protocols based on KD. Their performance on real world experiments using neural networks, though still unsatisfactory, closely matches our theoretical predictions.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Roman
papers_seen.title: Fair Feature Distillation for Visual Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Fairness is becoming an increasingly crucial issue for computer vision, especially in the human-related decision systems. However, achieving algorithmic fairness, which makes a model produce indiscriminative outcomes against protected groups, is still an unresolved problem. In this paper, we devise a systematic approach which reduces algorithmic biases via feature distillation for visual recognition tasks, dubbed as MMD-based Fair Distillation (MFD). While the distillation technique has been widely used in general to improve the prediction accuracy, to the best of our knowledge, there has been no explicit work that also tries to improve fairness via distillation. Furthermore, We give a theoretical justification of our MFD on the effect of knowledge distillation and fairness. Throughout the extensive experiments, we show our MFD significantly mitigates the bias against specific minorities without any loss of the accuracy on both synthetic and real-world face datasets.

papers_seen.author: Walter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation from A Stronger Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Unlike existing knowledge distillation methods focus on the baseline settings, where the teacher models and training strategies are not that strong and competing as state-of-the-art approaches, this paper presents a method dubbed DIST to distill better from a stronger teacher. We empirically find that the discrepancy of predictions between the student and a stronger teacher may tend to be fairly severer. As a result, the exact match of predictions in KL divergence would disturb the training and make existing methods perform poorly. In this paper, we show that simply preserving the relations between the predictions of teacher and student would suffice, and propose a correlation-based loss to capture the intrinsic inter-class relations from the teacher explicitly. Besides, considering that different instances have different semantic similarities to each class, we also extend this relational match to the intra-class level. Our method is simple yet practical, and extensive experiments demonstrate that it adapts well to various architectures, model sizes and training strategies, and can achieve state-of-the-art performance consistently on image classification, object detection, and semantic segmentation tasks. Code is available at: https://github.com/hunto/DIST_KD .

papers_seen.author: Fletcher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression in deep learning. This approach facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the teacher, to a smaller, more computationally efficient student model. The primary goal is to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. The process often involves transferring knowledge from the teacher's output distributions and intermediate features, not just the final predictions. This versatile framework has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Advanced strategies such as multi-teacher distillation, self-distillation, and teacher-free distillation have further expanded its utility, demonstrating its importance in developing practical and efficient AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models in resource-constrained environments. The process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, the student can achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer computational resources. Initially developed for reducing model size and inference time, the applications of this versatile framework have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and transferring knowledge across different model architectures and data modalities in fields such as natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Burton
papers_seen.title: Efficient Transformer-based Large Scale Language Representations using Hardware-friendly Block Structured Pruning
papers_seen.abstract: Pre-trained large-scale language models have increasingly demonstrated high accuracy on many natural language processing (NLP) tasks. However, the limited weight storage and computational speed on hardware platforms have impeded the popularity of pre-trained models, especially in the era of edge computing. In this work, we propose an efficient transformer-based large-scale language representation using hardware-friendly block structure pruning. We incorporate the reweighted group Lasso into block-structured pruning for optimization. Besides the significantly reduced weight storage and computation, the proposed approach achieves high compression rates. Experimental results on different models (BERT, RoBERTa, and DistilBERT) on the General Language Understanding Evaluation (GLUE) benchmark tasks show that we achieve up to 5.0x with zero or minor accuracy degradation on certain task(s). Our proposed method is also orthogonal to existing compact pre-trained language models such as DistilBERT using knowledge distillation, since a further 1.79x average compression rate can be achieved on top of DistilBERT with zero or minor accuracy degradation. It is suitable to deploy the final compressed model on resource-constrained edge devices.
