papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large, state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This process involves training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The core principle is to transfer the nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, often encapsulated in its soft predictions, to the more compact student network. This approach has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to compress models like large language transformers and generative adversarial networks. Advanced methods have been developed that utilize multiple teachers, distill knowledge from intermediate layers, and even operate in data-free settings to address privacy concerns. Furthermore, knowledge distillation plays a crucial role in communication-efficient frameworks like federated learning, demonstrating its versatility and importance in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Duncan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression paradigm where a compact "student" network learns from a larger "teacher" network. This technique facilitates the deployment of complex deep learning models in settings with limited computational resources. The process involves transferring knowledge through various mechanisms, including mimicking the teacher's final outputs, aligning intermediate feature representations, or preserving relational knowledge. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across diverse fields such as natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition. Beyond simple compression, this framework can be used for more advanced purposes, including transferring specific properties like adversarial robustness or inductive biases between different model architectures. It also enables novel applications like cross-modal learning and improving models in federated learning environments.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.author: Galloway
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique in deep learning for compressing large, cumbersome models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This teacher-student learning paradigm involves training a compact student model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to transfer the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, including nuanced relationships between classes, to the student, enabling it to achieve comparable or even superior performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing and computer vision, facilitating the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices and in specialized environments like federated learning. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation also serves as a potent regularization technique and a method for enhancing model performance and enabling novel cross-modal knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical model compression technique in deep learning, designed to create smaller, more efficient models suitable for real-world deployment. The process operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This transfer of knowledge enables the creation of lightweight models that retain high performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. The applications of this versatile technique are broad, spanning domains from natural language processing to computer vision, facilitating the use of advanced artificial intelligence in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Wells
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient neural networks. It utilizes a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to reduce the computational and memory requirements of state-of-the-art models, facilitating their deployment on resource-constrained devices like mobile phones. This process involves transferring the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, such as its output probability distributions and internal feature representations, to the student. The applications of this versatile framework extend beyond simple compression to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling knowledge transfer in privacy-preserving scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Peterson
papers_seen.title: Understanding Knowledge Distillation in Non-autoregressive Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Non-autoregressive machine translation (NAT) systems predict a sequence of output tokens in parallel, achieving substantial improvements in generation speed compared to autoregressive models. Existing NAT models usually rely on the technique of knowledge distillation, which creates the training data from a pretrained autoregressive model for better performance. Knowledge distillation is empirically useful, leading to large gains in accuracy for NAT models, but the reason for this success has, as of yet, been unclear. In this paper, we first design systematic experiments to investigate why knowledge distillation is crucial to NAT training. We find that knowledge distillation can reduce the complexity of data sets and help NAT to model the variations in the output data. Furthermore, a strong correlation is observed between the capacity of an NAT model and the optimal complexity of the distilled data for the best translation quality. Based on these findings, we further propose several approaches that can alter the complexity of data sets to improve the performance of NAT models. We achieve the state-of-the-art performance for the NAT-based models, and close the gap with the autoregressive baseline on WMT14 En-De benchmark.

papers_seen.author: Flores
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for compressing large, computationally expensive deep learning models into smaller, more efficient versions suitable for practical deployment. This method employs a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student can achieve comparable or even superior performance with a significantly smaller footprint. The framework's versatility is demonstrated by its successful application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, bridging the gap between high-performance research models and deployable artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Gonzalez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and computationally expensive for practical use in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile model compression technique to address this challenge. It employs a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, enabling the creation of compact models that are faster and require less memory without a significant loss in performance. The applications of this framework are widespread, spanning natural language processing and computer vision, and its utility extends beyond simple compression to include performance enhancement and knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Compression of Deep Learning Models for Text: A Survey
papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. But these models are humongous in size. On the other hand,real world applications demand small model size, low response times and low computational power wattage. In this survey, wediscuss six different types of methods (Pruning, Quantization, Knowledge Distillation, Parameter Sharing, Tensor Decomposition, andSub-quadratic Transformer based methods) for compression of such models to enable their deployment in real industry NLP projects.Given the critical need of building applications with efficient and small models, and the large amount of recently published work inthis area, we believe that this survey organizes the plethora of work done by the 'deep learning for NLP' community in the past fewyears and presents it as a coherent story.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a prominent technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. The process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This approach addresses the significant computational and memory challenges associated with deploying state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, student models can achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller footprint. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains and its adaptation to address challenges like data privacy and architectural mismatches, making advanced AI more accessible for real-world use.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to transfer the rich knowledge from the teacher, thereby creating a compact model that retains high performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. This enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated through its application across diverse tasks and the continuous development of advanced methods that go beyond simple output matching, solidifying its role in making advanced artificial intelligence more practical and accessible.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: James
papers_seen.title: Robust Cross-Modal Representation Learning with Progressive Self-Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The learning objective of vision-language approach of CLIP does not effectively account for the noisy many-to-many correspondences found in web-harvested image captioning datasets, which contributes to its compute and data inefficiency. To address this challenge, we introduce a novel training framework based on cross-modal contrastive learning that uses progressive self-distillation and soft image-text alignments to more efficiently learn robust representations from noisy data. Our model distills its own knowledge to dynamically generate soft-alignment targets for a subset of images and captions in every minibatch, which are then used to update its parameters. Extensive evaluation across 14 benchmark datasets shows that our method consistently outperforms its CLIP counterpart in multiple settings, including: (a) zero-shot classification, (b) linear probe transfer, and (c) image-text retrieval, without incurring added computational cost. Analysis using an ImageNet-based robustness test-bed reveals that our method offers better effective robustness to natural distribution shifts compared to both ImageNet-trained models and CLIP itself. Lastly, pretraining with datasets spanning two orders of magnitude in size shows that our improvements over CLIP tend to scale with number of training examples.

papers_seen.author: Potter
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the transfer of knowledge from a large, complex model to a smaller, more efficient one. This process operates on a teacher-student framework, where the compact student model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of the larger teacher. The primary objective is to enable the deployment of powerful, state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, where computational power and memory are limited. While initially conceived for creating smaller and faster models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used to enhance model performance, improve interpretability, and address challenges in areas like data privacy and federated learning across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the deployment of large, complex models in resource-constrained environments. The core idea involves transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained 'teacher' model to a smaller 'student' model, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. Beyond simple compression, this paradigm has been adapted to address a wide range of challenges. Researchers have successfully employed knowledge distillation to enhance model fairness by mitigating algorithmic and gender biases, to improve data privacy by creating models with differential privacy guarantees, and even to develop student models that outperform their teachers. This adaptability across various domains, including natural language processing and graph-based learning, highlights knowledge distillation as a powerful and flexible tool in the development of efficient and responsible AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression technique that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient neural networks. This is achieved through a teacher-student framework, where a smaller "student" model is trained to replicate the outputs or internal representations of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. The primary goal is often to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art models, making them suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has also been shown to improve the performance of student models, sometimes enabling them to outperform models of a similar size trained from scratch. The technique has been successfully applied across a wide array of domains, including computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph-based learning, with various methodological innovations continually expanding its utility.

papers_seen.author: Arnold
papers_seen.title: Does Knowledge Distillation Really Work?
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique for training a small student network to emulate a larger teacher model, such as an ensemble of networks. We show that while knowledge distillation can improve student generalization, it does not typically work as it is commonly understood: there often remains a surprisingly large discrepancy between the predictive distributions of the teacher and the student, even in cases when the student has the capacity to perfectly match the teacher. We identify difficulties in optimization as a key reason for why the student is unable to match the teacher. We also show how the details of the dataset used for distillation play a role in how closely the student matches the teacher -- and that more closely matching the teacher paradoxically does not always lead to better student generalization.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective model compression technique that facilitates the deployment of large, complex deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, including its understanding of data structure and inter-class relationships, the student model can achieve performance far superior to what it could by training on the data alone. This approach has proven successful across various domains, including natural language processing, speech recognition, and computer vision, enabling the creation of compact models that are faster and require less memory without a significant drop in accuracy. The flexibility of knowledge distillation allows it to be combined with other techniques like data augmentation and federated learning, extending its applicability to diverse and challenging scenarios such as privacy-preservation and few-shot learning.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models, particularly in fields like natural language processing, present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible model compression technique to address these challenges. This approach involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, including its predictions on unlabeled data, the student model can achieve comparable performance to its larger counterpart while being significantly smaller and faster. This technique has proven effective across a wide range of applications, from compressing large language models to enabling efficient object detection and transferring knowledge across different data modalities, making it a critical tool for creating practical, real-world artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models have achieved unprecedented performance but their immense size and computational cost often hinder practical deployment. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression framework to address this challenge. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer resources. This makes it possible to deploy state-of-the-art models on devices with limited computational power, such as mobile phones. The technique's versatility is demonstrated by its broad application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its adaptation into advanced methods like self-distillation and data-free distillation, further expanding its utility in developing efficient and robust AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Adapt-and-Distill: Developing Small, Fast and Effective Pretrained Language Models for Domains
papers_seen.abstract: Large pre-trained models have achieved great success in many natural language processing tasks. However, when they are applied in specific domains, these models suffer from domain shift and bring challenges in fine-tuning and online serving for latency and capacity constraints. In this paper, we present a general approach to developing small, fast and effective pre-trained models for specific domains. This is achieved by adapting the off-the-shelf general pre-trained models and performing task-agnostic knowledge distillation in target domains. Specifically, we propose domain-specific vocabulary expansion in the adaptation stage and employ corpus level occurrence probability to choose the size of incremental vocabulary automatically. Then we systematically explore different strategies to compress the large pre-trained models for specific domains. We conduct our experiments in the biomedical and computer science domain. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach achieves better performance over the BERT BASE model in domain-specific tasks while 3.3x smaller and 5.1x faster than BERT BASE. The code and pre-trained models are available at https://aka.ms/adalm.

papers_seen.author: Valencia
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile and Effective Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models, while powerful, are often too large and computationally expensive for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a highly effective model compression technique to address this challenge. The process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This allows the student to learn a compressed representation of the teacher's knowledge, resulting in a compact model that retains high performance while being significantly faster and smaller. This versatility has led to its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it an essential tool for creating practical and deployable artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Technique for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique for model compression within deep learning. This process operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of complex neural networks, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. Beyond simple compression, research has shown that knowledge distillation can also enhance the performance of student models. Its applications are broad, spanning critical domains like natural language processing and computer vision, demonstrating its importance in making advanced AI systems more practical and accessible.

papers_seen.author: Marshall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile and Effective Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models from larger, complex ones. This process operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model learns to mimic the behavior of a pre-trained teacher model, thereby inheriting its rich, generalized knowledge. The primary goal is to enable the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures, such as large language models, on resource-constrained devices where computational power and memory are limited. While initially conceived for creating lightweight networks, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly, demonstrating its utility for enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and transferring knowledge in privacy-sensitive scenarios across domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

This process allows the student model to achieve high performance, often superior to what it could attain if trained on data alone. The technique has found broad applications in diverse domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its utility now extends beyond compression to areas like performance enhancement and knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Harmon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary objective is to reduce computational and memory requirements, enabling the deployment of powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices while maintaining high performance. This is typically achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, often using its output probabilities as supervisory signals. The technique has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework used to enhance model performance, facilitate privacy-preserving distributed learning, and adapt models to new domains.

papers_seen.author: Cortez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and powerful technique for model compression within the field of deep learning. This paradigm addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from a large 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The student is trained to mimic the behavior of the teacher, often by learning from its softened probability outputs or intermediate feature representations. This process allows the compact student model to achieve high performance, often comparable to its much larger teacher, without the associated computational and memory overhead. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it an essential tool for developing practical and deployable AI systems.

papers_seen.abstract: As deep learning models increase in size and complexity, their deployment in resource-constrained environments poses a significant challenge. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and widely adopted technique for model compression. This method involves a teacher-student learning paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student can achieve comparable or even enhanced performance with a significantly smaller computational footprint. This approach enables the practical application of state-of-the-art models on devices with limited memory and processing power, proving effective across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful training paradigm where a smaller "student" model learns from a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. Initially conceived for model compression, this technique enables the development of lightweight, efficient neural networks that retain the high performance of their cumbersome counterparts. Beyond creating faster and smaller models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now a crucial tool for a range of tasks including domain adaptation, where models must adjust to new data distributions, and federated learning, which facilitates collaborative training across distributed devices with heterogeneous models without sharing private data. The success of distillation often depends on sophisticated strategies that go beyond simple output matching, such as aligning intermediate feature representations and leveraging statistically sound data augmentation. Despite its power, challenges in optimization remain, but knowledge distillation continues to be a versatile and impactful framework in modern deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: Compressing Large Neural Networks for Practical Applications
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, offer a promising solution by transferring knowledge from a large, powerful 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the creation of compact networks that retain much of the performance of their larger counterparts. Innovations in this field have led to advanced methods, including adversarial training frameworks that adaptively measure the discrepancy between models, and data-free approaches that preserve privacy by eliminating the need for the original training dataset. These developments extend the applicability of state-of-the-art models to a wider range of practical scenarios, from mobile devices to embedded systems, across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Castaneda
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and computational complexity of state-of-the-art deep learning models pose significant challenges for their deployment in practical, resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile model compression technique to address this issue. This method employs a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, this process enables the creation of compact, fast models that maintain high performance. The applications of knowledge distillation extend beyond simple compression, encompassing performance enhancement, improved model robustness, and knowledge transfer across different domains, making it an indispensable tool for developing practical and efficient artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Parker
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning and natural language processing. It utilizes a teacher-student framework where a smaller, more compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to transfer the rich knowledge from the complex teacher to the student, thereby reducing computational and storage requirements for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. This knowledge transfer can occur through the teacher's final predictions, intermediate feature representations, or attention mechanisms. The versatility of this approach has led to its successful application across a wide range of domains and has spurred the development of advanced methods, including multi-teacher and data-free distillation.

papers_seen.author: Hodges
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework Beyond Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning, widely recognized for its ability to compress large, complex models into smaller, more efficient "student" networks. However, its applications extend far beyond simple model compression. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is a versatile framework capable of not only creating efficient models but also enhancing their performance, enabling new functionalities, and addressing critical challenges such as fairness, privacy, and domain adaptation. By transferring knowledge from one or more "teacher" models, student models can achieve state-of-the-art results in diverse areas including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning. The evolution of distillation techniques, from mimicking output logits to advanced feature-mimicking and meta-learning approaches, further underscores its flexibility and growing importance in the development of robust and adaptable AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a prominent technique in deep learning for model compression. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the performance of a larger, more complex teacher model. The primary goal is to create smaller, faster, and more computationally efficient neural networks that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This process involves transferring knowledge from the teacher, often through its output probabilities or internal feature representations, to guide the student's training. The applications of this technique are diverse, spanning natural language processing and computer vision, and extend beyond simple compression to areas like improving model robustness, facilitating federated learning, and enhancing model performance.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the "teacher," to a smaller, more efficient model, the "student." This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their size and inference latency without a significant loss in performance. The core idea involves training the student model to mimic the output distributions of the teacher model, effectively learning a richer, more generalized representation than it could from ground-truth labels alone. This technique has found broad applications across various domains, including Natural Language Processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Research explores not only compressing models but also enhancing their performance, adapting them for multi-task learning, and enabling privacy-preserving or distributed learning paradigms.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Paradigm for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Originally conceived as a method for a smaller "student" model to learn from a larger "teacher" model, the paradigm has evolved significantly. Research now shows that the benefits of distillation extend beyond simple mimicry, with the regularization effects of soft labels playing a crucial role. This technique has proven effective in a wide array of complex domains, including natural language processing for text generation and translation, the compression of generative adversarial networks, and the optimization of graph neural networks. Advanced methods such as self-distillation, adversarial training, and extensions for domain adaptation further highlight its versatility. Ultimately, knowledge distillation is a critical tool for creating efficient, yet powerful, AI systems suitable for real-world applications.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a prominent technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. The process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This approach addresses the significant computational and memory challenges associated with deploying state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, student models can achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller footprint. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains and its adaptation to address challenges like data privacy and architectural mismatches, making advanced AI more accessible for real-world use.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models from larger, computationally expensive ones. The primary goal is to retain the high performance of the teacher while significantly reducing its computational and memory footprint, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures on resource-constrained devices. The applications for this versatile technique are widespread, spanning natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple size reduction, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance model performance, improve generalization, and transfer knowledge in privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Lopez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, cumbersome 'teacher' model, making it feasible to deploy state-of-the-art architectures on resource-constrained devices. However, the applications of knowledge distillation extend far beyond mere compression. It serves as a flexible framework for transferring knowledge to enhance model accuracy, enable continuous learning across sequential tasks, facilitate domain adaptation without source data, and even improve performance in multi-task learning settings. This versatility makes knowledge distillation a critical tool for advancing the practical application and capabilities of modern neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Cardenas
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile model compression technique in deep learning. It addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments by transferring knowledge from a large 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process allows the student to achieve high performance with a significantly reduced footprint, making advanced AI practical for applications on devices like mobile phones. While initially conceived for compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling complex learning paradigms, establishing it as a fundamental tool in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Moore
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful training paradigm where a smaller "student" model learns from a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. Initially conceived for model compression, this technique enables the development of lightweight, efficient neural networks that retain the high performance of their cumbersome counterparts. Beyond creating faster and smaller models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now a crucial tool for a range of tasks including domain adaptation, where models must adjust to new data distributions, and federated learning, which facilitates collaborative training across distributed devices with heterogeneous models without sharing private data. The success of distillation often depends on sophisticated strategies that go beyond simple output matching, such as aligning intermediate feature representations and leveraging statistically sound data augmentation. Despite its power, challenges in optimization remain, but knowledge distillation continues to be a versatile and impactful framework in modern deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Sims
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning designed for model compression and knowledge transfer. The process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This enables the deployment of complex neural networks on resource-constrained devices by creating lightweight versions without a significant drop in accuracy. Beyond its primary use for compression, the framework has proven to be highly versatile, with applications in enhancing model performance, transferring capabilities across different architectures, and addressing challenges in areas such as privacy-preserving learning and adversarial robustness.

papers_seen.author: Hoffman
papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.author: Vance
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Operating on a teacher-student framework, a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher to the student, enabling the smaller model to achieve high performance with significantly lower computational and memory requirements. While its primary application is model compression, the utility of knowledge distillation has expanded to include performance enhancement, improved model interpretability, and enabling novel applications in privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Osborne
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.author: Wright
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for model compression and performance enhancement in deep learning. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student network is trained to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process facilitates the creation of compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. Methodologies have evolved beyond simply mimicking output predictions to include transferring knowledge from intermediate feature representations, employing multiple teachers, and selectively applying the teacher's knowledge. These advanced strategies have found broad applications across natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the compression of large language models, improving machine translation, and even enhancing algorithmic fairness.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Improved Accuracy in Spoken Question Answering
papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. Automatic speech recognition (ASR) plays a significant role in the development of QA systems. However, the recent work shows that ASR systems generate highly noisy transcripts, which critically limit the capability of machine comprehension on the SQA task. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Model Compression Technique in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective model compression and training paradigm in which a compact 'student' model learns to mimic a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to transfer the knowledge from the high-performing teacher to the student, enabling the creation of smaller, faster, and more efficient models that are suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. This knowledge transfer can occur in various forms, from mimicking the teacher's final output probabilities (soft labels) to replicating its intermediate feature representations. The technique has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing for compressing large language models like BERT, and in computer vision for tasks such as object detection and image classification. Advanced distillation frameworks include using ensembles of teachers, adversarial training schemes, and self-distillation, where a model learns from its own past predictions. Furthermore, knowledge distillation is a key enabler for collaborative learning paradigms like federated learning, allowing knowledge transfer between heterogeneous devices.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models from larger, complex ones. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact "student" model is trained to replicate the performance and behavior of a pre-trained "teacher" model. The primary objective is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art neural networks, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. This is typically achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs or internal feature representations. The applications of this versatile framework are broad, spanning domains like natural language processing and computer vision, and its utility extends beyond simple compression to performance enhancement and improved model generalization.

papers_seen.author: Rogers
papers_seen.title: Confidence-Aware Multi-Teacher Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is initially introduced to utilize additional supervision from a single teacher model for the student model training. To boost the student performance, some recent variants attempt to exploit diverse knowledge sources from multiple teachers. However, existing studies mainly integrate knowledge from diverse sources by averaging over multiple teacher predictions or combining them using other various label-free strategies, which may mislead student in the presence of low-quality teacher predictions. To tackle this problem, we propose Confidence-Aware Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (CA-MKD), which adaptively assigns sample-wise reliability for each teacher prediction with the help of ground-truth labels, with those teacher predictions close to one-hot labels assigned large weights. Besides, CA-MKD incorporates intermediate layers to stable the knowledge transfer process. Extensive experiments show that our CA-MKD consistently outperforms all compared state-of-the-art methods across various teacher-student architectures.

papers_seen.author: Pacheco
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation with Adversarial Samples Supporting Decision Boundary
papers_seen.abstract: Many recent works on knowledge distillation have provided ways to transfer the knowledge of a trained network for improving the learning process of a new one, but finding a good technique for knowledge distillation is still an open problem. In this paper, we provide a new perspective based on a decision boundary, which is one of the most important component of a classifier. The generalization performance of a classifier is closely related to the adequacy of its decision boundary, so a good classifier bears a good decision boundary. Therefore, transferring information closely related to the decision boundary can be a good attempt for knowledge distillation. To realize this goal, we utilize an adversarial attack to discover samples supporting a decision boundary. Based on this idea, to transfer more accurate information about the decision boundary, the proposed algorithm trains a student classifier based on the adversarial samples supporting the decision boundary. Experiments show that the proposed method indeed improves knowledge distillation and achieves the state-of-the-arts performance.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.
