papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical framework in deep learning, initially designed for model compression. This process involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model, enabling the deployment of powerful artificial intelligence on resource-constrained devices. However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond creating smaller and faster models. It has evolved into a versatile tool for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and addressing complex challenges such as data privacy and federated learning. Its adaptability has led to widespread adoption and the development of advanced methods, establishing it as a foundational technique for creating more efficient, practical, and robust AI systems across various domains.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

This method employs a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, this process enables the creation of compact and fast models that maintain high performance. The versatility of knowledge distillation has led to its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making state-of-the-art AI more practical for real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Donovan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. This process involves transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained "teacher" model to a smaller "student" model. The student network is trained to mimic the outputs or internal representations of the teacher, thereby inheriting its performance capabilities while having a significantly smaller footprint. This approach has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing for compressing models like BERT, as well as in computer vision for tasks such as object detection and medical image segmentation. Advanced methods have been developed to address challenges like under-fitting and to enable distillation without access to the original training data, further extending the technique's applicability and utility.

papers_seen.author: Lambert
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The primary objective is to enable the deployment of powerful, state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their size and computational requirements without a substantial loss in performance. The process typically involves training the student to mimic the rich output distributions of the teacher, which contain more information than simple ground-truth labels. The applications of this paradigm are extensive, spanning natural language processing and computer vision. Advanced methods have evolved to include transferring knowledge from intermediate layers, using multiple teachers, and extending the technique's utility beyond compression to areas such as improving model robustness and fairness.

papers_seen.author: Taylor
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient neural networks. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to transfer the generalized knowledge from the cumbersome teacher to the lightweight student, enabling the deployment of complex models in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. This process allows the student model to achieve high performance, often superior to what it could attain if trained on data alone. The technique has found broad applications in diverse domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its utility now extends beyond compression to areas like performance enhancement and knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique to address the challenges posed by the increasing size and complexity of deep learning models. This method involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, more cumbersome 'teacher' model. The goal is to transfer the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the creation of compact, fast models that retain high performance. This makes state-of-the-art deep learning more accessible for deployment in resource-constrained or latency-sensitive environments, such as mobile devices. The technique has proven successful and versatile across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: The Evolution and Versatility of Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a pivotal technique for creating compact and efficient deep learning models by transferring knowledge from a large teacher model to a smaller student. This process goes beyond simple model compression, enabling deployment on resource-constrained devices and accelerating large-scale training. While the standard approach is effective, its limitations have spurred the development of advanced methods. These include dynamic teacher-student learning frameworks, the transfer of richer internal representations, and specialized adaptations for complex settings like federated learning and non-autoregressive machine translation. By addressing challenges such as optimization difficulties and error propagation, these evolved techniques demonstrate the adaptability and continued importance of knowledge distillation in modern NLP and deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Caldwell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Paradigm for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models, particularly in natural language processing, have created significant challenges for their deployment in real-world applications with limited resources. Model compression techniques have emerged as a critical field of study to address these challenges. Among these techniques, knowledge distillation has proven to be a particularly powerful and flexible approach. It involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process not only reduces model size and improves inference speed but can also enhance performance, improve interpretability, and enable new applications in areas like federated and lifelong learning. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by large models into more compact architectures, knowledge distillation offers a practical path toward making state-of-the-art AI more accessible and efficient.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prevalent model compression technique used to create smaller, more efficient "student" neural networks that learn from larger, more complex "teacher" models. This process transfers the knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student to achieve high performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. The applications of this technique are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and graph-based machine learning. Methods range from mimicking the teacher's output predictions to more advanced techniques like imitating intermediate feature representations. Researchers have also developed specialized distillation strategies for complex tasks, data-scarce scenarios, and for transferring properties like adversarial robustness, making it a versatile tool for deploying state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments.

The applications of this technique are diverse, spanning natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple size reduction, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance model performance, improve generalization, and transfer knowledge in privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique in deep learning, primarily for model compression. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. While initially conceived to create lightweight networks suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used to improve model robustness against adversarial attacks, transfer knowledge between different model architectures, and facilitate complex learning paradigms such as federated and continual learning. This technique has proven effective across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, demonstrating its flexibility and broad utility beyond simple compression.

papers_seen.author: Morrison

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique in deep learning for compressing large, computationally expensive models into smaller, more efficient versions. While originally developed to enable the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices, its applications have expanded significantly. The framework is now widely used to enhance model performance, facilitate knowledge transfer across different tasks, and enable complex applications like privacy-preserving federated learning. This versatility has established knowledge distillation as a crucial tool for developing practical and powerful artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Santana
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework Beyond Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful paradigm in deep learning, primarily recognized for its role in model compression. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller student model is trained to mimic the knowledge of a larger, more complex teacher model. This technique has evolved into a versatile framework for not only creating efficient models but also for enhancing model performance, improving interpretability, promoting algorithmic fairness, and enabling domain adaptation. Its flexibility and wide-ranging benefits establish knowledge distillation as a foundational tool for developing practical and robust artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Martinez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm designed to reduce the size and computational cost of large deep learning models. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to transfer the generalized knowledge from the cumbersome teacher to the lightweight student, creating a compact model suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments without a significant loss in performance. This is often achieved by training the student on the richer, soft probability distributions from the teacher's outputs. The technique has been successfully applied across a wide range of domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and has evolved to include more advanced methods beyond simple output matching.

papers_seen.author: Maldonado
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge by Mimicking Features
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a popular method to train efficient networks ("student") with the help of high-capacity networks ("teacher"). Traditional methods use the teacher's soft logits as extra supervision to train the student network. In this paper, we argue that it is more advantageous to make the student mimic the teacher's features in the penultimate layer. Not only the student can directly learn more effective information from the teacher feature, feature mimicking can also be applied for teachers trained without a softmax layer. Experiments show that it can achieve higher accuracy than traditional KD. To further facilitate feature mimicking, we decompose a feature vector into the magnitude and the direction. We argue that the teacher should give more freedom to the student feature's magnitude, and let the student pay more attention on mimicking the feature direction. To meet this requirement, we propose a loss term based on locality-sensitive hashing (LSH). With the help of this new loss, our method indeed mimics feature directions more accurately, relaxes constraints on feature magnitudes, and achieves state-of-the-art distillation accuracy. We provide theoretical analyses of how LSH facilitates feature direction mimicking, and further extend feature mimicking to multi-label recognition and object detection.

papers_seen.title: Distilled Semantics for Comprehensive Scene Understanding from Videos
papers_seen.abstract: Whole understanding of the surroundings is paramount to autonomous systems. Recent works have shown that deep neural networks can learn geometry (depth) and motion (optical flow) from a monocular video without any explicit supervision from ground truth annotations, particularly hard to source for these two tasks. In this paper, we take an additional step toward holistic scene understanding with monocular cameras by learning depth and motion alongside with semantics, with supervision for the latter provided by a pre-trained network distilling proxy ground truth images. We address the three tasks jointly by a) a novel training protocol based on knowledge distillation and self-supervision and b) a compact network architecture which enables efficient scene understanding on both power hungry GPUs and low-power embedded platforms. We thoroughly assess the performance of our framework and show that it yields state-of-the-art results for monocular depth estimation, optical flow and motion segmentation.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Clark
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of compact, efficient models suitable for real-world deployment. Operating on a teacher-student paradigm, it involves transferring knowledge from a large, complex model to a smaller one. This process reduces the computational and memory footprint of the student model, allowing powerful architectures to run on resource-constrained devices. While initially conceived for compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, not only to create smaller models but also to enhance performance, improve generalization, and enable novel capabilities like cross-modal learning.

papers_seen.author: Kim
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. It addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in real-world applications by training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. While primarily used to create lightweight yet powerful models that are significantly faster at inference, the applications of knowledge distillation extend further. The technique can be used to transfer beneficial inductive biases between different model architectures, improve algorithmic fairness by mitigating biases against protected groups, and facilitate domain adaptation by transferring knowledge from source domains to a new target domain. By enabling the creation of efficient, robust, and versatile models, knowledge distillation serves as a crucial tool in the practical application of deep learning.

papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of modern deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Initially developed for compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded, making it a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling advanced learning paradigms. This process successfully bridges the gap between state-of-the-art performance and practical deployability.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. The primary goal is to create lightweight models that retain high performance while reducing computational and memory requirements, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. The process typically involves training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, often by learning from its rich output probabilities rather than just the ground-truth data. This versatile framework has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and has been extended to address challenges in areas like data privacy, federated learning, and domain adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the deployment of large, complex models in resource-constrained environments. The core idea involves transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained 'teacher' model to a smaller 'student' model, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. Beyond simple compression, this paradigm has been adapted to address a wide range of challenges. Researchers have successfully employed knowledge distillation to enhance model fairness by mitigating algorithmic and gender biases, to improve data privacy by creating models with differential privacy guarantees, and even to develop student models that outperform their teachers. This adaptability across various domains, including natural language processing and graph-based learning, highlights knowledge distillation as a powerful and flexible tool in the development of efficient and responsible AI systems.

papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly in natural language processing and computer vision, have grown increasingly large and computationally expensive. This trend presents significant challenges for deploying these models in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible model compression technique to address this issue. It involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student to achieve performance far exceeding what it could attain by training on the data alone. The applications of this paradigm are diverse, extending beyond simple compression to areas like continual learning, data-free learning, and unifying knowledge from multiple sources.

papers_seen.author: Williams
papers_seen.title: Linkless Link Prediction via Relational Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) have shown exceptional performance in the task of link prediction. Despite their effectiveness, the high latency brought by non-trivial neighborhood data dependency limits GNNs in practical deployments. Conversely, the known efficient MLPs are much less effective than GNNs due to the lack of relational knowledge. In this work, to combine the advantages of GNNs and MLPs, we start with exploring direct knowledge distillation (KD) methods for link prediction, i.e., predicted logit-based matching and node representation-based matching. Upon observing direct KD analogs do not perform well for link prediction, we propose a relational KD framework, Linkless Link Prediction (LLP), to distill knowledge for link prediction with MLPs. Unlike simple KD methods that match independent link logits or node representations, LLP distills relational knowledge that is centered around each (anchor) node to the student MLP. Specifically, we propose rank-based matching and distribution-based matching strategies that complement each other. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LLP boosts the link prediction performance of MLPs with significant margins, and even outperforms the teacher GNNs on 7 out of 8 benchmarks. LLP also achieves a 70.68x speedup in link prediction inference compared to GNNs on the large-scale OGB dataset.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful paradigm in deep learning for compressing large, computationally expensive models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. This process involves a "student" model learning to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By training on the soft probability distributions or intermediate feature representations produced by the teacher, the student model can learn richer information and achieve better generalization than if it were trained solely on hard labels. This technique extends beyond simple model compression, enabling the transfer of inductive biases, performance improvements through self-distillation, and the unification of knowledge from multiple models. Its applications are widespread, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and privacy-preserving federated learning, making it a crucial tool for deploying state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.title: Unified Visual Transformer Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Vision transformers (ViTs) have gained popularity recently. Even without customized image operators such as convolutions, ViTs can yield competitive performance when properly trained on massive data. However, the computational overhead of ViTs remains prohibitive, due to stacking multi-head self-attention modules and else. Compared to the vast literature and prevailing success in compressing convolutional neural networks, the study of Vision Transformer compression has also just emerged, and existing works focused on one or two aspects of compression. This paper proposes a unified ViT compression framework that seamlessly assembles three effective techniques: pruning, layer skipping, and knowledge distillation. We formulate a budget-constrained, end-to-end optimization framework, targeting jointly learning model weights, layer-wise pruning ratios/masks, and skip configurations, under a distillation loss. The optimization problem is then solved using the primal-dual algorithm. Experiments are conducted with several ViT variants, e.g. DeiT and T2T-ViT backbones on the ImageNet dataset, and our approach consistently outperforms recent competitors. For example, DeiT-Tiny can be trimmed down to 50\% of the original FLOPs almost without losing accuracy. Codes are available online:~\url{https://github.com/VITA-Group/UVC}.

papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Barnes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models from larger, more complex ones. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to transfer the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher to the student, enabling the deployment of powerful artificial intelligence architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile or edge devices. This process allows the lightweight student model to retain high performance, often exceeding what it could achieve by training on ground-truth data alone. The versatility of this paradigm extends beyond simple compression to areas like performance enhancement, domain adaptation, and knowledge transfer.

Beyond simple compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used not only to create smaller models but also to enhance performance, improve generalization, and enable novel capabilities across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Different methodologies have been developed, such as self-distillation and multi-teacher distillation, showcasing the versatility of this framework.

papers_seen.author: Foster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Deep neural networks have become increasingly large and complex, which hinders their deployment on devices with limited computational resources. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. This method involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" network to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" network or an ensemble of models. The student learns to reproduce the teacher's outputs or its internal representations, effectively transferring the rich knowledge learned by the larger model. This process enables the creation of compact models that maintain high performance across a variety of domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, without requiring architectural changes or additional data.

This versatility makes knowledge distillation a foundational strategy for developing practical and effective artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Bush
papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Perez
papers_seen.title: BAM! Born-Again Multi-Task Networks for Natural Language Understanding
papers_seen.abstract: It can be challenging to train multi-task neural networks that outperform or even match their single-task counterparts. To help address this, we propose using knowledge distillation where single-task models teach a multi-task model. We enhance this training with teacher annealing, a novel method that gradually transitions the model from distillation to supervised learning, helping the multi-task model surpass its single-task teachers. We evaluate our approach by multi-task fine-tuning BERT on the GLUE benchmark. Our method consistently improves over standard single-task and multi-task training.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Nguyen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Small-footprint Highway Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has significantly advanced state-of-the-art of speech recognition in the past few years. However, compared to conventional Gaussian mixture acoustic models, neural network models are usually much larger, and are therefore not very deployable in embedded devices. Previously, we investigated a compact highway deep neural network (HDNN) for acoustic modelling, which is a type of depth-gated feedforward neural network. We have shown that HDNN-based acoustic models can achieve comparable recognition accuracy with much smaller number of model parameters compared to plain deep neural network (DNN) acoustic models. In this paper, we push the boundary further by leveraging on the knowledge distillation technique that is also known as {\it teacher-student} training, i.e., we train the compact HDNN model with the supervision of a high accuracy cumbersome model. Furthermore, we also investigate sequence training and adaptation in the context of teacher-student training. Our experiments were performed on the AMI meeting speech recognition corpus. With this technique, we significantly improved the recognition accuracy of the HDNN acoustic model with less than 0.8 million parameters, and narrowed the gap between this model and the plain DNN with 30 million parameters.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Self-Knowledge Distillation with Progressive Refinement of Targets
papers_seen.abstract: The generalization capability of deep neural networks has been substantially improved by applying a wide spectrum of regularization methods, e.g., restricting function space, injecting randomness during training, augmenting data, etc. In this work, we propose a simple yet effective regularization method named progressive self-knowledge distillation (PS-KD), which progressively distills a model's own knowledge to soften hard targets (i.e., one-hot vectors) during training. Hence, it can be interpreted within a framework of knowledge distillation as a student becomes a teacher itself. Specifically, targets are adjusted adaptively by combining the ground-truth and past predictions from the model itself. We show that PS-KD provides an effect of hard example mining by rescaling gradients according to difficulty in classifying examples. The proposed method is applicable to any supervised learning tasks with hard targets and can be easily combined with existing regularization methods to further enhance the generalization performance. Furthermore, it is confirmed that PS-KD achieves not only better accuracy, but also provides high quality of confidence estimates in terms of calibration as well as ordinal ranking. Extensive experimental results on three different tasks, image classification, object detection, and machine translation, demonstrate that our method consistently improves the performance of the state-of-the-art baselines. papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, especially in natural language processing, have become increasingly large and computationally expensive, hindering their deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression technique to address this challenge. It employs a teacher-student framework where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. While its primary goal is to create compact models suitable for real-world applications, the utility of knowledge distillation extends further. It serves as a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and transferring complex capabilities, making it an indispensable tool for developing practical and efficient artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has produced increasingly large and complex models that achieve state-of-the-art performance but are often impractical for deployment due to their computational and memory requirements. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, address this challenge by transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the creation of compact models that retain a significant portion of the teacher's performance, making them suitable for resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. The flexibility of knowledge distillation is evident in its successful application across various domains, including natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph-based learning, as well as its adaptability to scenarios where the original training data is unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that employs a teacher-student paradigm. In this framework, a smaller, more efficient "student" model is trained to replicate the knowledge and performance of a larger, more complex "teacher" model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones, without a significant loss in accuracy. Beyond compression, the applications of this versatile technique have expanded to include enhancing the performance of student models, improving generalization, and transferring knowledge across different model architectures or data modalities.

papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks but their significant computational and memory requirements pose major challenges for real-world deployment. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, offer a powerful solution to this problem. Knowledge distillation is a training paradigm where a smaller "student" model learns to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process allows the student to inherit the teacher's learned knowledge, resulting in a compact, efficient model that retains high performance. This approach has proven highly effective and adaptable, enabling the creation of practical models for diverse applications in natural language processing, computer vision, speech recognition, and distributed learning systems, thereby bridging the gap between cutting-edge research and deployment in resource-constrained environments.
